#1888. Hinshelwood: We can be vulnerable – but we’ll learn from Sutton defeat

Three goals in a 12-minute first-half spell put Chris Agutter’s team 3-0 up at Woodside Road on Saturday – and the Rebels were unable to find one their trademark second-half recoveries.

A disappointing afternoon ended with a number of Reds players with bruises and knocks and unable to play in Tuesday night’s National League Cup tie at home to Fulham under-21s.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

But it was a first defeat in 11 league games, and the Rebels’ job now is to show it was a blip in a fine first half of the season.

On Tuesday night Joel Colbran’s first goal of the season and an own goal by Nazim Benchaita five minutes from time earned Worthing a 2-1 home win over Fulham U21s in the National League Cup.

The Reds now have a blank weekend ahead and resume their league programme at Scunthorpe on Saturday week, where Hinshelwood will be looking for a more resilient defensive showing than he saw versus Sutton.

Hinshelwood said: “We didn’t turn up in the first half. We were too soft in conceding three goals in little over 10 minutes and just didn’t deal with things – like the long throw that led to their first goal and the long ball that resulted in their second.

"We’ve watched it all back and analysed it – it’s things we cannot do at this level. We have to learn from it and move on quickly.”

Hinshelwood said the disappointing thing was that Sutton’s disruptive approach – their shape and game-plan – was no surprise. He felt Worthing should have been much more ready to deal with it.

"We’re a young side and we do show vulnerability at times. We mustn’t dwell on it,” he said.

"Some of Sutton’s challenges were borderline. We were left with two or three who were battered and bruised and unable to play Tuesday. Someone said it was like watching football in the 1970s."

Just four days earlier Worthing had recovered from being 2-0 and 3-2 at home to Southend to draw 3-3.

But Hinshelwood said: “On Saturday you were waiting for that moment when we could get it back to 3-1 but it never came. We have to realise that we won’t always be able to fight back into a game as we have done a few times.”

Injury-wise, Dom Hutchinson and Harry Ransom are out for another eight and six weeks respectively with wrist fractures, while Sam Packham needs hamstring op.

#1887. Rare win at Culver Road banishes Robins' Lancing demons and books Peter Bentley Cup quarter final spot

James Westlake described Hassocks as terrible on their Southern Combination Premier Division visit to Lancing 17 days ago when the Robins collapsed from 1-0 up on 87 minutes to lose 3-1.

Their mission returning to the GoCardless Stadium in the Peter Bentley League Cup a little over two weeks later was therefore clear. Come away with victory in whatever manner possible from a place where no Hassocks side had won in their past 11 visits stretching all the way back to September 2004 and a 6-2 success in this same competition.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Goals from corners scored by centre back pairing Dan Turner and Liam Hendy got the job done in a gritty 2-1 victory. Hardly a classic but the Robins will not care given what happened last time and their woeful record at Culver Road over the past 22 years. Their reward is a home quarter final against Lingfield.

Hassocks had the better first half chances only to be frustrated by the woodwork and Lancers goalkeeper Elliot Dailly. Lewis Finney shot too high with the first real opportunity on 25 minutes before Dailly made a smart save with his legs to deny Lewis Croal from close range.

Jack Troak has not taken many free kicks for the Robins in the past but he has surely jumped up the pecking order after rattling the bar with a brilliant curling effort from 25 yards.

The rebound fell kindly for tall striker Jamie Wilkes, whose header towards the bottom corner was clawed out by the sprawling Dailly.

Five minutes before the break saw Dailly make his best save of the night. Raging Joe Bull crossed for Darren Budd to produce a superb first touch and layoff to Troak.

Dailly could only have seen Troak's powerful drive late as it came at him between Scott Packer and Dylan Hurst. Somehow, Dailly managed to react and touch the shot from Troak onto the post.

The first 25 minutes of the second half were a non-event. Lancing tightened up defensively to stifle Hassocks going forward, meaning there was no repeat of the opportunities the Robins had managed to muster during the opening 45. And with the Lancers showing little inclination to attack themselves, it all became rather tedious.

Attention amongst the away contingent gathered behind the goal strayed so far as to wonder why Hassocks chairman Pat Harding was wearing a pair of leather gloves which looked like they should belong to a Spitfire pilot.

Rather aptly, it was a Robin currently sporting a delightful World War II moustache who fired Hassocks ahead on 72 minutes as Hendy breathed new and much-needed life into the tie.

Finney released substitute Joe Turner with a lovely through ball down the right channel. Turner made his way to the by-line to deliver a cross blocked behind by Packer.

The resulting corner was taken by Finney. Packer could only half clear to Hendy, who drilled a clinical shot into the bottom corner.

Celebrations were somewhat muted, probably because Hendy made over 250 appearances for Lancing during 10 years at Culver Road earlier in his career.

Hendy and Lancing have history in the Peter Bentley Cup too; he netted the opening goal in the 2016 final when the Lancers beat Newhaven 2-1 to lift the trophy for the first and so far only time.

Falling behind meant Lancing had to become more positive in an attempt to get back into the game. Gabriel Robinson should have done better after Dan Turner failed to deal with an Archie McGonigle clip over the top. Robinson could only put a weak one-on-one effort a long way wide.

Ed Cooper then almost got caught out by a long Alek Amissah pass forward. Hendy ducked out of a header, allowing the pass to travel all the way back to Cooper.

All looked fine until Cooper charged outside his box and only realised he had gone too far as the ball zipped past him. In the end, Cooper did well to chase back towards his goal and throw himself on top of the ball just before Antoine Sharpe beat him to it.

With the Lancers stirring, this had shades of the league game when Hassocks were monumentally punished for not getting a second goal. Over to Dan Turner to provide one on this occasion with 13 minutes remaining.

Finney looped another fine corner delivery towards the far post. Troak won a towering header back across goal which Turner met with a technically excellent volley. Dailly got a hand to it but there was far too much power in the shot for him to keep it out.

The two-goal cushion lasted only four minutes as Lancing pulled one back with a really well-worked move to set up a nervous finale.

McGonigle kicked things off deep inside the Lancers half. Mo Khedidji and Robinson combined to return the ball to McGonigle, now breaking down the left beyond the Hassocks backline.

His square pass across the edge of the box tempted Cooper from his line. Sharpe got their first, going around Cooper and firing into the unguarded net.

Now thoughts amongst the travelling support really did flash back 17 days. Hassocks though showed themselves in no mood for a repeat and it was in fact the Robins who looked the more likely scorers in the final 10.

Troak bent another free kick on target and also fired a shot a long way over after being teed up by Omar Abdsami. The only moment of alarm at the other end came when Dylan Walter crossed from the right but Cooper averted any danger by making a diving punch clear.

Hassocks: Cooper; Bonwick-Adams, D Turner, Hendy, Bull; Wilkes, Budd; Fender, Finney, Troak; Croal.

Subs: Benson, Turner, Abdsami, Blake (used), Bromage (unused).

Gameweek four in the Europa League sees Crystal Palace welcome Hoffenheim to Selhurst Park for a league-phase clash this Thursday.

The two teams are meeting for the first time in a competitive fixture, with both looking to strengthen their chances of progressing to the knockout rounds, and here, Sports Mole provides details of how to tune into the match.

Crystal Palace vs. Hoffenheim will kick off at 17:45 UK time on Thursday evening.

The match is one of several Europa League fixtures taking place on the same evening, with Bournemouth also in action away to Sparta Prague while Sunderland welcome Dinamo Zagreb.

This Europa League match will take place at Crystal Palace's home ground, Selhurst Park, which has a capacity of 25,194.

The Eagles will be looking to make the most of home advantage, having opened their European campaign with a convincing 4-0 victory over Lech Poznan earlier this season.

Crystal Palace's clash against the German side will be shown on TNT Sports 1 for viewers in the UK, with coverage also available on TNT Sports Ultimate.

Crystal Palace are looking to bounce back from a difficult spell in the Premier League, where three successive defeats have left Pierre Sage's side in the relegation zone after nine matches.

The Eagles have collected four points from their opening three Europa League fixtures, beginning with a 4-0 home victory over Lech Poznan before losing 3-2 away to Lyon and drawing 2-2 with Besiktas.

They currently sit 15th in the 36-team League Phase table and will be keen to strengthen their position with another home win.

Sage's side can take encouragement from their record at Selhurst Park, where they are unbeaten in seven European matches, winning five and drawing two.

However, they will need to improve their recent domestic form if their new manager is to avoid coming under further pressure.

As for Hoffenheim, they have made a less convincing start to their European campaign, collecting three points from their first three matches.

Die Kraichgauer have struggled to maintain that momentum, though, exiting the DFB-Pokal on penalties to Holstein Kiel before suffering a 2-0 Bundesliga defeat against Werder Bremen last weekend.

Hoffenheim are also aiming to improve their away record in Europe, having won just one of their last six continental away matches, while they have lost all five of their previous meetings with English opposition.

By Matt Law | 04 Nov 2026 11:20, Last updated: 04 Nov 2026 11:27

Everton will be bidding to make it three straight wins in all competitions when they welcome Coventry City to the Hill Dickinson Stadium on Friday night.

The Toffees are currently seventh in the Premier League table, only two points behind fifth-placed Liverpool, while Coventry occupy 16th spot in the division.

Everton boast a record of three wins, four draws and two defeats from their nine league matches this season, which represents a strong start to the campaign for the Toffees given the criticism that came their way due to an underwhelming summer transfer window.

David Moyes' side sit seventh in the division and will enter Friday's match off the back of a 1-0 victory over Newcastle United at St James' Park.

Everton also beat the Magpies in the EFL Cup last Thursday, so it has been a strong week for the Merseyside outfit, who will be eyeing a third straight victory on Friday night.

The Toffees will face Brentford in their first match after the November international break before the small matter of a clash with Liverpool at the end of the month.

Everton have incredibly only won one home Premier League match against Coventry - a 2-0 success at Goodison Park back in April 1999, although they do lead the overall head-to-head record between the two teams 37 wins to Coventry's 23.

Coventry have actually won two of their last three games against Everton, including a 2-1 victory when the pair last locked horns at the home of the Toffees in December 2000.

The Sky Blues lost their opening four Premier League matches of the season, but they have now been victorious in three of their last five during an impressive run of form, overcoming Nottingham Forest, Newcastle United and Sunderland.

Frank Lampard's side beat Sunderland 3-1 last time out, and they currently sit 16th in the division on nine points, only three points behind eighth-placed Bournemouth.

Coventry are out of the EFL Cup, so their focus until January at least will be purely on the Premier League, and they will face Crystal Palace and Leeds United in their two matches following the November international break.

The Sky Blues have only lost three of their 18 Premier League meetings against Everton, and their recent form will certainly hand them confidence ahead of this contest.

Everton must make a fresh decision on Jack Grealish, with the on-loan Manchester City attacker missing the team's last two matches due to a disciplinary issue. As it stands, it is unclear whether the Englishman will be in contention for this match.

Moyes could have a full squad available for this game, with no fresh injuries being reported, and it would not be a surprise to see the same XI from the Newcastle clash last time out given the impressive nature of the performance and result.

Thierno Barry has scored eight goals in 12 appearances this season and will continue in the final third of the field, while Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall should again feature as the number 10.

As for Coventry, Aurele Amenda (calf), Haji Wright (thigh), Josh Eccles (ankle) and Luke Woolfenden (knee) are out of the Premier League match.

Meanwhile, Bobby Thomas (calf) and Frank Onyeka (muscle) both need to be assessed.

Jack Rudoni is the team's leading goalscorer this season with four, and the 25-year-old will again feature as the number 10; Taiwo Awoniyi is also set to continue in the side.

#1880. Hearts accounts reveal £2.4m loss and transfer spend amid bad news on Calvin Miller injury

Hearts have announced a loss of £2.4million after investing heavily to return to European football this season.

The Tynecastle club backed Derek McInnes after he took over as boss in the summer of 2025. The Jambos’ thrilling Scottish Premiership title challenge went to the last day of the season when they lost to Celtic at Parkhead to finish second to the Hoops.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Hearts lost to Sturm Graz in the Champions League qualifiers and then to Benfica in the Europa League, but victory over Rapid Vienna saw Wouter Vrancken’s side make it to the league phase of the Conference League, where they face Swiss side Thun on Thursday.

Hearts also reported a turnover of £23.1m for the 2025/26 financial year, are also in “positive” discussions about further investment to help Vrancken in the January transfer window and are confident of a “significantly improved financial result” in a year’s time.

The club’s financial results also revealed that staff costs went up eight per cent “with player acquisition costs of £7.8m across the year, reflecting significant investment in the playing squad”.

A statement on Hearts’ official website said: “The club took a deliberate decision to invest in the playing squad from a position of financial strength, helping secure a return to European league phase football for 2026/27. This additional investment in squad wages, combined with the absence of European income, resulted in an operating loss of £2.4m for the year.

“With European income returning and further progress in player trading, the club anticipates a significantly improved financial result in 2026/27.

“Strong underlying revenue growth offset much of the loss of European income for the 2025/26 financial year, with sponsorship and advertising income up 37 per cent and retail and hospitality income up 17 per cent, reflecting continued commercial progress and support from partners and fans alike.

“The club continued to benefit from exceptional financial backing from its benefactors and Foundation of Hearts members, and extends its sincere thanks for their continued commitment and support.

“The increased investment in the playing squad and football operations was supported by an investment from Tony Bloom towards the end of the previous financial year, which strengthened the club’s financial position and provided capacity to invest in improving the playing squad.

“As an equity investment, this funding is reflected in the balance sheet rather than recognised as income in the profit and loss account.

“The reported operating loss of £2.4m includes £1.8m of gains from player trading and is stated before depreciation, amortisation and finance costs. Further gains will be reflected in the 2026/27 financial year following player trading activity completed in July and August 2026.

“The club is also engaged in positive discussions regarding further investment to support the continued, measured pursuit of the club’s ambitions. The club’s balance sheet remains robust, with the accounts reporting net assets of £20.3m at the June 30 2026 financial year-end.”

Meanwhile, Vrancken revealed Calvin Miller will require surgery on a knee injury that will keep him out for two months.

Both Tomas Magnusson and Miller came off during the first half of the Jambos’ 2-1 Premier Sports Cup semi-final defeat to Edinburgh rivals Hibs at Hampden on Sunday. The Iceland midfielder was taken to hospital with concussion and the former Celtic, Morton and Falkirk attacker left the national stadium on crutches and his knee in a brace.

Vrancken, who will be without 10 first-team players for the game against FC Thun, was asked about Miller and said: “It will be two months, let’s say, depending on what the surgery says because it’s a meniscus injury. It’s a pity, but it is what it is.

“Tomas is doing good. The day after was already a lot better. There is a protocol, of course, with concussions. He will be for sure back after the (international) break.”

#1878. Celtic unwanted 'world record' quip, best starting XI admission and player who might cry if he scores

Celtic host Besiktas on Guy Fawkes Night hoping to rediscover the fireworks of exactly two years ago when a Champions League masterclass inflicted a 3-1 defeat on RB Leipzig.

The decline of the Parkhead club in Europe since that run to the knockout stages that saw them come within seconds of taking Bayern Munich to extra-time for a place in the last 16 has been well documented.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It should also be noted that such success on the continent is the exception as Celtic's two previous November 5 results in Europe will testify, namely a 4-1 home defeat by Sparta Prague in 2020 and a 2-1 home loss to Molde in 2015.

As bonfires are lit across the country, Celtic's focus will be on preventing their Europa League flame from burning out as they go in search of their first points of the campaign after successive defeats by Ferencvaros, Benfica and Celta Vigo.

One of only four teams still on zero points after three matches, Martin O'Neill's side are only being kept off the bottom of the 36-team table due to the fact that minnows Ararat Armenia have a worse goal difference.

There are still 15 points left to play for so all is not lost, but the recovery needs to start now.

“I was told that any team who’s lost their first three games haven’t made it through, so it doesn’t augur brilliantly for us if that’s the case,” O’Neill said during his pre-match press conference on Wednesday.

“So if we go on for a fourth one, then that would be a world record.

“We’re definitely running out of matches, no question about it. But we are capable of still qualifying if, let’s say, 10 points is the mark.

”It means you really have to go away and win, not draw."

There are six survivors from the Celtic team that played in that statement win over Leipzig. Alistair Johnston, Cameron Carter-Vickers, Auston Trusty and Callum McGregor started while Liam Scales and Hyun-Jun Yang appeared off the bench.

Johnston and Yang are both unavailable although the latter has returned to training and could return as soon as Sunday, when the Scottish champions host Kilmarnock in the Premiership.

After their weekend 2-0 defeat at Falkirk, Celtic have won just three of their last 10 matches in all competitions and O'Neill admits he is still unsure of his best starting XI.

"I keep getting asked this question and until I know exactly what everyone can do at the football club, then I probably won't know that," he said. "It's not always knowing about your best team because we've had a lot of games and we're rotating a bit as well to try and save some legs, save a little bit of energy.

"I think it's our ninth game in about 20 odd days. We're in these competitions and we're trying to do our best.

"Once each player has had an opportunity, for instance [Jordan] Latomba hasn't really had a proper opportunity, and once players get a couple of matches then you can make a decision. But your best team might be for a certain game and your best team for European competition might be something else."

Former Celtic striker Oh Hyeon-gyu returns to Parkhead for the first time since his 2024 summer departure. The South Korea international netted 12 goals in 18 months in Glasgow but only started six of his 47 appearances.

After being signed under Ange Postecoglou, he found game time increasingly hard to come by under Brendan Rodgers. But a move to Genk in the summer of 2024 allowed him to move his career forward and he joined Besiktas in January for a fee of around £12million.

Speaking in English at a pre-match media conference, Oh said: “I’m so excited. It’s very special for me to be back here.

“I couldn’t speak English properly back then but everyone welcomed me like family here. And Celtic became like my second home. Maybe I will be emotional if I score but I will give everything for Besiktas.”

Reflecting on his time in Scotland, Oh added: “I came here as a young boy with a dream. It was sometimes hard for me, sometimes good for me.

“I have got good memories here. I always be grateful for everything and the fans. If I score, maybe I will cry. I learned a lot about my position from Kyogo Furuhashi and Adam Idah.

“In my last season here, I didn’t play for the last six months so it was a hard time for me. But I’m very happy to be back here because I love Celtic so much. It has a special place in my heart.

“After I left Celtic, it was good motivation for me. I wanted to show what I could do and how much I have improved. Finally I am back here and I have to show them.”

Jack Hinshelwood - No 10: The academy graduate will likely be a starter in the No 10 as he gets back to his best after injury.

Ibrahim Osman - LW: The flying winger could get another chance to impress on the left flank but once again, Yalcouye is an option here too. Kaoru Mitoma remains injured.

#1875. Huddersfield Town's draw with Luton: Two points dropped or another point in the right direction

The Terriers' intense head coach Martin Drury believes his players look on him at times as "a bit of an idiot and a bit of a lunatic", never happier than when he has something to grumble about. It seems unlikely, but the point is he quite likes being a killjoy and it is working for his squad.

Talking about their mentality before the game he said: "I'm probably having to do less and less from that point of view," then added: "but sometimes it's nice when they give you a reason to,"

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

His players spoilt his fun when they dropped two points against the Hatters on Tuesday but they did give him something to work with.

Now Jack Wilshere's Luton have got their head around being in League One - something which took Huddersfield and takes most big clubs time (take note any Sheffield Wednesday fans still expecting to cruise promotion) - outplaying them is pretty difficult. Huddersfield managed it.

Drury tried to go all Michael Vaughan 2005 with his "look at them celebrating a draw," schtick, not knowing Wilshere had told the room minutes earlier post-match on-pitch huddles were becoming a thing for them.

But it was true Luton ought to have been more grateful for the point, and accurate or not, the narrative can help Town, which is all Drury is interested in.

Yet one piece of awful defending and an inability to turn threatening attacking play into cast-iron chances meant they had to settle for a 1-1 draw. Drury was obviously not jumping through hoops about that.

But seeing his players so down in the dumps about it perked him up, even if nobody thought to tell his facial expression.

"I just said to the players in the dressing room, every game will pose a new challenge and it gives us something else to learn from," said the first-time head coach, whose contradictions include being a compelling interviewee who does not enjoy speaking to the media.

"I'm disappointed we've not won but I liked that we had to come from behind. I liked that we were disappointed with the goal we conceded.

"Overall, I thought it was a good performance but there's key moments for us to learn from and that's what Luton gave us - some things to learn from. That's what we need because we want to keep growing and getting better.

"We need use that now as fuel to motivate us to get better."

Whilst Huddersfield played well between the boxes, it was bad football, not bad luck, which stopped them winning. The goal they conceded to Jordan Clark in the first half was awful, Sean Roughan coming out to win a long ball and not doing so, Town cutting out Jamie Donely's cross but Iban Bowat's header not getting it clear, and no on closing the former Barnsley player down before he hit the net.

At the other end, although Derensili Sanches Fernandes hit a post with a deflected from-kick and Joe Taylor almost pulled the net out of the ground with a volleyed equaliser which took him to 10 goals for the season, and 23 for the year, there was not enough goal threat.

Bali Mumba regularly wriggling down the line, Fernandes forcing Luton to swap Isiah Jones to the opposite side to try to deal with him, Cameron Humphreys twice going close to scoring direct from corners and Taylor even attempting the volley showed a team as confident as one top of the table and now unbeaten in eight games should be.

"I thought we were absolutely dominant in the first half, got to their box numerous times, hit the post," said Drury, taking care not to back up his words with anything as indulgent as a smile.

"We probably just lacked that little bit of decision-making in key moments. I felt we were trying to almost find the perfect angle to shoot and not use their defenders to help us, whether it be through the legs or shape one in. The goal is a very poor goal to concede. We have to do better in that moment because no disrespect, but that is not a well-worked goal. That is a goal that we've not defended well enough or we would normally concede.

"Both as individual players and the group as a whole, I thought there was a real strong mentality to kick on from there.

"I don't look at any of my players and think they didn't have a good game.

"I can't pick out players who didn't perform.

"But I think it probably tells you where we are as a group (that) everyone's got their head down in the changing room and it's flat because we've taken a point and we want three."

You can never be 100 per cent sure but it felt like Mr Miserable probably went to bed on Tuesday pretty happy.

Peck's maiden career hat-trick, scored in 18 first-half minutes at Championship basement club Preston North End, was exquisitely timed as United secured back-to-back league wins for the first time since April in a 3-2 success.

Speaking after the triumph, Wilder revealed that he'd had words with the 22-year-old after the recent away game at Portsmouth on October 14 – when he was unhappy with aspects of Peck's performance in the Fratton Park defeat.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Regarding the London-born schemer, it's very much a case of tough love as far as Wilder is concerned.

The experienced Blades chief remains a huge fan of Peck, whom he views as a future captain of the club, all being well.

While there was deserved praise at Preston, there was also a caveat.

Wilder, whose side are now up to ninth position – with an eighth-placed finish qualifying for the play-offs in May – said: "He's had a couple of opportunities as well, just after half-time.

"So, as always, it's not letting the players get too ahead of themselves and keeping their feet on the ground.

"Possibly he'll say 'the manager has had a bit of a pop at me because I could have got a couple more'.

"We dug him out at Portsmouth. There were a couple of things there in charging forward in the 92nd minute, when we were down to 10 men, it would have been an unbelievable result. Two-nil down to get back to two each and he's chased the game.

"But I don't want to stifle him as well (Peck). We've got some good players at the club, and he's one of them."

It was a night when travelling Unitedites sang Wilder's name following the final whistle in a season in which he has also faced some criticism among sections of the club's fanbase.

In his third spell in charge, Wilder continued: "I've got to be given the opportunity to build something. I look at other clubs and they (managers there) have been given that, understanding that we've got to win games.

"As everybody keeps telling me, it's a result-based business. We built off the back of coming out of the Premier League and we would have built there (after). We need to show a tiny smidgen of patience now and again.

"I think I've done that with the players and you've seen the benefits of that now. We're a quarter of the way through the season with 14 games (gone). It's still a load of football to be played and I think there's more growth in the ceiling for this group."

Patrick Bamford (shoulder) and Kalvin Phillips (ankle) missed the trip across the Pennines, but Wilder is hopeful that they could be involved at Charlton Athletic on Saturday in United's final game before the November international hiatus.

McTominay struck in the 43rd minute to level the match at 1-1, pouncing on a rebound to fire home a first-time volley from eight yards after former Manchester United teammate Rasmus Hojlund saw an effort saved.

Napoli host Lazio on Sunday in their final Serie A match before the international break, with McTominay and Gilmour due to meet with up the Scotland squad the following day.

#1871. Broadbridge Heath taste Sussex derby success – Horsham YM well-beaten by United

Broadbridge Heath 2-1 Crowborough Athletic

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Broadbridge Heath welcomed Crowborough Athletic to the Air Engineering Stadium for this midweek clash between two former Southern Combination League clubs but it was Bears manager Chris Simmons’ side that picked up the points.

Crowborough came into the game on a run of four games unbeaten and they started on the front foot forcing a corner in the opening minutes which saw the ball come out to the lively Rushaar Samuel-Smikle who hit a right foot shot high and wide of target.

On 18 minutes George Hutcheon won the ball off a Heath defender wide on the right and played it inside to Harry Forster, who played it into the path of Findlay Chapman. He struck a fierce right foot shot from the edge of the penalty area that was saved brilliantly by Alfie Hadfield diving across to his left to push the ball out for a corner.

The half continued that way with the Crows pressing high up the pitch and preventing Simmons’ side from playing their free-flowing football and it was no real surprise when the visitors took the lead on 24 minutes.

Marcus Goldsmith won the ball wide on the right and just inside the Broadbridge Heath half, the Crows skipper played a long diagonal right foot cross into the penalty area to Harry Forster who leaped like a salmon to place a looping header over Hadfield and into the net.

On 30 minutes another Crows interception, this time by Hutceon, saw him win the ball wide on the right on the halfway line and playing it forward to Samuel-Smikle who advanced towards goal before he cut inside on to his left foot and hit a shot just wide of the far post.

With 5 minutes of the half remaining Forster received the ball in the middle of the park and played it forward to Goldsmith who then picked a pass to Samuel-Smikle who hammered a right foot shot just wide of the post and it remained 0-1 at the break.

Whatever was said in the Broadbridge Heath changing room at half-time certainly had an impact on the game with the Bears more lively, sharper and passing far more accurate than before.

They equalised on 64 minutes when Ben Royall received the ball in the left back position and drove forward before playing the ball to the feet of Sam Hards who played a pass between two defenders to allow Zac Jeanes to get away down the left flank.

The Heath forward took the ball to the goal-line before playing a pass across the face of goal to Charlie Connell in acres of space for a simple tap-in.

The game was changed completely within a minute of the restart when Sal Marino played a diagonal pass from the halfway line down the left channel to Jeanes who played it inside towards Sam Church. A defender intercepted the pass but only managed to play it straight to Sam Hards some 14 yards from goal who dispatched a low left foot shot that flew under the diving Charlie Holmwood to give the Bears the lead.

It was the fifth straight game that young Hards had got on the scoresheet.

The Bears continued to create chances with Lewis Hyde heading a Jeanes free kick just wide of the post, Zac Young trying a long range shot that was gathered comfortably by Holmwood and a goalmouth scramble saw the ball ping around the 6 yard box. But the game ended with a win for the Bears in what can best be described as the proverbial ‘game of two halves’.

Simmons said afterwards: “It was a really disappointing 1st half performance, they out worked and out fought us and our quality on the ball was poor, 2nd half was better, our equaliser was more like us and then Sam continued his great form with the winner.”

BBH: Hadfield, Richardson, Royall, Holden, Hyde (Salaam 77), Peters, Young (Rawlins 90), Church (Marino 70), Hards, Connell, Mann (Jeanes 60).

After being sidelined for two weeks, injury hit and struggling Horsham YM were unfortunate to host Eastbourne United in rampant mode, bouncing back from their heavy defeat against Hassocks in the FA Vase on Saturday.

YM kept the visitors at bay for most of the first half, only to be overwhelmed in the second. In the slippery conditions an early sliding chance for Eastbourne went wide and although there were corners at each end, YM were getting limited possession and when it seemed inevitable that Eastbourne would score, Ryan Blunt duly obliged for them.

Amid two corners Eastbourne hit the post, but despite living dangerously, YM had done well to keep the deficit down to a single goal at the break.

#1867. Worthing FC puts focus on mental health as supporters association partners with suicide prevention charity Olly’s Future

The charity, founded by Worthing mum Ann Feloy, has been announced as Worthing FC Supporters Association's chosen charity of the year and a fundraising day was held on Saturday, October 31.

Nearly 4,000 fans attended the game against Sutton United at Woodside Road and representatives of Olly’s Future were there with collection buckets. The charity also received a split of the match-day raffle, bringing the total raised to £870.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Ann set up the charity in memory of her son Oliver Hare, who took his own life on February 14, 2017, just before his 23rd birthday. Its work includes delivering training worldwide to equip people with the skills to spot signs of someone who may be thinking of suicide and have a conversation that could help save their life.

Ann said: “We're delighted Worthing FC has chosen Olly's Future as its charity of the year. My son Oliver loved playing all kinds of sports, from football and rugby to tennis and squash.

“It's a local club being bold enough to get behind the message that suicide prevention is everyone's business, and particularly football where the majority of spectators are men.

“This is what the recent The Royal Foundation of the Prince and Princess of Wales' campaign On Your Side, hosted by Jake Mills Hub of Hope and fronted by Harry Kane, looks like on the ground.

“We all know the facts that three quarters of suicides are by men and that suicide is the biggest killer of men under 50. Supporting our suicide prevention charity goes a long way to reaching that vital target audience and we'll be working with the club to ensure we can help save lives from suicide together.

“However, this comes at a time when the town is in shock about the closure of its Worthing Samaritans branch, which has left volunteers reeling. I've spoken to many in the past week, since they were told of the closure of their premises in an efficiency drive.

“Local volunteers tell me they are being asked to work from home, which they feel is not tenable as it's vital for their own well-being to be with colleagues, or else drive to Brighton to carry out their shifts.

“For every step forward in suicide prevention, there seems to be two steps back. The Samaritans are closing numerous premises around the country - Worthing is not alone.”

The Rebels will be working with Olly’s Future throughout the coming season and the supporters association, run by Natalie Lunn, will be donating some of the proceeds from away match coach travel to the charity.

Natalie said: “I work as a nurse and know how difficult it is to access care for physical health let alone mental health. So when we were looking for a charity to support, I went online and found Olly’s Future, which is based locally.

“I have sons myself and some of their formative years were during Covid and I know how difficult it can be for young people. So,it is great to be able to contribute to a charity doing such valuable work.”

The club produced an enamel badge, linking the Love and Light logo of Olly’s Future with the team, for the fundraising day and this proved popular with supporters.

James Davies, Olly’s Future chief executive, has followed non-league football most of his life and he was part of the fundraising team on the day.

He said: “For us it is excellent to have such a relationship with a club which shows how much it cares about the issue of suicide.

“You see more than 3,000 people gathered together in one space and this offers a chance to open up about issues which are concerning them. They are with friends and are experiencing a sense of belonging as they get together to support the team.

“Non-league teams may not have the resources and the large fan-base of the bigger clubs, but they are very obviously rooted in towns such as Worthing and play a major part in the community. Tickets are also affordable in ways that premiership attendance is not for many people.”

His own recent personal experience has shown how much going to watch a match can mean to people who might otherwise be feeling isolated.

James explained: “I recently lost my grandmother and my grandfather, aged 87, had been her carer in her last years. He has started going each week to watch both Portland United and Weymouth matches along with other family members, which stops him just being at home and alone with his thoughts, and when I went with him, he really did open up about his feelings.”

Ben Greenhalgh’s powerful strike and Dan Smith’s opportune rebound punished two moments of Lewes disorganisation before the half hour. While the Rooks responded well, they struggled to break down a stubborn Darts backline and had to wait until the 82nd minute for a scorching Brian Garzon goal.

Despite pouring everyone forward late on, this left too little time to secure an all-important equaliser.

Lewes began the evening with three changes to their starting XI, with Ben Mundele, Tyler Christian-Law and Danny Bassett returning in place of Tyler Cox, Kurtis Cumberbatch and Bobby Unwin.

After a spectacular entrance featuring Southover Bonfire Society’s torches and fireworks, the game itself proved more of a slow burner.

Both teams used the opening stages to feel one another out, and the first chance came after almost 15 minutes, when an unmarked Charlie Walker headed Danny Bassett’s delivery over the bar. Lewes then lost defender Harry Mills to an awkward injury, forcing them into a reshuffle as Olly Hamstead came on.

Just a minute later, Dartford seized upon this as player-manager Greenhalgh found space on the edge of the box for a sharp left-footed strike into the top left corner. Dartford proved a tough nut to crack, with their fluid system quick to close down any gaps and continuing to threaten on the counter. Charlie Walker won a free-kick 20 yards from goal in the 55th minute but sent the set piece over the crossbar.

This spell proved Lewes needed a change of system, and with Tyler Cox replacing Mundele, the Rooks soon moved to a back three. It did the trick of freeing up Cox and Jack Enkh, who posed regular problems for the visiting defence.

With Bassett and Walker also taken off, the Rooks opted for a system featuring multiple runners but no clear central target. Chances started to flow at both ends, with Enkh crashing a shot into the side-netting, Garzon having an effort saved by Ryan Sandford and Hamstead clearing the danger at the other end as Max Fiddes went clean through.

Gondoh was then foiled by Sandford as his shot took a deflection off George Whitefield.

In the 82nd minute, Lewes found their breakthrough as Gondoh drove down the right and found Garzon on the edge of the box, where he fizzed a low shot past Sandford. The Rooks pushed hard in the remaining minutes, but Dartford dropped deep and closed off any angles towards goal.

The best remaining chance fell to Tyrese Owen in an added-time pinball in the box, as his audacious backheel was hooked away. Lewes therefore tasted defeat at home for just the second time this season, while a five-match unbeaten run in October came to an end.

The ruthless Hornets served up a Halloween treat for their supporters as they stormed to a 5-0 win at Farnborough on Saturday.

The visitors led 2-0 at half-time through James Hammond’s free kick and Greg Luer’s tidy finish. George Cox’s rocket, Reece Myles-Meekums’ close-range effort and Harvey Sparks’ ferocious strike sealed Horsham’s biggest step two win in the second half.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The thumping victory moved the Hornets up to tenth – and within three points of the play-off places – going into this Saturday’s home clash with AFC Totton.

Di Paola told us: “We’ve had a Jekyll & Hyde week really, but Saturday was brilliant. We played really, really well. There were some excellent goals and it was a brilliant performance.

“Even when they put us under the cosh at times, we defended really well and looked like a good unit. Collectively there were some really good performances.

“It was a much-needed win against one of the teams near us. It’s amazing because if you get the second or third goal, with the way we play, then the game becomes quite easy. What’s been the challenge in this league, and will continue to be the challenge, is getting those second or third goals to take the game away from the opposition.

“We had such good support on Saturday. It’s such a nice thing when you have a good performance and that level of support. I could see how happy they were.”

Horsham went ahead at Farnborough in the 43rd minute courtesy of a delicious Hammond free-kick. Luer then added the Hornets’ second on the stroke of half-time after good work from Charlie Hester-Cook to win the ball deep in Farnborough territory.

Cox made it three with a ferocious 25-yard piledriver on 74 minutes before Myles-Meekums poked home from close-range for Horsham’s fourth four minutes later.

Substitute Sparks then added the icing on the cake in second half stoppage time to confirm the Hornets’ biggest ever National League South win.

And Di Paola revealed Sparks’ goal was his pick of the bunch.

He added: “Harvey’s was my favourite just because of the way we pulled them all over the pitch and then attacked the space. That’s the kind of thing you look at and work on in training.

“It doesn’t always happen like that. It was nice to pull them all the way back into our half, go all the way back through the pitch, come outside where we’ve created space and go and score. It was a good way to win the game.

“The bundled goal was a bit different, but it was a good day at the office really.”

But Horsham were far less fluent away to SCFL Premier outfit Pagham in the Sussex Senior Cup on Tuesday evening.

A heavily-rotated Hornets team left it late to edge past the Lions 1-0, Ashley Nadesan tapping home with just three minutes remaining after Pagham’s goalkeeper dropped a high-hanging cross at his feet.

Di Paola said: “The highlight for me was that the game finished. It was an awful game of football played on an awful pitch.

“The pitch levelled the game, which meant we couldn’t play any real football. That’s not an insult to Pagham. When I was at East Preston, me and another guy used to jump on the mower and try and make the pitch as nice as possible back in the day. At Climping, when it got to October and the pitch was like a cow field. I’m not being a snob, I just think it’s very difficult to do anything on a bad pitch.

“There were a fair few performances that I was really unhappy with – and I said that to the boys at half-time. I thought some of them were bad – not because we haven’t gone and rattled 20 past them, but because of the general application and lack of desire.

“We mixed and matched it. You have to demonstrate why you’re not playing. It doesn’t mean you have to play well, you need to have the right attitude.

“People don’t need to impress me with goals or unbelievable play, I want players to give everything. I felt in the first half, in particular, we were slow in everything we did. We didn’t press, we didn’t sprint, we played within ourselves.

“A few didn’t do themselves any favours in the first half. In the second, we were slightly better. I thought Niall McManus was good, I thought Jack Brivio had a good second half, but not many of them came out with a great deal of credit.

“I’m glad we got through and got a goal late on. It was a tough night, frustrating night, an awful game of football. Anyone who came to watch that just didn’t see any real quality in the whole game.”

The victory at Pagham was Di Paola’s 300th as Horsham manager – but the boss was ambivalent about the milestone.

He added: “When I get to 1,000 games I will be quite proud of that one. I think that could be next season if we carry on, which I think is quite an achievement – but those kinds of milestones don’t really mean anything to be honest. I didn’t know anything about it.

“But that’s 300 good days in 12 years. We’ve almost got a year of good days!

“I personally don’t really look at stuff like that. It doesn’t make a lot of difference to me. When we get to the 1,000th game I will crack open a cider and wonder what I’ve done with my life!”

The Hornets have no fresh injury concerns ahead of Saturday’s home encounter with 18th-placed AFC Totton.

By Lewis Blain | 04 Nov 2026 12:11

Manchester United have made progress in their shock pursuit of Manchester City defender Rayan Ait-Nouri, with the Algeria international reportedly open to leaving the Etihad Stadium.

The 25-year-old left-back is understood to be interested in a move to Old Trafford, while personal terms are not expected to present a problem.

However, the rivalry between the two Manchester clubs could prove a significant obstacle as United explore their January transfer options.

According to Sky Germany's Florian Plettenberg, Ait-Nouri is keen on leaving Manchester City during the January transfer window, with United still interested in his signature, having tried to sign him on deadline day.

The former Wolverhampton Wanderers star has struggled to establish himself at City since arriving in 2025, making a departure increasingly plausible.

United's interest represents a potential opportunity to address their left-back situation, although negotiating directly with their local rivals would be a particularly complicated transfer.

There is little doubt that Ait-Nouri would offer United an attractive solution at left-back, but signing a City player would be a controversial move given the rivalry between the clubs.

United may therefore be better served exploring alternatives, particularly Barcelona's Alejandro Balde and RB Leipzig's David Raum.

Ait-Nouri remains an interesting option, especially with personal terms reportedly straightforward, but United should not allow the Manchester rivalry to dictate their recruitment.

#1857. Official: Baresi honoured by City of Milano with inscription in the Famedio

Franco Baresi’s passing has left a hole in the hearts of AC Milan fans, but also of those in the city of Milano.

Some footballers transcend the game, especially those who become something else. For Baresi, football allowed him to offer more to the city that raised him through his extensive charity work. However, it wasn’t just the citizens of Milano who benefited from this.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Through the Fondazione Milan, the former defender helped people across the globe and that is why he’s considered so highly.

He was an excellent defender, perhaps an even better servant to the Rossoneri, but he was above all, he was a fantastic man. It speaks volumes that tributes still arrive for him and that the city stood still on the day of his service.

Baresi has already been remembered with murals, but the City of Milan have now offered their own memorial to one of its greatest sons, as the club detailed in a statement this afternoon.

“The City of Milano today honoured Franco Baresi, AC Milan’s legendary Captain, by inscribing his name in the Famedio at the Monumental Cemetery, a memorial dedicated to the figures who have shaped the city’s history and identity.

“The ceremony, led by Mayor Giuseppe Sala and City Council President Elena Buscemi, took place in the presence of Franco Baresi’s family and AC Milan Legend and Brand Ambassador Daniele Massaro, representing the Club.

“Baresi was honoured alongside 13 other distinguished figures, recognising both his extraordinary achievements on the pitch and the values he represented to generations of supporters and the wider Milan community.

“Born in Travagliato, near Brescia, Franco Baresi devoted his life to AC Milan and the city of Milano from a young age. He played a defining role in one of the greatest eras in football history. The Club retired his number 6 shirt in his honour and celebrated his 50 years with AC Milan in 2024. He had served as Honorary Vice President since 2020.

“Others honoured this year include Ornella Vanoni, a devoted Rossoneri supporter, Bruno Pizzul, Giovanni Gastel and Don Antonio Mazzi, alongside prominent figures from Milano’s cultural and civic life.

“Since December 2024, as part of the Club’s 125th anniversary celebrations, the Famedio’s Crypt has also been the final resting place of AC Milan founder Herbert Kilpin, alongside other figures who have shaped the city’s history, including Giuseppe Meazza, Giorgio Gaber, Enzo Jannacci and Alda Merini.

“The tribute to Franco Baresi goes far beyond football. It reflects the deep bond between AC Milan and Milano, a city whose history, social fabric and cultural identity the Club has helped shape for more than 125 years.”

The desire to keep improving was high in Gotts’ mind when he talked about his new deal.

#1848. GdS: From Bournemouth to Batman – ‘magic’ Maignan returns in the derby

Against Inter, Diego Moreira took the headlines, but Mike Maignan filled the pages of reports thanks to his save for AC Milan.

Derbies are normally decided by goals, which is why Moreira was this fixture’s poster boy. However, it may have been an Inter man on the front page if it weren’t for Maignan; it must be said.

As Gazzetta dello Sport writes, ‘when Maignan is magic, Milan don’t lose’ and it’s tough to disagree. Indeed, after the Bournemouth game, he has again proven his worth with some big saves in the derby.

Without him, Djed Spence probably scores and who knows how the game would play out from there. Thankfully, that only has to be imagined, not recalled.

#1847. Will Rodri face England? Barcelona and Spain star's return timeline revealed after huge injury blow

By Lewis Blain | 04 Nov 2026 12:38

Barcelona and Spain have suffered a significant injury setback after Rodri was ruled out for around a month with a hamstring problem.

The midfielder is set to miss Blaugrana's upcoming meeting with Atletico Madrid, as well as Spain's two Nations League fixtures against Czechia and England.

His absence could provide England with a major boost ahead of their trip to Spain, with Rodri remaining an influential figure for club and country.

According to journalist Fabrizio Romano, Rodri has suffered a hamstring injury that is expected to keep him out of action for approximately one month.

The 30-year-old sustained the problem during Barcelona's 3-0 victory over Aston Villa in the Champions League on Tuesday night, requesting a substitution late in the first half after experiencing discomfort in his right hamstring.

Hansi Flick withdrew the midfielder at half-time to prevent further damage, introducing academy graduate Marc Bernal alongside Pedri.

Bernal delivered a composed performance as Barca maintained their defensive shape and secured their first Champions League clean sheet in 18 matches.

However, Rodri's injury means he will miss this weekend's meeting with Atletico, while his recovery timeline also rules him out of Spain's upcoming UEFA Nations League commitments.

Luis de la Fuente's side are scheduled to travel to Czechia before hosting England, with the midfielder's absence depriving Spain of one of their most important players.

?⚠️ Rodri suffers hamstring injury and will be out of action for Barcelona and Spain for the next month. Out for Barça next game against Atlético this weekend. ❌ https://t.co/owY6co3e0A

Losing Rodri for a month is a significant setback for both Barcelona and Spain, given his ability to dictate the tempo, protect the defence and provide composure in possession.

His importance to Barcelona this season is reflected in his statistics, having featured in 14 matches across all competitions, accumulating 946 minutes and an average match rating of 7.28.

That makes him the club's fifth most-used player this season, underlining how regularly he has featured in Flick's plans.

For Spain, his absence against England is arguably even more concerning.

Rodri has consistently been one of the most influential midfielders in international football, and replacing his positional intelligence and ability to control matches is no straightforward task.

The Three Lions could therefore receive a considerable boost, potentially giving Thomas Tuchel's side greater opportunities to disrupt Spain's usual possession-based approach.

Spain still possess considerable midfield quality, but Rodri's absence could change the complexion of the contest, particularly against an England side looking to exploit any weaknesses in the hosts' midfield.

#1846. JJ Gabriel reaches verbal agreement with Real Madrid after Man Utd transfer request

JJ Gabriel has reached a verbal agreement with Real Madrid after indicating his desire to leave Manchester United, according to reports.

Gabriel, who turned 16 on October 6, informed United of his desire to leave in September and has not trained with the club since then.

The forward joined Manchester United’s academy four years ago and quickly established himself as one of the most highly-rated youngsters at the club, featuring for the U18 side at the age of just 14.

Gabriel played under Michael Carrick during the club’s pre-season camp, and was expected to make his competitive first-team debut earlier this season against Brighton in the Carabao Cup.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

However, Gabriel and his entourage instead explored alternative options, with the youngster making it clear that he wanted to pursue first-team football elsewhere.

Several clubs across Europe, including Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain, all expressed interest in signing the teenager.

But reports from Sky Germany indicate that Real are now closing in on a deal, having reached a verbal agreement in principle with Gabriel.

Gabriel, who has an Irish passport, could finalise a move to the Spanish giants as early as January next year.

United would be due compensation should the move be completed, although the figure will be lower if he signs for a club outside the Premier League.

Speaking earlier in the campaign when reports of Gabriel’s desire to leave United first emerged, Carrick said: ‘I just think we’ve got to be really careful of the whole situation.

‘He’s a young boy, he’s 15 and the biggest [thing] for me definitely and as a club point of view is looking after our younger players. Their welfare, their wellbeing, their exposure.

‘And I think all of us we’ve got to be really conscious of that, really, in this situation.

‘As a club, for sure, we’re all involved in those conversations. I just think we’ve got to be very careful of that.’

#1844. Mason Mount offering Michael Carrick a midfield solution which could have legs

It is not uncommon to hear football club executives talking about the importance of the “money being on the pitch”.

In other words, managers having their best players fit and available most if not all of the time. Quality at the top level is essential but so is robustness. They go hand in hand.

Unfortunately for Manchester United, the money has not been on the pitch down the years nearly as much as the club would want or expect.

Bruno Fernandes stands out for what he does with the ball primarily, but also because he plays almost every minute of every game and, while his sheer indefatigability is extreme, United know they need more of his ilk.

This is why the forthcoming season is such a big one for Mason Mount. His quality has seldom been in doubt. The problem is he has rarely been on the pitch long or consistently enough to show it.

Indeed, the one-time England midfielder has started just 25 Premier League matches since his £60m move from Chelsea three years ago and that perennial unavailability is one of the reasons doubts were being cast about his Old Trafford future going into this summer.

Yet Michael Carrick was keen to keep Mount, United have rebuffed inquiries around him and intriguingly the 27-year-old could yet have an impact on what the club do during the remaining six weeks of the transfer window.

For the second time in the space of six days, Mount was deployed in a deeper midfield role alongside new £48m, signing Andrey Santos for Friday’s resounding 5-0 victory over Norwegian side Rosenborg in Trondheim, just as he had done against Wrexham last weekend.

Mount has spent the majority of his career playing further forward, either off the right or as a No. 10 but Carrick likes him in a fluid No. 8 role, a position Erik ten Hag had identified for the player only for persistent injuries to detonate those plans.

The logic is simple: Mount is mobile, can cover the ground, is adept under pressure, has line breaking passing, vision and a nose for goal. He is also a good presence in the dressing room and a leader in his own way. Watch him imparting advice to Shea Lacey as they walked back to the centre circle after the youngster’s goal opened the scoring against Rosenborg and you get a glimpse of that.

The question, of course, is whether he can stay fit long enough to impose those qualities that help to explain why Liverpool and Arsenal had also been so keen to sign him back in 2023 and Carrick’s predecessor Ruben Amorim was also such a fan.

With United’s summer budget only stretching so far, Carrick was always going to have to think on his feet in certain areas of the pitch.

What will be interesting to see over the coming weeks is whether the manager feels Mount is robust enough to complement Santos, fellow summer signing Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo.

MASON MOUNT SCORES FOR MAN UNITED!He takes the ball with a quality turn, and curls it into the corner of the goal 🤩📺 @tntsports & @discoveryplusUK pic.twitter.com/M9ErA2HKbo

Much of the chatter among United fans at present centres on who the third midfield signing will be after Santos and Tielemans.

Given Mount’s injury record, it would be a significant risk not to recruit again in that department in the hope he could stay fit over a full season. Four options in two positions behind the No 10 of Fernandes sounds fine in principle but what happens if Mount’s season was to follow a similar trajectory to the previous three?

If United are going to strengthen in other areas, there will need to be compromises or alternative solutions that help to free up cash along the way but gambling in midfield may not be the best way to go.

With Champions League football to factor in this season, it is still hard to believe United will not seek to strengthen again in midfield but the club seem ready to take their time on that front. And all the while an assortment of names continue to fly around.

After spending £85m on Santos and Tielemans, a massive outlay on a third midfielder at this stage would be a bit of a surprise.

Could that negate a move for Real Madrid’s Aurelien Tchouameni? Alex Scott is greatly admired by United but Bournemouth are determined to keep him and have put a prohibitive pricetag on him.

AS Roma’s Manu Kone is not thought to have universal backing internally. Tyler Adams’ name has been floated again but the Bournemouth and US midfielder’s injury record counts against him.

There has not yet been evidence of a serious appetite to go for Brighton’s Carlos Baleba, whom they considered signing last summer. Sander Berge at Fulham and Borussia Dortmund’s Felix Nmecha are among a number of other midfielders who have been linked with United.

Another midfield signing could well emerge but United are keeping their cards close to their chest. Whatever materialises, though, it will still not change the fact this is a huge season for Mount.

⚽️ Shea Lacey⚽️ Jacob Devaney⚽️ Harry Amass⚽️ Ethan Williams Four #MUAcademy prospects were on the scoresheet in Trondheim 🧬💙 pic.twitter.com/fguQ36ANTM

“It was a good day. Clean sheet, scoring goals and everyone coming through injury-free hopefully is everything you want. Keeping the players fit and improving through pre-season is amongst the most important things. You want to build through the pre-season and you have to manage to players differently. It is never going to be perfect but we scored some great goals and we are moving forward nicely.

“I thought we defended well as a team for the most part. A clean sheet is a beautiful thing. I think we are in a good place with four weeks to go until the start, gradually getting some boys back from the World Cup. As it stands right now, we are in a pretty good place.”

This is what the official start of the season will look like for Michael Carrick’s side:

August 22- Hull vs Manchester UnitedAugust 30- Manchester United vs IpswichSeptember 6- Everton vs Manchester UnitedSeptember 13- Manchester United vs Manchester CitySeptember 20- Fulham vs Manchester United

They face two of the three promoted sides on the first two weekends and there is a very early Manchester derby.

August 1- Manchester United vs Atlético Madrid August 8- PSG vs Manchester United August 12- Manchester United vs Leeds August 15- AC Milan vs Manchester United

Having played Wrexham and Rosenborg in their first two games, the level of competition will rise significantly for Manchester United in the coming weeks.

There is the final whistle and Manchester United have cruised to a 5-0 win over Rosenborg in Norway. Goals from Lacey, Zirkzee, Devaney, Amass and Williams have seen Michael Carrick’s men ease to victory. A pretty one-sided game.

The first yellow card of the game is given very late on as Devaney is booked for a high boot.

A late change for Rosenborg as Hald-Hernes replaces Borgersen.

The visitors have dominated this game and they now have their fifth goal. It is created by great work from Kamason on the right side of the box before he squares it to Williams, who has the easiest of tap-ins at the far post.

Other than a few short periods in this game, Rosenborg have looked poor. They may be midway through their league season but you can see why they are down in 10th in the Norwegian top flight with just four wins from their opening 13 league games.

You would expect that Michael Carrick will be very keen to see his side keep a clean sheet.

Manchester United have their fourth of the evening. Kamason is found making an overlapping run on the right side of the box and his cross fired towards the back post is tapped in by Amass. That was a goal assisted by one full-back and scored by the other.

Good work from Soboczynski results in Rosenborg winning a corner out on the left. They take it short before a shot is hit from the edge of the box straight down the throat of Vitek.

Rosenborg hit the post. Manchester United should probably have been given a free-kick in the build-up as Soboczynski appeared to push Devaney over but play goes on. The ball comes to E Ceide at the far post but his effort strikes the outside of the post.

Just a few minutes after making a raft of changes, Manchester United have their third goal of the evening. Rosenborg fail to clear a corner from the right and the ball falls to Devaney on the six-yard box. He takes one touch before firing into the top of the net.

Bearing in mind Rosenborg are in the middle of their league season, this has been an encouraging showing so far from United. Joshua Zirkzee has been lively. He’s still more likely to leave than stay at Old Trafford this summer but performances like this won’t hamper his value. He set up Shea Lacey for his goal with a good pass after again dropping deep into space and he’s taken that goal to give United a 2-0 lead quite brilliantly. Patrick Dorgu has been a threat and Mason Mount has dovetailed well in central midfield with new signing Andrey Santos.

Both sides are going to make a raft of changes on the hour mark, with the rest of the Manchester United starting XI being changed other than Vitek in goal.

Santos brings down Borgersen not far outside the Manchester United penalty area to give Rosenborg a decent opportunity. It is a pretty decent effort from E Ceide that goes just wide of Vitek’s right post.

The visitors have not been great since the break but they have their second and it is a great solo goal from Zirkzee. Lacey, out on the left touchline, squares it for Zirkzee, who takes the ball towards the Rosenborg penalty area. He fakes a shot, which takes numerous Rosenborg defenders out of the equation as they slide past. He then sits down the Rosenborg keeper before slotting into an empty net. A fine goal from Zirkzee.

Soboczynski has his second chance since coming on at the break after good work from E Ceide down the left but the former’s effort goes wide.

That is a really poor decision from the linesman. Duris was played in behind the Manchester United defence and thought he was through for a one-on-one chance but the offside flag goes up. However, replays prove that Duris was clearly being played onside by Amass, who has looked shaky since coming on at the break.

Zirkzee receives a pass from Dorgu on the D and takes one touch before shooting. His effort takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner, which Wahlstedt slightly unconvincingly punches away.

That is a very good chance for Rosenborg to equalise early in this second half. Amass and Heaven makes a mess of things deep in their own half, presenting Rosenborg with a good opportunity inside the Manchester United penalty area. Two Rosenborg substitutes combine as Soboczynski squares it for Borgersen but the latter makes a mess of it and shoots well wide from 10 yards out.

Michael Carrick has decided to make just a few changes at the break with Amass and Kamason coming on. Shaw and Maguire have gone off, which has seen Yoro move inside from right-back to centre-back.

Our first goalscorer of pre-season = Shea Lacey! 💎 pic.twitter.com/AyFOWNh5Fi

With no delays, the first half is brought to an end and Manchester United take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Lacey’s goal. Expect a raft of chnages at the break.

As this half has worn on, Manchester United’s dominance has only increased.

Mbeumo appeared to be racing through one-on-one but Mortensen just about gets back to outmuscle Mbeumo and allow the ball to go back to his keeper. There were a few appeals for a foul by Mortensen but that challenge was just about fine.

Other than those early stages, Manchester United have dominated the rest of this first half and are pressing for a second. For the second time in the half, they strike the frame of the goal. Mbeumo clips in a cross from the right into the Rosenborg penalty area and it picks out the head of Yoro. However, from eight yards out, the Frenchman’s header comes back off the bar.

Moments after they hit the frame of the goal, Michael Carrick’s side take the lead. Zirkzee picks up the ball inside his own half and, from the halfway line, feeds a pass into the on-running Lacey. Dorgu wants Lacey to play the ball across to him at the back post but the latter opts against it. Instead, just inside the Rosenborg penalty area, he cuts onto his preferred left foot and curls one into the far corner. A good finish from Lacey.

Just as I was saying that both sides were lacking a cutting edge in the final third, Manchester United are inches away from taking the lead as they strike the post. Santos feeds a delicate pass into the path of Dorgu on the left side of the box. Dorgu strikes his effort powerfully but it comes off the outside of the far post.

Both sides have lacked a cutting edge when they get into the opposition final third, hence why there has not been a plethora of good chances.

Mbeumo beats his man down Manchester United’s right and cuts it back to Mount on the edge of the Rosenborg penalty area. Mount hits it first time but his shot is blocked and spins behind for a corner. It is Manchester United’s first of the game but it is headed away.

That was nearly the moment for Rosenborg to take the lead. Pereira’s cross from the left-hand side of the box takes a deflection and nearly ends up at the feet of Chiakha at the back post but it is just out of his reach.

Rosenborg looked the sharper in the early exchanges but Manchester United are growing into the game and starting to gain more control.

Manchester United create their first opening of the game. Rosenborg poorly five the ball away deep inside their half and immediately Zirkzee plays it into the path of Mbeumo, whose shot from the right side of the box is saved by Rosenborg keeper Wahlstedt, who initially spilt the shot but gathered at the second attempt.

Mount trips Sahsah just outside the Manchester United penalty area, which will give Rosenborg a good shot to take an early lead. Rosenborg look a little sharper unsurprisingly in these early stages.

The Rosenborg captain Selnaes takes but hits it straight into the wall.

With Rosenborg in the midst of their season and Manchester United just in their second pre-season game, you would expect the hosts to have more rhythm and flow in their game.

Manchester United to appear to be lining up with a back four, with Yoro starting at right-back rather than his more customary centre-back position.

We are under way in Norway. Rosenborg are playing in white, with Manchester United in blue.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel, with Harry Maguire leading Manchester United out, and we are getting closer to kick-off in Norway.

Rosenborg: Wahlstedt, Mortensen, Singsdal Volden, Nemcik, Pereira; Bomholt, Selnaes, Fossum, Sunde, Chiakha, Sahsah.Substitutes: Sandberg, Amdam, M. Ceide, Rosten, Witry, Dahl, Hald-Hernes, Slordal, Hedman, Borgersen, Bakke, E. Ceide, Duris, Soboczynski.

Manchester United: Vitek; Yoro, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw; Santos, Mount; Lacey, Zirkzee, Dorgu; Mbeumo.Substitutes: Heaton, Mee, Amass, Armer, Kamason, Collyer, Devaney, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Gore, Thwaites, Gabriel, Obi, Williams.

It’s a good opportunity for Shea Lacey tonight. He’s expected to be deployed in the hole in behind Joshua Zirkzee. A talented, highly technical footballer with a good left foot, he’ll be wanting to make the most of the chance. Another opportunity for Mason Mount to stake a claim in one of the two deeper midfield positions next to new signing Andrey Santos. Big season ahead for Mount.

OUTS:Casemiro ⇢ Inter Miami, FreeRasmus Hojlund ⇢ Napoli, £38mJadon Sancho, FreeTyrell Malacia, Free

Forward JJ Gabriel, who does not turn 16 until October, is on the bench for Manchester United this evening. The 15-year-old has represented England at U15, U16 and U17 level. He won the inaugural Premier League Under-18 Player of the Season award for the 2025/26 campaign.

Manchester United’s preparations for the new season continue in Norway as they take on Rosenborg in their second pre-season game. These sides did meet in a pre-season friendly two years ago in July 2024, with Rosenborg winning that encounter 1-0.

Manchester United kicked off their pre-season against Wrexham nearly a week ago, which they lost 1-0 in Helsinki. Michael Carrick opted to deploy two different XIs for each half, meaning 22 players got a run-out. Manchester United kick off their Premier League campaign at newly promoted Hull City on August 22.

They have added two midfielders to their ranks over the last few weeks, both from the Premier League. Brazilian Andrey Santos has joined from Chelsea whilst Belgium’s Youri Tielemans has arrived from Aston Villa. Santos made his first Manchester United appearance in the loss to Wrexham whilst Tielemans is yet to feature having made the knockout stages with Belgium at the World Cup. A number of players are still yet to return from World Cup duty, including the likes of Lisandro Martinez, Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo, although Rashford still faces an uncertain future.

Former Leeds goalkeeper Karl Darlow has also arrived but he is currently recovering from a minor procedure. Benjamin Sesko is still trying to shake off a shin injury whilst Matthijs de Ligt is not yet available due to a back injury which plagued for most of last season. Manuel Ugarte faces a lengthy spell on the sidelines having picked up a serious injury whilst playing for Uruguay at the World Cup. After this game, the level of competition for Manchester United for the rest of pre-season ramps up a number of notches, with the likes of Atlético Madrid and back-to-back European champions PSG to come over the next couple of weeks as Carrick’s men prepare for a season in which they return to the Champions League.

Rosenborg are in the midst of their league campaign in Norway and are experiencing a tricky campaign. They are currently 10th in the Norwegian top flight, having won just four of their 13 league games thus far, but their form has picked up of late as they have won three of their last five games. They won their last match 3-0 against Start six days ago.
