#1843. Jesus Owono’s team-mate defends goalkeeper after death of Jesus de Miguel

Andorra star Lautaro Spatz has offered his ‘sincere condolences’ to Jesus de Miguel’s loved ones following the footballer’s tragic death, while also sharing a message of support for his team-mate Jesus Owono.

Tenerife centre-forward De Miguel sustained severe head and chest injuries following a heavy collision with Andorra goalkeeper Owono, who was subsequently shown a red card for the challenge.

Owono had raced out of his his goal in an attempt to clear the ball when the deadly coming together occurred in the closing stages of Monday’s Spanish second-division contest.

It quickly became apparent that De Miguel required urgent medical attention and while the striker’s condition was described as ‘stable but serious’ after he was carried from the field and taken to hospital, his condition quickly deteriorated.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

A heartbreaking statement on Tenerife’s social media pages on Tuesday morning confirmed that De Miguel has succumbed to his injuries, devastating news that has rocked the footballing world to its core.

Players and organisations have united in support of De Miguel’s friends and family in the hours that have followed, with heartfelt tributes shared and moments of silence observed across the globe.

Meanwhile, the Spanish FA postponed all Copa del Rey and Copa de la Reina matches that were scheduled to take place on Tuesday to allow for time to ‘grieve over this sad loss’.

It has also been announced that Tenerife’s Segunda Division clash with Granada – which had been due to kick off on Saturday – will be moved to a later date.

‘Following the tragic news of the death of Jesus de Miguel, a player for CD Tenerife, the LaLiga Hypermotion match between Granada CF and Tenerife, scheduled for Saturday, November 7th at the Nuevo Los Carmenes stadium, has been postponed,’ read a statement on Granada’s official website.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘The new date for the match is pending confirmation. The club reiterates its deepest condolences to the loved ones of Jesus de Miguel, as well as to the entire CD Tenerife family, sending them all strength and encouragement in these difficult times.’

Con el corazón encogido. Impresiona esto. Cientos de aficionados están despidiendo en estos momentos a Jesús de Miguel junto a la puerta 9 del Heliodoro. #jesusdemiguel pic.twitter.com/9aoHdlAh87

Reuters reported on Tuesday that police in Spain had launched an investigation for possible involuntary manslaughter in the wake of De Miguel’s death.

Under Spanish law, any death deemed to be non-natural automatically triggers a judicial inquiry.

However, criminal proceedings against Andorra shot-stopper Owono are ‘very unlikely’, according to Santa Cruz de Tenerife chief prosecutor Jose Luis Sanchez-Jauregui.

🖤 A moment of silence in memory of @CDTOficial forward Jesús de Miguel Alameda and the victims of last week’s train accident in Spain. pic.twitter.com/o1e4bQRX3E

Owono is yet to make a public statement in relation to the incident and Venancio Tomas Ndong Micha, the president of the Equatorial Guinean Football Federation, has said the 25-year-old was ‘experiencing profound distress and anguish’ following the news of De Miguel’s death.

Spanish radio station COPE reported that a section of supporters inside the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium had yelled ‘murderer’ at Owono, appearing to blame the goalkeeper for the tragic circumstances that played out.

But Andorra defender Spatz, who helped carry De Miguel off the pitch on a stretcher, took to Instagram to defend Owono on Tuesday night, insisting his team-mate would ‘never intentionally hurt anyone’.

‘There are moments when football stops making sense. Moments that stay with you forever and make you realise just how fragile life can be. What we have experienced is something none of us will ever forget. A tragedy that has left us completely heartbroken, speechless and with a sadness that is difficult to put into words,’ Spatz wrote.

‘First of all, I would like to express my most sincere condolences and send all my love to the family, friends and loved ones of Jesus, as well as to the entire Chicharrera fanbase and the football community.

‘Since yesterday, the entire FC Andorra squad has been shocked, devastated and deeply affected by what has happened. It is a tragedy that we could never have imagined experiencing on a football pitch.

‘I would also like to say a few words about my team-mate, goalkeeper and friend, who has been deeply affected by what happened. Those of us who know him know what kind of person he is, how much he is suffering at this moment, and that he would never intentionally hurt anyone.

‘In football, accidents happen, but nobody could ever imagine that one of them could lead to such tragic consequences.’

The Andorra centre-back added: ‘Today, football doesn’t matter. All that matters is standing together in grief, showing the utmost respect and sending all our strength to the family and everyone suffering from this terrible loss.

‘Rest in peace, Demi. [broken heart emoji].’

A separate message on Andorra’s official website read: ‘We are deeply moved by the death of Jesus de Miguel. The first thing we want to do is extend our most sincere condolences to his family, CD Tenerife, and all those close to him.

‘We know that no words can ease such pain, but we want them to know that we stand by their side and deeply share their sadness.

‘We also want to extend all our support to CD Tenerife, its players, its technical staff, its workers, and its fans. We are deeply affected by what has happened and share the pain the club is experiencing. From the very first moment, we have been in contact with them and are at their disposal for anything they may need.

‘Likewise, we are in contact with LaLiga, the Government of Andorra, and the relevant organizations to offer all our collaboration and the necessary support during these very difficult times. We have also requested the postponement of the next match against RCD Mallorca, as we believe these are moments of profound grief in which respect and support for all those affected must prevail.

‘What has happened has had a great emotional impact on our players, the technical staff, and everyone who is part of FC Andorra. These are especially tough times for everyone, and we want to ensure that no one has to face them alone. For this reason, the club is providing psychological support to all those who need it.

‘We are a team, on and off the field. Now more than ever, we must stand together, support each other, and take care of one another.

‘All of football and all of sports are in mourning. These are moments of profound sadness in which we must remain united, support those who need it most, and show the utmost respect.

‘Our most sincere condolences to Jesús’s family and to everyone at CD Tenerife. Rest in peace, Jesus.’

#1842. Michael Carrick spotted ordering Man Utd star to leave the pitch after Roma win

Michael Carrick was spotted telling Matheus Cunha to leave the pitch immediately after the final whistle in Manchester United’s comeback victory over AS Roma.

The Brazil international scored twice as United fought back from two goals behind to win 3-2 at Old Trafford on Tuesday night. After Bruno Fernandes’ penalty, Cunha pounced on a defensive error to level the contest before firing home a winner on 86 minutes.

The former Wolves star removed his shirt and leapt into the crowd in celebration, earning himself a booking. A second yellow followed in injury time for an overzealous challenge as United held on.

Cunha slowly trudged around the perimeter of the pitch as he made his way to the tunnel, desperate to see the final minutes of the match play out.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

He briefly disappeared down the tunnel before reemerging to join the post-match celebrations after the final whistle had blown.

But TV cameras picked up Carrick appearing to tell his player to go straight to the dressing room with Cunha seen pleading with his boss on the pitch. The unhappy Brazilian eventually made his way back down the tunnel, flanked by a club official.

IFAB rules, which also govern Champions League matches, state that a player who has been sent off ‘must leave the vicinity of the field of play and the technical area’ and cannot return, even after the full-time whistle has been blown.

Cunha is set to miss United’s next Champions League match away to Sporting CP on 25 November.

Victory handed Carrick a lifeline with United’s focus now shifting to Aston Villa on Sunday.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘At half-time, I was wanting them to be more positive, if anything, and not get too disappointed and frustrated,’ said Carrick.

‘When you keep trying to do something, the easiest thing is feeling sorry for yourself. If something goes wrong, you get disappointed. That’s not going to help anybody. We might as well all go home if that’s the case. We’ve got to keep looking for the next moment, the next solution.

‘I don’t like to keep talking to the lads about what this place can do and the history and what’s gone before too much, but it’s there.

‘This place does magical things, it’s done it before and it’ll do it over and over again at some point in the future. There’s just something in this place that when we do have these types of nights, we do it the hard way.

‘But one moment can flip the whole place in a different direction. I spoke about that with the boys. Let’s have one moment that can trigger it. And we had that.’

#1841. Arsenal transfer news: Mikel Arteta 'ponders big move' for versatile £70m attacker in January window

By Lewis Blain | 04 Nov 2026 13:11

Arsenal are continue to keep a close eye on Atletico Madrid forward Alex Baena as manager Mikel Arteta considers strengthening his attacking options ahead of the January transfer window.

The 25-year-old Spain international has enjoyed an impressive start to the campaign, attracting interest from several of Europe's leading clubs.

However, Atletico's reluctance to sell and a potential £70m asking price could complicate the Gunners' hopes of securing his signature this winter.

The Premier League champions retain a long-standing interest in Baena and Arteta is 'pondering a big move' for him in 2027, as per TEAMtalk.

Arsenal tracked the Spanish attacker during his time at Villarreal and have continued to monitor his progress since his £40m move to Atletico in summer 2025.

Baena has registered five goals and four assists in 14 appearances this season, taking his career total to 92 goal contributions in 253 matches.

His versatility is a major attraction, with the 25-year-old capable of operating on the left, centrally or even as a makeshift number nine.

Arsenal view him as an option to strengthen their attacking depth, particularly after allowing Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard to leave during the summer.

However, Atletico are determined to retain Baena, who is contracted until 2030, and would only consider an exceptional January offer. That has led to the belief that a move would be more realistic next summer, with a fee of at least £70m required to tempt the Spanish club into negotiations.

Bayern Munich are also seriously interested, while top-flight rivals Tottenham Hotspur, Manchester City, Newcastle United and Aston Villa have monitored his situation.

Baena's growing reputation is hardly surprising given his performances for both club and country.

His nine goal contributions in 14 appearances already this season demonstrate his increasing influence, while his involvement in Spain's 2026 World Cup triumph over the summer has further enhanced his profile.

For Arsenal, his ability to operate across multiple attacking positions would be particularly valuable. Arteta needs another high-quality option on the left, especially with Eberechi Eze yet to consistently impress when deployed there and recent injuries to alternatives like Christos Tzolis.

Baena would offer creativity, goals and tactical flexibility, making him an attractive addition to an already talented forward line. However, Atletico have little reason to sell midway through the season, meaning Arsenal may need to wait until the summer and prepare a substantial offer.

At £70m, it would be a major investment, but Baena's versatility and proven quality at the highest level make him an intriguing target for Arteta.

Michael Carrick’s struggling side came from 2-0 down to clinch an unlikely 3-2 win over Serie A side Roma at Old Trafford.

Manchester United, enduring their worst start to a season since the 1980s, went behind after just 11 minutes as Matias Soule took advantage of space left by the absent Dalot to fire past Senne Lammens.

Bruno Fernandes got the Red Devils back in the game with a retaken penalty won by Matheus Cunha, who then scored two late goals to stun the Italians and spark bedlam at Old Trafford.

O’Hara praised Manchester United’s unlikely comeback but said the team were ‘pathetic’ in the first-half and was particularly critical of ‘atrocious’ Portugal international Dalot.

‘We were watching the Manchester United game and the first-half was pathetic, we were in shock at how bad they were,’ O’Hara said on talkSPORT.

#1835. Chelsea: Morgan Rogers names area to improve despite superb start

By Axel Clody | 04 Nov 2026 13:42

Morgan Rogers did not need long to justify Chelsea’s investment. With six goals and four assists in 12 matches, he has become one of Chelsea’s key players this season. He is directly involved in the build-up play and is gradually establishing himself among the players who excite the fans.

This immediate impact does not mean the Englishman considers his work finished, however. On the contrary, the player himself acknowledges that he still has room to improve in one of the most important aspects for someone with his profile: the ability to turn chances into goals.

Rogers’ start becomes even more significant when the context of his arrival is considered. Chelsea spent about £117m to sign him from Aston Villa, placing considerable expectation on his shoulders before he had even pulled on the blue shirt.

In a transfer of that size, there is little room for a quiet adaptation period or a season of getting used to the environment. The pressure for an immediate impact has followed him since day one, and he is coping with it on the pitch.

? Fermin Lopez, Morgan Rogers and Nico Paz: Club stats this season ?? Fermin Lopez: 6 goals, 6 assists ??????? Morgan Rogers: 6 goals, 4 assists ?? Nico Paz: 5 goals, 6 assists All making their mark! ? https://t.co/o1GsWqphG7

Rogers’ attacking contribution helps explain why he has already won over part of the stands. His numbers show a player who not only finds the net but can also create for his team-mates and influence the development of moves.

The combination of goals and assists shows how much influence he has in attack, while his ability to carry the ball and create danger makes him an important part of how the team functions.

There is nevertheless a difference between producing flashes of brilliance and delivering a complete performance over 90 minutes. That is precisely where the Englishman’s game can step up.

Rogers has shown he can change situations, but the next step is to sustain that influence more consistently, shaping matches without relying solely on isolated moments.

The player does not hide where he believes he needs to improve. In a recent interview, Rogers admitted that his efficiency in front of goal and his ability to convert the simplest chances are aspects that still deserve attention in his development.

‘I think being more clinical in front of goal, being more ruthless in and around the box, is something that previously I was a bit disappointed in myself because I’d score a nice goal every once in a while, but I wouldn’t score the easy goals.’

‘I’m trying to work on that here. I’m trying to improve in my final actions, so that’s my biggest one. I’m an attacker, so I try to score goals and assist and create chances. I want to keep improving. I’m not there yet but it’s a good start,’ he concluded.

The assessment of Morgan Rogers also comes down to consistency. The Englishman has already shown that he can be decisive at different moments, but his attacking contribution can still translate into more complete performances.

The difference lies in being able to influence the game continuously, without his impact being concentrated in a few standout moments.

This room for improvement does not diminish the merit of what he is achieving. On the contrary, it shows the potential of a player who, despite carrying the weight of one of the most expensive signings in football history, has started the season with numbers and a leading role.

Rogers was expected to take on responsibility when he arrived at Chelsea, and his first months suggest he is living up to it.

The next stage, however, demands more than maintaining the current output. If he can improve his decision-making in the final moments and make better use of his chances in the box, Rogers could stop being only a player capable of producing great moments and become a dominant presence throughout matches.

#1833. Sweden make Dejan Kulusevski call-up decision after Tottenham injury return

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Dejan Kulusevski has been called up by Sweden ahead of the November international break as the Tottenham playmaker continues his recovery from a long-term kneecap injury.

Kulusevski has not played for Sweden since suffering the injury while playing for Spurs in May 2025.

The 26-year-old has faced a gruelling period on the sidelines, which included two separate surgeries to correct the issue, but has begun to be slowly reintroduced by Spurs over the last month.

Kulusevski has featured off the bench in each of Spurs’ last three games, playing a combined 17 minutes during wins against Coventry, Chelsea and Crystal Palace.

Spurs will continue to be cautious with the former Juventus man, but his inclusion in Graham Potter’s Sweden squad for the upcoming international break represents another step forward.

Kulusevski missed out on selection for the World Cup over the summer, which he described as one of the hardest parts of an “impossible” journey back to fitness.

Potter, though, has been eager to get him back involved, and while he accepted they would need to remain patient, he had initially hoped to call him up during the last international break in September.

Sweden and Spurs are in constant conversation about how best to manage Kulusevski’s recovery, but Potter has admitted that the final decision ultimately lies with the north London club.

"He is progressing step by step. First, he needs to return to playing with Tottenham, and they are the ones who have the final say. They see him every day, and they are the most capable of making the decision,” Potter said ahead of the September international break.

“When he is not playing with his club, it is difficult for us to call him up even if we want to. He is a top-class player, and we respect his situation. He is not far off, but when you have been absent for a long period, it is important to be cautious in the final stage of rehabilitation."

#1832. Rafa Benitez sends clear advice to Unai Emery over Man Utd job

Unai Emery should reject Manchester United and continue with Aston Villa if he receives an offer to take charge at Old Trafford.

That’s the view of former Liverpool manager Rafa Benitez, who has warned Emery that the grass isn’t always greener amid speculation linking his fellow Spaniard with the United job.

There had been optimism amongst United’s fanbase after Michael Carrick was appointed on a full-time basis in the summer having led the Red Devils to an impressive third-place finish.

But just six months on and Carrick’s future has been plunged into doubt after what has been a wretched start to the new campaign, with United languishing down in 17th in the Premier League table – only two points better off than rock-bottom Sunderland.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

A thrilling comeback victory over Roma in the Champions League brought the club’s miserable nine-match winless streak to a halt on Tuesday night, easing some of the pressure on Carrick.

However, United’s overall performance was bordering on diabolical for much of the first half and questions over Carrick’s position will intensify again should his side suffer a further setback at home to Villa this weekend.

Sunday’s contest has been billed as a potential managerial audition for Emery, the man in the opposition dugout, who has worked wonders across his four-year spell at Villa Park.

According to Benitez, though, Emery should think very carefully before leaving a club where he has universal ‘support’ to join a club where he may not be given the same backing.

Asked if his compatriot should jump ship if he received a call from United, Benitez told talkSPORT: ‘I had six years at Liverpool, three at Newcastle, six months at Chelsea and not so much at Everton.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘But I can tell you that if you’re at a club where they support you, they give you almost everything that you need, you can build something and Unai is already doing that.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘So I think it is a time for him to continue doing that and later on see.

‘In a couple of years, if he cannot get what he wants, his aspirations or his targets, maybe he has to consider other things.

‘But to find now an owner, the fans, everybody loves you, and then they give you support, it’s quite difficult to find.’

Benitez thinks Emery does not get the credit he deserves in their native Spain despite the extraordinary success the 55-year-old has achieved with Sevilla, Villarreal and now Villa.

‘The reality is that in Spain we don’t praise our people. We’re used to praising people coming from abroad,’ he added.

‘So if you are building something then it’s, “Okay, fine”, and then you go abroad and win something and people consider you a legend.

‘It happens a lot in Spain, it’s one of our big problems in Spain.’

Speaking to Amazon Prime after United’s Champions League epic with Roma, Carrick took the opportunity to praise the character his players displayed to come back from two goals down and emerge victorious.

However, he was also keen to stress that the win would only mean something if they were able to back it up on a consistent basis, with games coming thick and fast over the winter period.

‘It’s one game so it depends on what happens next. We’ve got to capitalise on that, but the boys showed an awful lot in the second half.

‘This was right at that moment. It depends on what happens next. We’ve got to make the most of it, we’ve got to move forward, but I’m feeling a lot better about things.

‘It’s a win for us as a football club. To see the supporters go home happy is what we live for, to give them performances and nights like this so they can get back energised again.

‘As a team, we’ve shown a lot of character to weather what we’ve had to. You find out a lot about each other.

‘The players will find out things about me, I certainly do about them and their character, what it means to them and what they’re prepared to put in.’

#1831. “Keeping an eye on young players” – Moretto names January target alongside Inacio

AC Milan could sign another young defender for the first team in January, according to a report from Matteo Moretto.

As the winter mercato nears, Milan will be focused on adding a first-team defender to lessen the pressure on the current options. However, they will not only look for experience. Although Endrick is something of a middle ground, he’s still a player for the future, rather than being a finished product.

In other words, the signings may still be players with a ceiling, even if they are ready to make an impact.

This afternoon, Moretto provided an update on the situation involving Timmo Hardung, but that’s not all. In fact, he also gave some information on the January mercato, with the Rossoneri looking to sign a young talent from Belgium, as MilanVibes relays.

“AC Milan are looking to acquire a central defender and strengthen their defence with a new player. Gonçalo Inacio remains among the most popular players for January, especially for coach Amorim.

#1830. Paul Merson makes JJ Gabriel claim as Man Utd youngster agrees to join Real Madrid

Paul Merson says Manchester United will be ‘gutted’ to lose JJ Gabriel to Real Madrid as he ‘could have been a superstar’ at Old Trafford.

The 16-year-old has reached a verbal agreement to join Real Madrid in January after walking out on United earlier in the season.

Gabriel, who was branded the ‘best 15-year-old in Europe’ last year, was expected to become Manchester United’s youngest player in the Carabao Cup in September.

But the club decided to delay his introduction to first-team football and Gabriel’s representatives immediately removed him from United and began looking elsewhere for opportunities.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

PSG and Bayern Munich both expressed interest in signing one of the most highly-rated youngsters in world football but Real Madrid have seemingly won the transfer race.

Bernabeu bosses have not contacted United to discuss the situation but Gabriel, who turned 16 last month, has verbally agreed to join Real Madrid in January.

Merson believes Manchester United will be ‘gutted’ to lose such a top talent but understands Gabriel’s desire to play for Madrid.

‘This kid’s a good player,’ the former Arsenal and England winger told Sky Sports. ‘He’s a very good player.

‘He could have been a superstar so Manchester United will be gutted. I think this rule’s got to change. I think it’s because his mum and dad have got an Irish passport that he’s allowed to go abroad.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘And I think that needs to change. Manchester United have worked on this kid, made him the player he is. Obviously, he’d have been gifted at the same time.

‘Don’t get me wrong, but this needs to be done. The thing is, he’s going to Real Madrid. I said Manchester United are one of the biggest clubs in the world.

‘He’s going to the biggest club in the world. The biggest club. So it’s not like there’s not a player in the world who wouldn’t go to Real Madrid.

‘You ask any player who’s playing in the Premier League, everybody, if Real Madrid come for you, it’s very rare you turn Real Madrid down.

‘So, great opportunity for the kid, but I still think that rule might have to change. Otherwise, this ain’t, this is not the first time it’s going to happen.

‘You got to remember, look at Rio Ngumoha, who’s at Liverpool. He was at Chelsea two years ago he left Chelsea.

‘So it happens. It happens. It will happen all the time. But I think that rule’s got to change, in my opinion.

‘Just give these academies a chance where they’re putting a lot of hard work just for someone to go, I’m leaving now.’

As Merson referenced, Gabriel secured a European Union passport which will make it easier for him to sign for a club outside England.

Gabriel, a forward who can play across the front-three, was named the Premier League Under-18 Player of the Season last year.

Manchester United have endured a dismal start to the season but will hope to gain some momentum following an incredible comeback win against Roma on Tuesday.

#1829. Chelsea: Emi Martinez and defender spotted in training after Xabi Alonso updates

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Xabi Alonso could be in a position to welcome Emi Martinez back for Chelsea's Premier League clash against Sunderland this weekend, while Aaron Anselmino has taken a big step in his recovery from injury.

Martinez has missed Chelsea's last three games across all competitions after undergoing surgery for a broken jaw sustained upon a collision with Jarrad Branthwaite in the win over Everton last month.

The Argentina international was expected to be sidelined for around six weeks, but Standard Sport reported before the win against Manchester United that there was optimism Martinez could be back fit ahead of schedule, and Alonso confirmed as much in the pre-match press conference.

"Yes, there is a chance. We need to still wait for next week, but let's see how things go," Alonso said in response to being asked if Martinez could return against Sunderland. "But there is a chance."

It would appear that Martinez is on course to be in contention to replace Mike Penders in goal at the Stadium of Light on Sunday afternoon as he was put through his paces at Cobham on Wednesday ahead of Chelsea’s final fixture before the November international break.

The 34-year-old was spotted in the session wearing a protective face mask and will need to do so if selected against Sunderland.

"In case he's ready to play, he will need a face mask probably," Alonso added.

There was also the rare sighting of forgotten £17million signing Aaron Anselmino, who has not featured in a Chelsea senior matchday squad since the Carabao Cup second round win over Luton in August.

The 21-year-old defender has been sidelined with an unspecified injury, but is on the road to recovery.

“He’s not available yet,” Alonso revealed last week. “He's had a few things, a few injuries and it still will take a few weeks until he's fully fit and we need to be cautious with him because he has had a few of them so he's still not there.”

#1828. CAF African Player of the Year: 10 nominees revealed with Yan Diomande missing, three names spark debate

By Axel Clody | 04 Nov 2026 13:52

The Confederation of African Football (CAF) on Wednesday revealed its list of 10 nominees for the 2026 African Ballon d’Or. It is a prestigious selection, but several choices raise eyebrows.

Three Moroccans, three Senegalese and no sign of Ibrahim Maza or Yan Diomande: the list of 10 candidates for the 2026 African Player of the Year award will fuel plenty of discussion.

Achraf Hakimi, Brahim Diaz, Ismael Saibari, Sadio Mane, Ismaila Sarr, Pape Gueye, Amad Diallo, Yoane Wissa, Antoine Semenyo and Teboho Mokoena have been selected by the Confederation of African Football.

?????? ?? ??? ???? (???) - ???????? #CAFAwards2026 https://t.co/jgE5qPNl4C

The reigning champion, Achraf Hakimi, was crowned in 2025 ahead of Mohamed Salah and Victor Osimhen. The Morocco captain has strong arguments to win a second consecutive award, given his performances with Paris Saint-Germain and Morocco’s run at the World Cup.

He would become the first player to retain the award since Mohamed Salah in 2018 and the first Moroccan to win it twice. Ismael Saibari, who has had a particularly accomplished year, is the other Moroccan candidate, while Brahim Diaz completes Morocco’s strong representation.

The three Senegalese players could turn into a handicap for their country. Sadio Mane remains the most prestigious name, while Ismaila Sarr, brilliant in the Conference League with Crystal Palace, and Pape Gueye have played a part in Senegal’s excellent year. They risk splitting the votes, whereas Hakimi appears the most obvious Moroccan candidate.

The absences of Ibrahim Maza and Yan Diomande are surprising, particularly given some of the names selected. Both are among the candidates for the African Young Player of the Year award.

Maza has established himself at Bayer Leverkusen and with Algeria, while Diomande, who became the most expensive African player in history in the summer transfer window, has stepped up a level at RB Leipzig, Real Madrid and with the Ivory Coast national team.

Their youth does nothing to diminish the value of their performances: age should be neither an advantage nor a ceiling. They finished ninth and fifth respectively in the 2026 Kopa Trophy.

The inclusion of Amad Diallo, despite his qualities and growing importance at Manchester United, appears questionable at the expense of Diomande.

The selections of Yoane Wissa and especially Teboho Mokoena can also be debated. The South African from Mamelodi Sundowns remains a reference on the continent, but his year appears less striking individually than those of several players left out.

Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha could also have laid claim to a place after accompanying his country’s historic run. The CAF selected only outfield players, leaving Cape Verde without a representative despite an exceptional year. Even before the list is reduced to three finalists and the CAF Awards ceremony on 7 December in Lagos, Nigeria, the first selection has already produced some major losers.

#1827. Goalkeeper Jesus Owono issues first statement after death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel

FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono says he is enduring ‘the most difficult days of my life’ following the death of the Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel.

The 30-year-old died in hospital on Tuesday following a challenge from Owono during FC Andorra’s game against Tenerife in the Spanish second division on Monday.

De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest after Owono had sprinted from his goal towards the halfway line and struck the Tenerife striker in the chest with his knee as he attempted to clear the ball.

After being taken to hospital, Tenerife described De Miguel’s condition as ‘stable’ on Monday night but the club issued a second update in the early hours of Tuesday morning which said that his ‘medical condition has deteriorated neurologically.’

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

De Miguel died later on Tuesday morning, while police in Spain have opened an investigation for possible involuntary manslaughter.

In his first statement since De Miguel’s death, Owono says he will ‘face whatever comes with the utmost respect’.

‘These are the most difficult days of my life. I’m struggling to find the words and finding it very hard to process what has happened,’ Owono said.

‘I feel immense pain at the loss of Jesus. I’m thinking of him, his family, and all the people who loved him.

‘I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I can’t think of anything other than Jesus and the pain we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesus.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The club added at the end of the statement: ‘FC Andorra requests the utmost sensitivity and respect.’

On Tuesday, Owono received support from his national team, Equatorial Guinea, following De Miguel’s death.

Venancio Tomas Ndong Micha, the president of the Equatorial Guinean Football Federation, said: ‘I feel it is necessary to convey our full solidarity and support at this time to our player, Jesus Lazaro Owono.

‘We know that, as an involuntary participant in this fatal incident during the match, he is experiencing this situation with profound distress and anguish.

‘The Equatorial Guinean Football Federation offers him our full personal and professional support, fully aware of the severity of this event—something no one in our sport ever wishes to witness.

‘We share in your mourning and remain entirely at your disposal. Please accept our deepest respect and support during these most difficult times.’

FC Andorra defender Lautaro Spatz, who helped carry De Miguel off the pitch on a stretcher, also defended Owono, insisting his teammate would ‘never intentionally hurt anyone’.

‘There are moments when football stops making sense. Moments that stay with you forever and make you realise just how fragile life can be. What we have experienced is something none of us will ever forget. A tragedy that has left us completely heartbroken, speechless and with a sadness that is difficult to put into words,’ Spatz wrote on Instagram.

‘First of all, I would like to express my most sincere condolences and send all my love to the family, friends and loved ones of Jesus, as well as to the entire Chicharrera fanbase and the football community.

‘Since yesterday, the entire FC Andorra squad has been shocked, devastated and deeply affected by what has happened. It is a tragedy that we could never have imagined experiencing on a football pitch.

‘I would also like to say a few words about my team-mate, goalkeeper and friend, who has been deeply affected by what happened. Those of us who know him know what kind of person he is, how much he is suffering at this moment, and that he would never intentionally hurt anyone.

‘In football, accidents happen, but nobody could ever imagine that one of them could lead to such tragic consequences. Today, football doesn’t matter. All that matters is standing together in grief, showing the utmost respect and sending all our strength to the family and everyone suffering from this terrible loss. Rest in peace, Demi.’

#1826. Fenerbahce 3-2 Liverpool: Reds stunned in Istanbul to lose perfect Champions League record

Even Liverpool’s multi-million pound bench could not rescue a team floundering in Istanbul as a chaotic performance was punished by Fenerbahce as they twice came from behind to win 3-2.

Alexander Isak had scored within three minutes of coming on to put the visitors ahead going into the final quarter but, like in the first half, the lead lasted just four minutes before former West Brom trainee Archie Brown equalised courtesy of some lax defending.

But worse was to follow as Vedat Muriqi outjumped three players to nod in the winner and end Liverpool’s 100 per cent record.

And while Andoni Iraola will be scrutinised for making five changes, including resting three of his front four in Sunday’s defeat to Arsenal, it was the way the team lost their cool and control in a game they had in hand which was more damaging.

It was a harsh result on 19-year-old Trey Nyoni, who belied his relative inexperience with a composed performance capped by an excellent volley to open the scoring, becoming Liverpool’s youngest player to register his maiden goal in the Champions League and second-youngest scorer in the competition after Trent Alexander-Arnold.

But Liverpool’s Turkish troubles continued – they lost twice to Galatasaray last season – on a typically fractious night in Istanbul, with former Manchester United forward Mason Greenwood scoring the first equaliser with a free-kick which deflected in off Jeremy Jacquet.

Arsenal XI vs Slavia Prague: Starting lineup and confirmed team news

They had been in total command up to that point but from there the game descended into something more manic, which suited a team hammered 6-0 at Villa Park last month and stoked a febrile home crowd.

Many of Liverpool’s players did not cope well in that atmosphere but, to his immense credit, Nyoni shone.

Iraola’s choice to leave out Isak, Florian Wirtz and Cody Gakpo as they come to the end of a run of nine games in 27 days was understandable but it left his side toothless.

Bradley Barcola was deployed as striker but his unfamiliarity with the role was evident after failing to properly anticipate Joe Gomez’s low cross to the near post.

He did flick one header wide but struggled with the physicality of Fenerbahce’s centre-backs, even though Kojo Oppong was making his first Champions League start.

There was a lot of naivety within the visitors’ ranks – Victor Munoz snatched at an early chance when he was found in acres of space before redeeming himself by eventually forcing Ederson into a save – but none of it came from Nyoni.

The teenager was composed on just his seventh Champions League appearance – with everything going through him at the base of midfield.

His use of the ball, tactical awareness and unshakeable belief in his own ability meant amid the hurly burly of a typically Turkish clash he was head and shoulders above everyone else.

Many of Liverpool’s players did not cope well in that atmosphere but, to his immense credit, Nyoni shone.

Even the usually unflappable Virgil van Dijk’s patience was tested, pushing Irfan Kahveci to the floor at a second-half corner, having twice had Romelu Lukaku leave something on him in the early stages.

When Liverpool’s breakthrough came it was fully deserved as Rio Ngumoha’s cross to the far post saw Van Dijk’s pressure force Brown to head weakly to the edge of the penalty area where Nyoni dispatched the dropping ball via a deflection off Oppong.

But after a sliding Kahveci smashed against the crossbar from five yards, Greenwood’s free-kick went through the wall.

Isak headed in Gakpo’s cross with his first chance after those two and Wirtz were summoned in the 66th minute, but the unmarked Brown tapped in the equaliser and more poor defending saw Muriqi head home the winner.

#1824. Getafe vs. Brighton: How to watch, date, time, live stream and TV channel for Conference League fixture

By Matthew Cooper | 04 Nov 2026 13:58

Getafe and Brighton meet in the UEFA Conference League on November 5, with the Spanish side welcoming the Seagulls to the Coliseum for matchday three of the league phase.

The hosts currently sit 20th in the table and are searching for their first win, while the visitors are unbeaten in ninth.

Here, Sports Mole details everything you need to know about how to follow Thursday's match.

The match will kick off at 8pm UK time on Thursday, November 5.

The fixture will take place at the Coliseum, which is the home stadium of Getafe.

The ground has a capacity of 16,500 and Getafe have played there since 1998.

The Conference League match will be shown live on TNT Sports 2, with coverage beginning at 7pm UK time.

UK viewers can stream the match live via HBO Max after TNT Sports moved from Discovery+ to HBO Max earlier this year.

Viewers can access the stream through a standalone TNT Sports subscription or by adding TNT Sports to selected HBO Max entertainment packages.

Highlights of the match will be available on UEFA's website, HBO Max and the TNT Sports Football YouTube channel, while TNT Sports will also post clips on their social media channels.

Getafe have failed to pick up a win in Europe so far this season, drawing 1-1 with Romanian side Universitatea Craiova and losing 5-2 to Swiss team Lugano in their opening fixtures.

Jose Bordalas's men need a positive result against Brighton to boost their hopes of reaching the knockouts and they will take heart from the fact they beat Sevilla 3-1 in La Liga on Sunday.

Brighton, meanwhile, are competing in Europe for the first time since 2024 and they have made a strong start.

The Seagulls have four points from their first two league phase games, having thumped Lithuanian club Kauno Zalgiris 4-0 before drawing 0-0 with Czech side Jablonec.

#1823. Arsenal player ratings vs Slavia Prague: 9/10 statement performance in nervy Champions League win

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal survived a late goal to beat Slavia Prague 2-1 and continue their strong start in the Champions League.

Noni Madueke opened the scoring after charging through on goal in behind and Viktor Gyokeres, who assisted that opener, then got on the scoresheet himself with a wonderful curled finish.

At that stage the Gunners were cruising, but they dropped off significantly in the second half and allowed Slavia to grow in confidence and get back into the game.

Wiktor Nowak scored in the 90th minute as Slavia threatened a grandstand finish but Arsenal did enough to hold on and move up to third in the league-phase standings.

Here is how Matt Verri rated the Arsenal players...

Bit too casual at times with the ball, as he tried to keep himself interested on a very routine night. Did his best to preserve Arsenal’s clean sheet with a truly outrageous save with his fingertips late in the match, but got done with a teasing cross in stoppage-time.

Looked close to his best in attack, flying forward to support Madueke. Perfect cut-back should have been finished by Merino. Bullied Sturm when called into action defensively too. Sloppier after the break as Arsenal’s standards dipped.

Even without being at full pelt, Slavia could not live with his running power. Stopped attacks and drove Arsenal up the pitch. Looked exhausted as the second half went on - big surprise he played the full 90 minutes.

Confidence was flowing and he gave Vlcek nightmares - the defender just resorted to kicking him. Came close to scoring after some glorious footwork created space. Joy to watch when he glides away from challenges.

#1822. Mikel Arteta responds to concerns over ‘exhausted’ Arsenal star after Slavia Prague win

Mikel Arteta has played down concerns over Declan Rice’s fitness after Arsenal’s 2-1 win over Slavia Prague in the Champions League on Wednesday night.

First-half goals from Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres gave Arsenal a commanding lead but Arsenal struggled in the second half and Slavia Prague deservedly pulled a goal back through Wiktor Nowak in the 90th minute.

Rice completed a full 90 minutes in Prague but the 27-year-old showed clear signs of tiredness in the second half.

‘Declan Rice is by far the best midfielder in the country, for me,’ former Arsenal and England Women’s midfielder Karen Carney told TNT Sports after Arsenal’s win.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

‘When he’s tired and fatigued they are a different team, and when he’s not in it.

‘In the second half he looked absolutely exhausted and then that’s, for me, when Arsenal are a different team and they kind of lose their way a little bit.

‘So that’s something I’m a little bit concerned about because he’s a top player but when his energy goes I think they slightly fall apart a bit.’

But when asked about the decision to play Rice for a full 90 minutes against Slavia Prague, Arteta said: ‘The game required it, and he did.

‘He was as well rested against Fleetwood so he had a very good week to recover before Liverpool.

‘It’s his second game in a week and not the fifth one. We expect our players to be able to do that and I think he had some very good moments throughout the game.’

Former Liverpool and England midfielder, Steve McManaman, who was a TNT Sports pundit alongside Carney for Arsenal’s game, also feels Arteta lacks squad depth in his attack.

‘They haven’t got enough forwards, have they? They just put more midfielders on and then move midfielders into forward positions so they all just lose a little bit of shape, that’s what I find,’ McManaman said.

‘You’ve got Declan on, you’ve got Zubimendi on, you’ve got Merino on, you’ve got Odegaard on, yet they were still just running all over and losing the ball.

‘So even the best can sort of lose their minds a little bit in European games. It shows you have to be focused all of the time, but the main thing is they’ve got the result, they went to Prague after a difficult Liverpool game and got three points. If they win against Hull at the weekend everyone will forget how difficult this game was.’

#1821. Guimaraes will not force Newcastle exit like Isak, says Howe

Eddie Howe is confident Bruno Guimarães will not demand to leave Newcastle United for Arsenal and echo Alexander Isak’s acrimonious departure to Liverpool last summer.

Howe admitted he could not guarantee that Guimarães will still be at the club in September but gave a strong defence of his captain’s character and insisted the Brazil international will return for pre-season training next week as planned.

Given the huge gap between Newcastle’s valuation of Guimarães and what Arsenal have indicated they would be willing to pay for the 28-year-old, there is a belief on Tyneside that the only way the captain would join the London club is if he behaved as badly as Isak did 12 months ago.

Newcastle value Guimarães at £100m, while Arsenal, through intermediaries, have only indicated they would be willing to pay about £60m including bonuses.

Isak did not travel on the club’s pre-season tour to Asia and then went on strike, refusing to train or play, until Newcastle agreed to sell him to Liverpool for a British record £128m on deadline day.

Asked if he feared a repeat of that with Guimarães this time around, Howe replied: “I’ve spoken to him as I would do with Bruno normally. He is a fantastic person and we have had some really good conversations both before, during and after the World Cup. What we speak about obviously has to remain private but he is a great player and a great person.

“Look, I don’t know what is going to happen with Bruno. That is up to other people to speculate about but also other people to have conversations about which I’m not a part of. I don’t think it is fair to compare situations and what happened previously. You’ve got to look at this in its own right.

“Bruno is captain of our football club. He has been an unbelievable player and person all the time we have worked together. I speak on behalf of everyone at the football club when I say we absolutely love him and of course everyone wants him to stay.

“The plan is for him to come back on July 31, he gets an extended break because of the World Cup and is currently enjoying a holiday with his family... There is nothing to say that Bruno won’t be back training with us.”

"We've had some really good conversations" 🗣️Eddie Howe speaks on Newcastle's transfer window so far and speculation around Bruno Guimarães ⚫️⚪️ pic.twitter.com/zB1W31Fne0

Arsenal’s interest in Guimarães is well known but there has been little progress since they began their pursuit more than a month ago.

Whether Arsenal can come up with an offer that tempts Newcastle into negotiations remains to be seen but it is thought the Premier League champions will try to harden up their interest before Guimarães returns for pre-season training.

Newcastle United were held to a 1-1 draw by Gateshead in their second pre-season friendly of the summer. A 79th-minute own-goal saved the Premier League club’s blushes but what did we learn from the match?

Steur did not grab many headlines when he arrived from Ajax for £20m earlier this month because of Sandro Tonali’s move to Tottenham Hotspur. But those familiar with Dutch football would have been excited that Newcastle had signed him.

The 18-year-old has impressed with his performances in training and gave a glimpse of his significant potential in his first public display. He is young and sources have told Telegraph Sport that he must develop physically before he is ready to play every week in the Premier League – but you can already see he has a very high ceiling.

As you would expect from a player described as Ajax’s best midfield prospect for a generation, he is assured on the ball. He is also a progressive passer, always looking to break the lines to get his team moving forward. Eddie Howe will love him.

Whisper it, but there were shades of Bruno Guimarães in his style of play, in the way he took the ball under pressure, in tight spaces, and played on the turn. Patience will be needed but the signs are really encouraging.

Guimarães’s future is all supporters have wanted to speak about for weeks. I was at a wedding on Friday and it felt like everyone asked me about it at some point – including the bride and groom immediately after completing their first dance.

It has already become a summer-long transfer saga that has not progressed since Arsenal’s interest was revealed last month. Telegraph Sport has repeatedly checked whether there have been any fresh developments over the past week and the answer from senior Newcastle sources has remained consistent: there are no talks ongoing and nothing has accelerated, despite claims Arsenal were preparing an official £70m bid.

However, Newcastle need clarity from their captain. He is due back for pre-season next week and is expected to fly to Spain for their training camp on July 31. He has intimated he would like to move to Arsenal but unless Newcastle receive a bid that matches their asking price, he and his representatives have been told he will not be allowed to leave.

Schär has been a brilliant player for Newcastle, but at the age of 34 and coming off the back of a serious ankle injury, he looked understandably rusty against Gateshead.

This will be the former Switzerland international’s ninth season at St James’ Park and he was at fault for giving away a soft free-kick that led to Gateshead scoring first.

Schar accepted a contract extension earlier this summer on reduced terms and although Howe values his quality and experience, he is going to be a back-up centre-back this season.

Neave, 19, started the game as Newcastle’s centre-forward as Will Osula was missing and Nick Woltemade and Yoane Wissa were given additional time off after playing in the World Cup for Germany and DR Congo respectively.

But those players will return to training next week and, although Neave forced a good save in the first half, he is not ready to start in the Premier League. There is little point keeping him around as a fourth-choice striker when he needs to be playing regularly at this stage of his career.

A loan move is on the cards and he could be a really smart signing for a Championship club or a team competing at the top of League One. The most important thing is that he gets regular senior games rather than hangs around at Newcastle on the fringes of the first-team squad.

Eddie Howe has said "he does not know" what will happen with Bruno but pretty strong defence of his character and denied similarities with Isak. Said they have spoken regularly throughout the summer and he will be back for pre season training on July 31st #nufc

Eddie Howe’s side will head down to Ashton Gate before jetting off to La Manga for a training camp on July 31, which will feature many of those who played in the World Cup, including Bruno Guimarães who has been linked with a move to Arsenal.

In Spain, Newcastle will face Valencia at the Mestalla, before returning to the UK to play Everton at Murrayfield. They will then host Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg at St James’ Park for their final tune-up matches before the Premier League season starts.

But the capacity has been steadily reduced for safety reasons and it is rarely used for anything other than local athletic events and Gateshead FC games.

There were officially only 50 tickets left for sale a few minutes before kick-off, but there are lots of empty seats.

There will also be a minute’s silence before today’s game against Gateshead.

It has been a difficult and, at times, acrimonious 12 months for Eddie Howe, who must have wondered whether the job was still worth the hassle given the criticism and online vitriol he received at times last season.

Few would have blamed him if he had quit, but Howe has always been fully committed and always knew there would be a period like this to come through.

He has been in the job almost five years and last season was the first time he had been vilified by a section of the fanbase. It left its mark. The boos that followed defeats at St James’ Park hurt and he worried the unity that had powered the team’s success had fractured irreparably.

The apparent collective shrug that greeted another run to the Carabao Cup semi-final, while guiding the team into the knockout rounds of the Champions League for the first time was a source of bewilderment and frustration.

Howe has not complained or moaned. Although he wobbled towards the end of last season and there were some calling for him to be sacked, he was supported and encouraged by those above him. That loyalty mattered.

The problem is, negativity lingers in the fanbase. Even a picture of Howe at pre-season training, posted on social media by the club, led to abusive comments questioning his ability and character. Some of it was toxic. It was rightly called out by other supporters.

Goals from Elliot Anderson (wonder what happened to him?!), Allan Saint-Maximin and Jay Turner-Cooke helped Newcastle overturn a 2-0 half-time deficit when they last visited Gateshead International Stadium in 2023.

Speaking through Gateshead’s club media, Cattermole said of facing Newcastle: “It’s obviously a different test. We have to respect the opposition, they’re a high-quality team and it might not be what we’re getting in our league but we’ll still try to implement what we believe we want to be in and out of possession. It’ll be a great physical challenge for us.

He added: “They [my players] have all shown up great. What a game for them. What a game for them to go and test yourself against some big names and fantastic coaching staff, for us all it’s a great challenge for us. We hope we give them a good test, we hope we give them the challenge they want as well. I played in many of these games as a player as well. We expect it to be competitive.”

The youngster has impressed in training over the last couple of weeks but it is thought he has a lot of work to do physically to be ready for the Premier League.

Full-back Leo Shahar was in and around the first team last season as was striker Sean Neave. Alex Murphy, who started one game in the Champions League last season is expected to go out on loan before the window shuts, but starts alongside Fabian Schar in the centre of defence.

Worryingly there is no sign of Sven Botman and Will Osula who both played in the behind-closed-doors friendly against Darlington last weekend.

Joelinton, Tino Livramento and Lewis Miley are still being eased back into things after injuries at the end of last season.

Another new signing, goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen, is on the bench and will play the second half against their National League neighbours.

Gateshead lost manager Rob Elliot to Carlisle at the end of last season and are now managed by former Sunderland and Middlesbrough midfielder Lee Cattermole.

Fabian Schär returns from an ankle injury that has sidelined him since January, but only one of Newcastle’s four summer signings (Sean Steur) starts.

Welcome to live coverage of Newcastle United’s pre-season friendly against North-East neighbours Gateshead. Eddie Howe’s side make the three-mile journey south of the River Tyne having beaten Darlington 3-0 in their first outing of the summer last weekend. The Magpies’ National League opponents this afternoon, helmed by former Sunderland captain Lee Cattermole, have already played three times in pre-season, thrashing Blyth 6-0 and drawing against Heaton Stannington and Hebburn Town. The Heed threatened a shock win in their last meeting with Newcastle three summers’ ago, leading 2-0 at the interval before conceding three second-half goals.

This contest at Gateshead International Stadium will be Newcastle’s first match since the death of Kevin Keegan and the club have confirmed that a minute of silence will be observed before kick-off. Newcastle’s men’s, women’s and academy teams will wear black armbands for all pre-season matches this summer.

Newcastle United's men's, women's and Under-21s teams will wear black armbands across all pre-season matches this summer as the club honours the life of Kevin Keegan.Full details ⤵️

Newcastle will welcome Liverpool, with whom Keegan enjoyed success in the 1970s, to St James’ Park for their Premier League opener, and the two sides are in talks over a suitable pre-match tribute. Flowers, messages and mementos have been laid outside Newcastle’s ground since Keegan’s death on Monday, including a heartfelt message penned by fellow club legend Alan Shearer, which read: “I hope you realised how much you meant, to me, to this club, to everyone. Thank you does not seem enough. Rest In Peace Boss. Alan Shearer.”

With regards to the football, there is an acceptance among Newcastle supporters that, having finished 12th in the Premier League last season and lost Anthony Gordon, Kieran Trippier and Sandro Tonali, this is a summer of transition. The uncertainty surrounding the future of £100m-rated club captain Bruno Guimarães, who is on the radar of Arsenal, will be a concern; Newcastle will be keen to avoid a repeat of the furore that circled Alexander Isak’s departure last summer. Guimarães will join the team next week following his World Cup exploits with Brazil and is expected to take part in Newcastle’s La Manga training camp, which starts on July 31.

Summer signings Sean Steur and Ewen Jaouen were each handed 45 minutes in the behind-closed-doors victory over Darlington, during which Howe used different XIs for the two halves. #1818. Cardiff 3-3 West Ham: Scott Parker oversees incredible fightback in first game in charge

Scott Parker saw his West Ham side recover from three goals down to draw 3-3 at Cardiff in a thrilling first game in charge.

Jack Moylan’s first hat-trick in English football had Cardiff in cruise control at half-time and Hammers fans venting their anger.

But the Hammers – inspired by captain Jarrod Bowen – fought back in incredible fashion as Divine Mukasa, Arne Engels and Max Kilman netted to secure a point.

Parker was confirmed as Hammers boss on Wednesday morning – just 24 hours after Nuno Espirito Santo’s departure – but it was a tough watch for the former England midfielder initially as Moylan had Cardiff 3-0 ahead inside 39 minutes.

Moylan scored a hat-trick on his Republic of Ireland debut against Grenada in May, but this was his first club treble since scoring three for Shelbourne in May 2023.

The draw extends Cardiff’s unbeaten home league run to 10 games over the last two seasons, while West Ham occupy the final play-off place in eighth.

Nuno’s 13-month tenure had ended after the Hammers had won just twice in six matches and lost successive home games to Southampton and West Brom.

Taty Castellanos had hinted at better times ahead, forcing Nathan Trott in to early action after Bowen’s effort had deflected to him.

But the Hammers were behind after Alex Robertson found Moylan in the 11th minute.

Moylan advanced to find the top corner of Mads Hermansen’s net with a ferocious strike from 20 yards.

Hermansen tipped aside Calum Scanlon’s cross and Will Fish headed over as Cardiff probed.

Moylan cleverly slowed down for Morato to bundle him over, a clear penalty.

Angry Hammers fans responded with cries of ‘you’re not fit to wear the shirt’, and many of them appeared to be making a swift departure three minutes later.

Joel Bagan’s corner cleared Fish at the near post, but Moylan came in behind him to head home his sixth goal in five games, and his 10th of the season.

Parker sent on Mohamadou Kante and Joel Piroe for Soungoutou Magassa and Castellanos at half-time and there was instantly more conviction from the Hammers.

Bowen floated a delicious pass through after 58 minutes, and Mukasa lifted the ball over Trott and in off a post.

The deficit was reduced further seven minutes later when Piroe flicked on Bowen’s pass and Engels slid home his first Hammers goal.

Kante nearly toe poked the ball past Trott before Kilman touched home Bowen’s brilliant cross, and West Ham almost won it through substitutes Ezra Mayers and Tomas Soucek.

#1816. RB Leipzig 2-3 Man City: Erling Haaland scores winner to edge Champions League thriller

Erling Haaland struck a late winner as Manchester City edged a thrilling Champions League clash with RB Leipzig 3-2.

City were twice pegged back by the enterprising Germans, who are managed by their former defender Martin Demichelis, but Haaland settled the contest 12 minutes from time.

It was his 14th goal of the season, his 13th in nine career appearances against Leipzig and his 62nd in 61 Champions League games.

City had taken the lead with an own goal from Castello Lukeba but the hosts quickly levelled through Ridle Baku.

Enzo Fernandez restored the lead but City needed Haaland’s late intervention to secure victory after the impressive Antonio Nusa struck a second equaliser.

Despite the win, it was not a night City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma will care to remember.

Leipzig took the game to City early on and Nusa troubled the Italian with a shot from the edge of the box which he fumbled over the crossbar.

Nusa was then involved in a break down the right which led to an opportunity for the inrushing David Raum but his effort was blocked.

Christoph Baumgartner then went close with a curling effort from distance and Brajan Gruda also fired wide from a dangerous position.

City began to settle and Phil Foden curled an effort narrowly wide but they benefited from a huge stroke of luck to take the lead in the 37th minute.

Nico O’Reilly raced on to a long ball from Rayan Cherki but his cutback appeared wasteful. Lukeba, however, did not realise he was under no pressure and ended up bundling the ball into his own net.

Leipzig regrouped at half-time and returned in determined fashion with Nusa and Baumgartner both forcing saves out of Donnarumma.

But the City goalkeeper was badly caught out when he strayed off his line as Baku broke down the left. He may have been anticipating a cross as Baku reached the byline and rifled in a shot at his near post.

Leipzig could have had another moments later as Nusa played in Ezechiel Banzuzi with a backheel but he missed the target.

City rallied and Haaland got his first chance of the game as a Cherki pass was deflected to him but Maarten Vandevoordt kept out the Norwegian’s snap-shot.

They regained the lead after Leipzig allowed Iliman Ndiaye too much space on the left and he whipped in a cross for Fernandez to head home.

Again City could not hold on to the advantage as Nusa drilled a low shot across goal to equalise from a clever pass by Christopher Nkunku.

But Haaland, despite a largely quiet night, was not to be denied and raced in at the back post to slide home Elliot Anderson’s superb low ball into the box.

Both sides hit the woodwork in the closing stages, with Donnarumma almost embarrassed again as Raum’s free-kick looped over him and struck the bar. Cherki also thumped against the bar at the other end.

#1815. Mikel Arteta brands Arsenal stars ‘extremely far from our standards’ in Slavia Prague win

Mikel Arteta was not impressed with his Arsenal team in the second half of their 2-1 win at Slavia Prague on Wednesday, saying they were ‘extremely far from our standards’ after the interval.

The Gunners continued their unbeaten start to the Champions League group stage with victory in Czech Republic, with three wins and a draw from their opening four games.

Noni Madueke opened the scoring after just nine minutes and the Premier League champions had a two-goal lead by half-time thanks to Viktor Gyokeres.

Slavia Prague made things difficult for their high profile guests, though, producing 18 shots over the match and scoring a late consolation through Wiktor Novak.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Arteta praised the Czech side, who have picked up just one point from four matches, but accepted that the second half performance from his men left a lot to be desired.

‘First of all, you have to value the fact it’s very difficult to win away from home,’ Arteta told a post-match press conference. ‘We’ve done it against a very tough opponent, we expected that toughness.

‘Two very different halves – the first we played at a really high level in terms of intensity, tempo, quality and clarity in what we had to do, and what the game was demanding. We were very efficient – we should have scored three, four or five.

‘We didn’t make that gap, and at half-time, the message was clear. There was still a lot to do in the game – this was a team we were up against with huge spirit, and if you give them something, they will grab it.

‘Right from the beginning of the half, we were extremely far from our standards, the basics, the concepts, and everything we discussed to avoid. It was far from what we expect from each other, but we found a way to hold onto the result and win the game.’

‘It’s our third away game in quick succession, and we’re the only team to have played three away games in the Champions League and just one at home – there are a lot of factors – but I don’t like to use that, because in the first half we were at the level we wanted.

‘I take full responsibility for the drop in the second half.’

Goalkeeper David Raya had a similar report to his manager and said Arsenal must improve as the campaign continues.

‘First half, we played really really well. We dominated the whole game, created a lot of chances and could have scored a few more goals,’ he said.

#1814. Steve McManaman says he ‘feels sorry’ for two Arsenal stars

Steve McManaman said he ‘felt sorry’ for Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz following Arsenal’s 2-1 win over Slavia Prague as Mikel Arteta’s playing style means the forwards often ‘get the blame’ for the side’s more cautious performances.

Arsenal maintained their unbeaten record in this season’s Champions League as a pair of first-half strikes from Noni Madueke and Gyokeres proved decisive before Wiktor Nowak’s late consolation.

The result ensured the Gunners, last year’s runners-up, sit third four matches into their league-phase campaign following previous victories over Napoli and Lille and a 2-2 draw away to Bayern Munich.

September’s 3-0 defeat at the hands of Brighton in the Premier League remains Arsenal’s only loss in all competitions this term, an impressive run that Arteta’s men will look to continue when they return to action at home to Hull this weekend.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Arteta made a total of six changes to his team that got the better of Liverpool on Sunday, with Gyokeres starting through the middle in place of Havertz at Prague’s Fortuna Arena.

The Sweden international has endured a tough start to the new season but played a key role in the opening goal, assisting Madueke with a hooked pass behind Slavia Prague’s defence for Arsenal’s breakthrough inside just nine minutes.

He then got on the scoresheet himself to double the visitors’ advantage shortly before the break, beating Nazar Domchak with a superb effort that went in off the upright.

While it proved a far more difficult second half for Gyokeres as Arsenal held firm to protect their lead, ex-Liverpool and Real Madrid star McManaman felt the striker should have come away proud with his night’s work.

However, the ex-England international expects Havertz to return to Arteta’s starting XI when the north Londoners return to top-flight action against Hull on Saturday.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘I liked him in the first half. I think in the second half, when Arsenal became a little bit dishevelled, they weren’t as close to him so I think it’s hard,’ McManaman said of Gyokeres’ performance.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘When they are playing well, he is up there on his own. In the first half, they were very compact, they were very close to him, they were getting around the sides, they were making chances, so he looked dangerous.

‘In the second half, when it got really stretched and they were wide and he was up on his own, he looked as if he was just left alone a lot.

‘I think when Arsenal play as more of a unit, attacking and defending together, I think he looks better.’

Given Arsenal aren’t renowned for being the most ‘entertaining’ of teams, McManaman finds himself ‘feeling sorry’ for Gyokeres and Havertz in certain matches.

‘I do feel sorry for Arsenal forwards sometimes because they’re not an entertaining team, they’re not like a Barcelona. They defend very deep, they defend as a whole and it’s a long way to get to the other end of the pitch to score goals,’ he added.

‘They’re never going to be this entertaining, lovely, free-flowing side scoring goal after goal after goal, and then Gyokeres and Havertz sometimes get the blame because of that. It’s normally the midfielders and the defenders that we talk about.

‘But as I said, Gyokeres had a great first half, he did his best in the second half and he deserves what he got because he got an assist and he got a goal.’

Asked if it could be time for Arteta to trust Gyokeres with more minutes, McManaman replied: ‘Whenever a big game comes around, Arteta reverts to Havertz doesn’t he?

‘People keep saying that Havertz scores goals in the big games and he certainly did that against Liverpool so you can’t really contest that.

‘But I just think he trusts Havertz a little bit more. That’s all it is.

‘Gyokeres played against Slavia Prague and he did exactly what he needed to do. He had an impact on the game, he had a huge impact on the game and we’ll wait and see for Saturday.

‘But I always think that when big games come around, if it was a final or Arsenal or Manchester City, if both Gyokeres and Havertz are fit, then Arteta would always revert back to Havertz.’

Facing the media shortly after the final whistle, Arteta heaped praise on Gyokeres’ all-round display, applauding the Swede’s ‘connection’ with his team-mates.

The Arsenal head coach explained: ‘I thought he was really good. It was a game we believed would be really good for him, for the demands the opponent puts in and the spaces he could use.

‘He’s done it really well, not just for the assist and the goal, but he was really connected to the team. It’s really great news for him, because he really needed that performance.’

On Gyokeres’ combination play, Arteta added: ‘He did that really well, understood really well when to appear, when to threaten, because they leave people, they follow man-to-man in the midfield and leave spaces there.

‘So when I said he was really connected to the team, that was another example. I thought he had a great performance alongside the goal and assist.’

Asked whether not starting had been a challenge for Gyokeres, Arteta replied: ‘It’s a question for him, but I’d imagine every player wants to play every game, and Viktor is no different.

‘The players need to impact the game like he has done today when they get the opportunity, to show the level they can produce. It’s really positive for the team.’

#1813. Slavia Prague 1-2 Arsenal: Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres score as Gunners stay unbeaten in Champions League

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Viktor Gyokeres grasped his opportunity as Arsenal beat Slavia Prague 2-1 in the Champions League.

Gyokeres made the most of a rare start, his sixth of the season, with an assist and a stylish goal as the Gunners climbed to third in the Champions League table.

Noni Madueke scored the opener and Arsenal were cruising until the closing stages, when Wiktor Nowak pulled one back to leave Mikel Arteta’s men hanging on in stoppage time.

Gyokeres, whose only previous goal this season was in the Carabao Cup defeat at Fleetwood, was one of six changes Arteta made to the side which beat Liverpool 1-0 at the weekend.

Ben White and Piero Hincapie started in defence in the Czech capital with Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino slotting into midfield and Eberechi Eze a lively presence behind Gyokeres.

There was also a late run-out for youngster Max Dowman, who is suspended domestically but eligible for Europe following his red card at Fleetwood.

Madueke put them ahead in the ninth minute after Gyokeres muscled his marker off the ball on the halfway line and hooked the ball forward into space.

The England winger raced past the defence and slid his angled shot through the legs of Nazar Domchak.

The Slavia goalkeeper then had to come out and block from Gyokeres, tip Merino’s drive over the crossbar and make a fine reflex save from the Spain international.

Arsenal had a mild scare eight minutes before half-time when Tomas Holes got free in the area at a long throw and poked his shot wide.

But the Premier League champions immediately went up the other end and doubled their lead through Gyokeres.

The Sweden striker exchanged passes with Merino as he made his way into the area before opening up his body and clipping the ball across Domchak and in off the far post.

#1812. Bukayo Saka ‘a bit fragile,’ reckons former Arsenal and Manchester United defender

Silvestre sees Madueke as an improving force in Saka’s absence, although there is still room to become sharper in the final third.

‘That’s why you have a big squad and Madueke would start for most of the teams in the Premier League, if not all,’ said the Frenchman. ‘He has the quality and I think he is getting his confidence now, he is trying to score and create more.

‘He doesn’t have the killer instinct yet, but he is growing into it and he is trying to get there.’

Silvestre, who won five Premier League titles with Manchester United, reckons Arsenal’s forward line as a whole can let them down, with their strength clearly lying in defence. The recent 1-0 win at Liverpool being a good illustration.

‘Winning at Anfield, with a clean sheet as well makes it a very good defensive performance,’ he said. ‘We can’t say the same with the offense. I would say that’s one for the record, and one that you look back at the end of the season and say it was an important 3 points. But it wasn’t a full on, top class, 90 minute performance from Arsenal.

‘But it’s important to get those wins against teams who are also potentially in the race, and to keep your distance from them.

‘The positives are the defensive side of things, the 3 points, and the fact that it was at Anfield. It breaks that negative dynamic but I think it’s just for the stats really.

‘I think you need your best players at the key moments featuring in the semi-finals and the final of competitions. Arsenal need to keep Timber fit, Saliba is coming back also. You need your strong 11 and the best defence once you reach the final. So it’s still a long way away but they defend well, as a unit for sure.’
