#1792. Parker to treat three-goal comeback as a learning opportunity for West Ham

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

New West Ham boss Scott Parker says Wednesday's remarkable three-goal comeback against Cardiff City should be viewed as a learning opportunity for everyone at the club.

Former Hammers midfielder Parker was only appointed by the club on Wednesday morning, following the dismissal of Nuno Espirito Santo.

And within a few short hours, he cut a frustrated figure on the touchline in the Welsh capital as Jack Moylan's hat-trick saw West Ham go 3-0 down within 39 minutes.

However, second-half strikes from Divine Mukasa, Arne Engels and Max Kilman rescued a point for Parker's new team, who amassed 14 shots and 2.52 expected goals after the interval, compared to three efforts and 0.08 xG for Cardiff.

Prior to half-time, both teams had four shots apiece, but Cardiff had won the xG battle by 1.07 to 0.27, with their figure boosted by a Moylan penalty.

Speaking after the game, Parker said: "I met the boys for the first time this morning at the airport, so I haven't had much input, but I wanted to be on the sideline, and I decided not to just sit in the stands and oversee it.

"In the first half, we were clearly really poor. I thought we were poor in both phases of the game.

"Out of possession, we were quite passive at certain moments, and with the ball there was certainly a lot to work on. There were a lot of backwards passes, and the goalkeeper had a lot of touches."

Asked if West Ham's comeback came as a shock, Parker said: "Maybe not so much a surprise, but a big learning. The second half was the polar opposite to the first, really, and to come back into the game like we did was brilliant.

"It was a forceful team, an aggressive team, a front-footed team, which was obviously a big improvement.

"There's a lot of learning to take from this. It's a quick turnaround, but we'll go to Blackburn with a bit more influence from me."

Scott has his say   https://t.co/QMrUl32HIw https://t.co/kh7rIMcXRy

— West Ham United (@WestHam) November 4, 2026

West Ham sit eighth in the Championship after their draw, occupying the final play-off place, though they did inch within five points of leaders Middlesbrough, who lost 2-0 at Wrexham.

Goals from George Thomason and Oliver Rathbone in the final 20 minutes condemned Boro to just their second defeat of the campaign, and their first since going down 2-1 to Blackburn Rovers on August 22.

Wolves can now usurp them at the summit if they beat Wrexham in one of Saturday's early kick-offs, having climbed to second with a dramatic 2-1 win at Bristol City.

Cesar Peixoto's side looked set to see their unbeaten run halted at four games when Scott Twine's glorious free-kick put Bristol City in front in the first half, with the visitors still behind entering the 82nd minute.

But Newcastle United loanee Sean Neave scored his first two senior goals after coming off the bench, with the 19-year-old's late double flipping the result on its head.

Wolves have now lost just two of their last 19 league games against Bristol City (W13 D4), with their previous meeting in December 2017 also being a 2-1 victory secured by two late goals.

#1791. Tottenham new boys score in shoot-out win over Sydney FC

Tottenham Hotspur fans enjoyed their first glimpse of summer signings Andy Robertson and Sandro Tonali in the shirt, with both players scoring penalties in the shoot-out that followed a 1-1 draw with Sydney FC.

Spurs took the lead through a first-half Mathys Tel free-kick, before Roberto De Zerbi’s youthful defence was undone by Takahiro Sekine, who tucked away one of the Australian side’s only chances of the game.

Magic from Mathys Tel 🪄A brilliant free kick from the Frenchman gets @spursofficial off to a flyer, as the striker puts it top bins to take a 1-0 lead in SydneyWatch #TOTvSYD live and exclusive on Paramount+ 📺 pic.twitter.com/ntqTgleasJ

Tonali was brought on as a half-time substitute, before Robertson took the captain’s armband from Archie Gray after he was introduced in the 65th minute.

The former Liverpool left-back delivered three dangerous crosses which went unconverted, something of a theme for a Spurs team who failed to make the most of long spells of dominance.

James Maddison and Mateus Fernandes were not in the match-day squad, while Pedro Porro, Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven and Jean Paul van Hecke have yet to join the group after the World Cup.

There was another impressive showing from 17-year-old prospect Luca Williams-Barnett, who is pushing for first-team opportunities this upcoming season.

Penalties followed the final whistle, with Spurs scoring all four of their spot kicks. Goalkeeper Martin Dubravka, signed on a free transfer this summer, saved one and Sydney FC’s Josh Lacey hit the post to give Spurs the spoils 4-2.

Spurs win the shoot-out 4-2. That will be that.

Hoefsloot dives to his right and pushes Donley’s penalty around the post.

But then Dubravka saves from Popovic, and Spurs remain 3-2 up. Score the next one and they win the shoot-out.

Very similar placing to Tonali’s penalty. Does Dubravka have a save in him?

He doesn’t need to have one because Josh Lacey has hit the post. 3-2 to Spurs after three pens each.

Plenty of power and right into the side netting. No mistake from Spurs’s big money summer signing.

Dubravka then guesses the right way, but Toure finds the bottom left corner. 2-2.

The 17-year-old takes the mickey a little bit, dinking the ball straight down the middle. Spurs score their first penalty.

Then Popovic steps up and sends Dubravka the wrong way. 1-1.

Spurs were the game’s dominant force, but they did not convert that control into enough goals. No cause for alarm though, and no injuries from what we can tell. There will be some penalties on the way.

Williams-Barnett with a superb piece of control and turn forward, but the danger was snuffed out as he dribbled the ball into the penalty area. Then the youngster shoots from outside the box, deflected behind for a corner.

Andy Robertson has been impressive, and the goalkeeper makes a fingertip save to flick his low cross away from danger. Almost third time lucky for Yang who was waiting at the back post for a tap-in.

Andy Robertson's first outing as a Spurs player 🫡 pic.twitter.com/q5bdzQknJ2

Spurs controlling possession, pushing for the goal that would spare them having to take some penalties. As happens with this friendlies, the game has become more bitty since all the changes.

If the game finishes as a draw, there will be a penalty shoot-out. Donley has fizzed some crisp forward passes since coming on in midfield. Then Donley underlaps, picked out by Williams-Barnett but his low cross is straight at the goalkeeper.

Andy Robertson getting forward to good effect once again, standing up a cross for Yang in the middle but the substitute heads wide from seven or eight yards out.

Referee waves play on as Spurs pour forward and Robertson flashes a ball across the box, and the slight deflection was enough to put off Yang at the back post and he missed the target. Should have been a tap in.

Spurs close to a second, but Tonali’s shot from the edge of the box is pushed around the post. There was more good approach play from Williams-Barnett to tee up the Italian.

More Spurs changes: Andy Robertson is on, and takes the armband, he replaces Kyerematen. Up front, Richarlison and Solomon are off, replaced by Min-Hyeok and Dane Scarlett. Donley and Melia replace Gray and Gallagher in midfield.

A couple of appeals for a Spurs penalty after Kyerematen burst beyond the Sydney defence from left-back. He could have crossed sooner, but was tackled, and then there was a challenge on Richarlison. Referee waves it away.

Very youthful Spurs back four on the pitch now, which played a part in the nature of the equaliser they conceded. No Romero, Van de Ven, Van Hecke or Senesi available for selection today, but Andy Robertson is warming up on the touchline.

Spurs straight back into another long spell of possession, with Tonali winning a foul in midfield after a smooth turn forward.

A touch of ill fortunate for Spurs, the half-time substitute Takai inadvertently poked the ball through to Sekine who lifted the ball over Dubravka to equalise. Delicate finish, and Spurs are breached.

Conor Gallagher still closing down tirelessly, but he has been a little untidy with the ball at his feet. I suspect he was the bleep test winner in training. Sydney do well to play through the pressure and keep possession for a while.

Good industry from Tonali in midfield to regain possession, and Williams-Barnett shows real poise on the ball again. Easy to see why Spurs are excited about him.

Kyerematen defends well at the back post when it looked like Macallister was about to head at goal.

Then Spurs are away on the break, and Williams-Barnett skims the crossbar with a left-footed shot from a tight angle.

Three half-time Spurs changes: Tel, Bergvall and Davies off, Takai, Tonali and Williams-Barnett are on. Takai goes to centre-back with 17-year-old Williams-Barnett in an attacking midfield position.

A decent half’s work from Spurs, they look in a good place physically and their high pressing has caught the eye. Not quite clinical enough in the penalty area so far though, they have butchered some good chances.

Sydney have come to life as an attacking force, Spurs’s defence undone by a ball over the top. Dubravka caught in no-man’s-land, and Mac Allister poked the ball beyond him but did not generate enough power to score.

Cracking effort from the Sydney forward Macallister, trying to chip Dubravka from some 45 yards out. The goalkeeper was worried and scrambling, the effort misses the target.

Sydney looking ragged now, and Gallagher cracks a shot off the foot of the post from the edge of the box. Then Youlley takes on a shot from long range which is high, wide and handsome. Richarlison is then fouled by Popovic, dragging down the forward to stop a counter. Yellow card.

Conor Gallagher is charging forward at every opportunity, applying pressure on Sydney’s defenders whenever they have the ball. With no European football, Spurs can really lean into a high-octane approach this season.

Great take, right footed to the the goalkeeper’s side, and the strike was too powerful for Hoefsloot. A clean hit, and Spurs now lead. A well-deserved goal on the balance of play.

The game has slipped into a lull now, after a bright Spurs start. De Zerbi’s team do now have a free-kick at the edge of the D after Manor Solomon is fouled.

Tel amnd Gallagher threaten down the left for Spurs, with the midfielder finding the winger with a reverse pass. Tel’s cross is cleared.

Then Sydney muster their first shot of the game, Youlley with a strike from 25 yards out which Dubravka pushes away from danger.

Sydney FC starting to get their foot on the ball a little more now, but still no sign that they have capability to hurts Spurs going forward. Kyerematen is then fouled in the Sydney half.

Sydney are yet to have a touch in the Spurs penalty area, it has been one-way traffic so far. De Zerbi will be pleased with what he has watched so far, but no killer touch in the box as yet.

Conor Gallagher with a nice touch to win a free-kick near the left touchline. Sydney just about hanging on. The goalkeeper claims Tel’s cross from the free-kick.

Spurs’s closing down is choking Sydney’s build up play, and Gallagher wastes a good chance when free in the box. Shot blocked when there was time and space to pick his spot.

Lucas Bervall’s low cross is turned behind for a corner and Spurs remain in the ascendancy. Another threatening delivery, and Ben Davies may well have had a shout for a penalty, dragged to the turf by Grant. If this was a Premier League game, I’m sure VAR would have taken a close look at that.

Hoefsloot with a really poor pass from his six-yard box, straight into the path of Tel 25 yards out, but his side-footed effort was saved by the goalkeeper. Pitches like this make technical errors an inevitability.

Sydney’s goalkeeper Hoefsloot punches a corner clear under some pressure, attacking set-pieces were a rare positive for Spurs last season. The Premier League team are dominating possession in the early minutes.

Conor Gallagher and Richarlison leading an aggressive Tottenham press in the early exchanges. Tel enjoys plenty of touches down the left flank, but his inswinging cross from the left is headed clear. Rio Kyerematen is puhsing on from left-back.

After a rendition of Oh When The Saints Go Marching In on the trumpet, we are under way. A chance for Aussie Spurs fans to feel like they are in N17 for the evening.

The pitch looks slightly more lush than the surface Chelsea had to play on across town yesterday. The Allianz Stadium looks distinctly similar to the Etihad. Archie Gray captains Spurs.

No James Maddison in the squad for this game, perhaps still being managed physically after last year’s serious knee injury. Suspect we will see a more senior side picked for the friendly against Chelsea on Saturday.

The 21-year-old has a sweet left foot, on display when he scored this goal against Manchester City while on loan at Leyton Orient.

JAMIE DONLEY. THAT'S INCREDIBLE. 🤯The @SpursOfficial loanee with an incredible effort from distance that ends up in the net to give @leytonorientfc the opening goal against Manchester City 😱#EmiratesFACup pic.twitter.com/bHnKg92Q2y

Lucas Bergvall has been linked with a move away from Spurs, but he starts in midfield. No Fernandes in the squad at all. No summer signings in the starting line-up, but Tonali and Andy Robertson are on the bench.

Spurs starting XI: Dubravka; Kyerematen, Davies, Hardy, Tye Hall; Gray, Bergvall, Solomon, Gallagher, Tel; Richarlison

Subs: Kinsky, Robertson, Takai, Tingey, Byrne, Tyrese Hall, Russell-Denny, Donley, Tonali, Ajayi, Yang, Williams-Barnett, Scarlett

Spurs fans took their first look at summer signing Mateus Fernandes in a 2-0 victory over Auckland, and their pre-season tour continues today against Sydney FC.

Fernandes, an £85m purchase from West Ham United, also scored a stunning volley in a behind-closed-doors game against MK Dons.

Sandro Tonali is part of the travelling squad for these friendlies, as is new centre-back Jean Paul van Hecke. Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero and Pedro Porro have been given extra time off after their respective nations reached the World Cup final, won by Porro and Spain.

Van Hecke and Senesi ranked very highly among defenders for progressive passing, which offers an insight into the qualities Roberto De Zerbi is prioritising this summer.

The Italian likes his teams to bait opponents into pressing them high up the pitch, before moving the ball through central areas using third-man combinations and wall passes. The addition of two ball-playing centre-backs and two new central midfielders should mean Spurs can play like a recognisable De Zerbi team.

While Dane Scarlett and Richarlison scored against Auckland, Spurs’s squad still lacks high-class options in forward areas, with a move for Bournemouth’s Eli Junior Kroupi mooted earlier in the summer.

Spurs fans will be excited to watch 17-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett, the midfielder who is one of the outstanding players in his age group in the country.

“He’s a talent,” Ledley King said. “There’s a lot of hard work ahead of him, but there’s no doubt that he’s someone with great ability.

“He’s seen players like Harry Kane come through the academy and, through sheer hard work and determination, put themselves in a position to kick on. He couldn’t have a better role model.

“There’s no doubt we’re excited by his talent and the next part will be up to him.”

#1790. Gaziantep vs Kasimpasa - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 04 Nov 2026 16:42, Last updated: 04 Nov 2026 16:42

Gaziantep will be desperate to halt their alarming slide when they welcome Kasimpasa to Gaziantep Stadyumu on Friday in the Turkish Super Lig.

The hosts have lost five consecutive league matches and are hovering just above the relegation zone with eight points from their opening 10 fixtures, while their visitors occupy fifth place with 17 points and arrive unbeaten in their last three league outings.

Gaziantep have endured a miserable spell in the league, with their latest setback coming in a 2-0 defeat away to Trabzonspor.

Orhan Ak's side struggled to make an impact against the Black Sea outfit, conceding once in each half as they suffered another damaging result following defeats against Erzurumspor, Istanbul Basaksehir, Corum and Kocaelispor.

Their 4-0 Turkish Cup victory over Etimesgutspor provided some relief, but that result has done little to disguise their domestic difficulties, particularly as they have scored just twice across their last five league matches while conceding 12 goals.

The lack of attacking output is becoming a significant concern for Ak, whose team have struggled to turn possession into meaningful opportunities and have repeatedly found themselves chasing matches after falling behind.

Gaziantep have also struggled to establish Gaziantep Stadyumu as a source of points, failing to win any game as hosts yet, drawing two and losing three times in five home matches.

However, the Falcons are unbeaten in their last five meetings with the Apaches, picking up three wins and two draws, while they have also avoided defeat in their last three encounters against them as hosts, winning twice and drawing once.

Kasimpasa, meanwhile, have enjoyed a considerably more encouraging opening to the campaign, losing just one of their 10 league games so far while recording four wins and five draws.

Emre Belozoglu's team were held to an entertaining 2-2 draw by Besiktas in their previous league outing, with Claudio Winck and Michael Rafferty finding the net as they twice threatened to take all three points.

That result extended their unbeaten league sequence to three matches, following victories over Eyupspor and Samsunspor, while they also recorded a 3-1 win over Corluspor in the Turkish Cup, extending their unbeaten run across all competitions to four matches.

Kasimpasa have also collected useful points on their travels this season, recording 10 points from five away games, with three wins, one draw and one defeat, which should give them optimism ahead of this trip.

Gaziantep have several availability concerns ahead of Friday's encounter, with Myenty Abena facing suspension following a yellow-card accumulation, while Ulrich Meleke, Ogun Ozcicek, Arda Kizildag and Sontje Hansen are among those carrying injuries.

Serdar Dursun is also expected to miss out, while Nazim Sangare and Fuat Bavuk remain unavailable.

Kasimpasa have fewer confirmed concerns, although Kamil Ahmet Corekci is expected to remain sidelined with an Achilles tendon injury.

Godfried Frimpong and Kevin Mouanga are also carrying fitness problems, leaving the visitors potentially short of defensive options, while no further suspensions have been reported.

Adrian Benedyczak has scored six goals in the league this season, and he will be the man to watch for the Apaches in this encounter.

Dadakdeniz; Perez, Abena, Sylla, Calhanoglu; Bacuna; Sorescu, Gidado, Maxim, Kozlowski; Stewart

Gianniotis; Jensen, Ilie, Arous, Winck; Demirbay, Mendes; Hajradinovic, Rak-Sakyi, Kol; Benedyczak

Gaziantep's home advantage and historical record in this fixture could make Friday's encounter more competitive than the league standings suggest, but their current defensive problems are difficult to overlook.

Kasimpasa have shown considerably more attacking consistency, and their recent form should ultimately see them claim all three points.

#1789. Chelsea injury update: Emi Martinez, Joao Pedro, Maxence Lacroix latest news and return dates

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea have had a few days rest following their 2-0 win over Manchester United, with the focus now on Sunderland.

The Blues will make the trip up north to the Stadium of Light on Sunday afternoon, hoping to sign off for the final international break of 2026 on a positive note.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso could be boosted by the return of Emi Martinez for the game and will provide an update on the fitness of star striker Joao Pedro, who has now missed the last three games.

Facing a Sunderland side who are bottom of the Premier League table and trying to balance playing in the Europa League, Chelsea may fancy their chances of avenging the 2-1 loss on the final day of last season - a result that cost them European football.

With that in mind, here is the latest Chelsea injury news and return dates…

Martinez has missed Chelsea's last three games across all competitions after undergoing surgery for a broken jaw sustained upon a collision with Jarrad Branthwaite in the win over Everton last month.

The Argentina international was expected to be sidelined for around six weeks, but Standard Sport reported before the win against Manchester United that there was optimism Martinez could be back fit ahead of schedule, and Alonso confirmed as much in the pre-match press conference.

"Yes, there is a chance. We need to still wait for next week, but let's see how things go," Alonso said in response to being asked if Martinez could return against Sunderland. "But there is a chance."

It would appear that Martinez is on course to be in contention to replace Mike Penders in goal at the Stadium of Light on Sunday afternoon as he was put through his paces at Cobham on Wednesday ahead of Chelsea’s final fixture before the November international break.

The 34-year-old was spotted in the session wearing a protective face mask and will need to do so if selected against Sunderland.

"In case he's ready to play, he will need a face mask probably," Alonso added.

Potential return date: Sunday November 8, vs Sunderland (A)

Joao Pedro was forced to sit out Chelsea’s rare home loss to Tottenham due to picking up a thigh injury in training on the eve of the game.

Martinez and Chelsea defender spotted in training after Alonso updates

Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal triple raid; Man Utd want Bellingham

Jesse Derry back at Chelsea tonight in Sporting loan twist

Winter escapes and activities to end the year in style

No definitive timeframe has yet been set for the return of the Brazilian and Chelsea will be understandably cautious with such an important player, who seems unlikely to play again before the November international break.

“He has an injury on his thigh and he's going be out for a few weeks," Alonso said on Joao Pedro before the defeat by Liverpool. "Let's see how many. We don't want to predict on that. But not ready for the next games.

“He's a key player. We will miss him, but we have to be ready to deal with the injury, and be competitive and try and win with the players we have available. This is the situation.”

Potential return date: Saturday November 21, vs Leeds (H)

Jordan Henderson was a surprise absentee from the Chelsea squad to face Manchester United, despite having played 90 minutes against former club Liverpool in the Carabao Cup three days prior.

The summer signing has forged a decent midfield pairing with Moises Caicedo of late and should be in contention to face another of his old clubs this weekend as any concerns over an injury have already been allayed.

Alonso said Henderson was ill and suffering with a fever last Saturday.

“He's ill," Alonso said of Henderson to TNT Sports. “There's no injury, but he was not feeling well yesterday and today had a fever in the morning, so he was not feeling good enough to come with the team.”

Potential return date: Sunday November 8, vs Sunderland (A)

Chelsea’s influential captain Reece James suffered a knee injury in training at Cobham on his return from another hamstring issue.

After consulting with a specialist, he underwent successful surgery last month that was described as “minor” and Alonso has been reluctant to put a date on his potential return.

However, Standard Sport understands that it is likely to be around three months before James is back in action.

Maxence Lacroix limped off late in the first half of the Carabao Cup penalty shoot-out defeat to Liverpool with a suspected hamstring injury.

Alonso said that Chelsea would need to assess the problem before estimating a recovery time, later admitting that he would be out until after the November international break.

“Max picked up an injury and we expect that he will not be ready before the international break. So he will be a few weeks out,” Alonso said before the win over Manchester United.

Reports have since suggested that Chelsea fear Lacroix, like James, may not play again until the New Year.

Jorrel Hato was a surprise absentee from the Chelsea squad that travelled to Liverpool in the Carabao Cup fourth round and was not available against Manchester United either.

Following the 2-0 win over the Red Devils, Alonso revealed that the Dutchman was battling a back injury.

“How long, we don't know, but he’s not available for tomorrow,” Alonso said. “He has a back problem and he's not feeling okay for tomorrow.”

Potential return date: Sunday November 8, vs Sunderland (A)

Jamie Gittens has yet to make a single Premier League appearance for Chelsea so far this season, with his only two outings to date coming against Luton and Leeds in the Carabao Cup.

The winger has been so unlucky with injuries since arriving in west London from Borussia Dortmund last summer, a trend which continued as he suffered an ankle problem while on international duty with England’s Under-21s last month and needed crutches.

Alonso’s last update confirmed that Gittens was still facing “weeks” on the sidelines, putting him on track to return at some point in November or perhaps even early December.

Potential return date: November or December

In Wednesday’s training session, there was also the rare sighting of forgotten £17million signing Aaron Anselmino.

The 21-year-old has not made a Chelsea senior matchday squad since the Carabao Cup second round win over Luton in August and he has been sidelined with an unspecified injury.

However, he has taken a big step on the road to recovery.

“He’s not available yet,” Alonso revealed last week. “He's had a few things, a few injuries and it still will take a few weeks until he's fully fit and we need to be cautious with him because he has had a few of them so he's still not there.”

Potential return date: November or December

#1787. Man United transfer news: Three strikers Red Devils could sign in January following Benjamin Sesko injury update

By Matt Law | 04 Nov 2026 16:53, Last updated: 04 Nov 2026 16:56

Manchester United could enter the January transfer window for a new striker, with Benjamin Sesko's ongoing shin problem a serious concern for the club.

Sesko is expected to be out until the start of 2027 with the shin injury that he initially suffered towards the end of the 2025-26 campaign.

Bryan Mbeumo is operating through for the middle for Man United at this moment in time, but the Cameroon international is better off the right.

Joshua Zirkzee is an option, but the Netherlands international continues to struggle to make his mark for the 20-time English champions.

Here, Sports Mole looks at three strikers who could be signed by Man United in January to hand themselves a major boost for the second half of the season.

Man United are currently being linked with a move for Calvert-Lewin, who has scored five goals in 11 appearances for Leeds during the 2026-27 campaign.

The 29-year-old made the move to Elland Road on a free transfer in the summer of 2025, and the striker has been impressive for Leeds, netting 20 times in 50 appearances for the club.

Calvert-Lewin is proven in the Premier League, scoring 75 times in 283 appearances in the competition, while he has also scored four times in 14 caps for England.

Man United would not have to break the bank to sign Calvert-Lewin, although it would not be a straightforward deal given the rivalry between the Red Devils and Leeds.

Calvert-Lewin scored against Man United in the Premier League earlier this season, and it is understood that the 20-time English champions are admirers of his talents.

Toney's future is again the subject of speculation, with the England international potentially a loan option for Man United at the start of 2027.

The 30-year-old has been in impressive form this season, scoring 14 goals and registering two assists in 15 appearances in all competitions for his Saudi club.

Toney made the move to Al-Ahli from Brentford in the summer of 2024, and his record for his current team stands at 86 goals and 19 assists in 108 appearances.

The forward scored 72 goals in 141 matches for Brentford, including a record of 36 goals in 83 games in the Premier League.

The Englishman is not a long-term option for Man United but could be an ideal short-term signing given that he is proven in the Premier League.

Toney might also feel that he has unfinished business in England's top flight.

Mateta's contract at Palace is due to expire at the end of the campaign, and there are currently no indications that he will be signing a fresh deal.

The 29-year-old has had a frustrating season to date due to injury, while he was sent off in Palace's last Premier League game against Tottenham Hotspur.

Mateta has scored 63 goals and registered 14 assists in 207 appearances for Palace in all competitions, including 50 goals and nine assists in 166 Premier League matches.

The Frenchman is seemingly looking for a way out at Palace and is said to be keen to explore a switch to the 20-time English champions next year.

A loan move for the striker is unlikely given his contract situation, but he could potentially be available for a bargain transfer fee in the winter market.

#1786. 'I told them': Scott Parker reveals team talk that sparked incredible West Ham comeback

New West Ham manager Scott Parker has revealed the half-time team talk that prompted a memorable turnaround away at Cardiff in his first match in charge.

The Hammers trailed 3-0 after only 39 minutes of their latest Championship clash in Wales on Wednesday night, which came just hours after Parker had been officially confirmed as the successor to the sacked Nuno Espirito Santo.

But Parker’s message at the interval hit home as West Ham staged an incredible recovery to snatch an unlikely 3-3 draw.

Goals either side of the hour mark from Divine Mukasa and Arne Engels were followed by Max Kilman’s 82nd-minute strike, cancelling out Jack Moylan’s first-half hat-trick and giving Parker his first point as Hammers boss.

“I came in here at nine o’clock this morning and met the players for the first time, so I didn’t have a lot of input as such,” he said afterwards.

“As you can imagine, it was a difficult half-time talk. I just helped them tactically and told them, ‘OK, this is the way it needs to be now’.

“Certainly out of possession, we needed to be more aggressive.

“There were tactical changes and substitutions, and we became more front-footed. We took a few more risks.”

It is not the first time that Parker’s half-time speeches have had the desired effect. Bournemouth previously released footage of Parker’s team talk when his former club were locked at 0-0 with automatic promotion rivals Nottingham Forest in the penultimate game of the 2021/22 Championship season.

Bournemouth went on to earn promotion with a 1-0 win via a late Kieffer Moore goal, while Parker has previous with motivating West Ham.

Former team-mate Carlton Cole labelled the midfielder as “inspirational” when he stood up to give a Hammers team talk as a player, with West Ham going from 3-0 down to draw 3-3 with West Brom.

Speaking about his side’s performance against Cardiff, Parker said: “The first half was poor in many aspects. We were very passive and slow with the ball.

“The biggest positive is the team we saw in the second half. That’s what the biggest learning was.

“These boys have come off two defeats. You come to Cardiff away and you’re three-nil down at half-time. I can only imagine what they were feeling.

“They showed a lot of character and that pleased me the most.”

Pre-season promotion favourites West Ham currently sit eighth in the Championship table after 14 games played, five points behind league leaders Middlesbrough.

#1784. ‘I leave with my head held high’ – Ronaldo confirms Portugal retirement

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Portugal icon Cristiano Ronaldo has announced his retirement from international football.

Ronaldo is the leading scorer and appearance-maker in the history of men's internationals, plundering 146 goals in 234 games since his Portugal debut in 2003.

He captained Portugal to their first-ever major trophy at Euro 2016, with Eder scoring the winning goal against hosts France in the final after he had gone off injured, while also lifting the Nations League trophy on two occasions, in 2019 and 2025.

Ronaldo considered retiring from Selecao duty after their round-of-16 exit at this year's World Cup, only to be talked into staying on by the FPF (Portuguese Football Federation).

However, Ronaldo then abruptly left their camp during the last international break, accusing new head coach Jorge Jesus of breaching his trust after he was left on the bench throughout a Nations League win over Norway.

Ronaldo, who also accused Jesus of failing to read a series of pre-agreed points regarding that decision to leave him on the bench, was subsequently given a 30-day suspension by the FPF on October 19.

With the Selecao facing Denmark and Wales in the Nations League on November 14 and 17, that would appear to mean there will be no farewell appearance for the five-time Ballon d'Or winner, who posted an emotional video statement on Instagram on Thursday.

Ronaldo said: "The time has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt of our national team.

A post shared by Cristiano Ronaldo (@cristiano)

"I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years, I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it, and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world. Today, the time has come for me to pass it on to the future.

"It was not an easy decision, because some decisions are not made with the mind alone, they are also made with the heart. A journey that started in August 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end.

"I made mistakes, I suffered, there were times where I could not give the Portuguese people what they so desperately wanted. But I never gave up, and above all, I never stopped feeling proud to represent Portugal.

"If I ever made you happy, if one of my goals made you embrace someone or feel proud of our country, then it was all worth it.

"I leave with my head held high, proud of the path I have taken and knowing I gave everything I had for Portugal. I will never stop being one of you.

"I spent my life working to become the best player in the world. Today, I learn that my greatest achievement was earning the honour of representing the best country in the world."

10 – Cristiano Ronaldo is the only to have scored at least 10 goals at both the FIFA World Cup (11) and UEFA European Championship finals (14). Perfect. https://t.co/HPOUYCOfEv

Ronaldo retires as the only player to have scored at least 10 goals at both the World Cup (11) and the European Championships (14), with the latter figure being a competition record.

He became the first player to score at six different editions of the World Cup this year, when he helped himself to a brace in a group-stage win over Uzbekistan, while he is also the oldest player to feature in a World Cup knockout-stage match, at the age of 41.

However, none of Ronaldo's World Cup goals came in the knockout stages, and he was also memorably dropped by Fernando Santos during the 2022 edition, which was won by his great rival Lionel Messi and Argentina.

Ronaldo's international retirement comes less than a month after Messi made his final appearance for the Albiceleste, bowing out during a 3-0 win over Benin.

Tottenham concluded their tour Down Under with a 2-1 victory over London rivals Chelsea at Accor Stadium in Sydney.

Sandro Tonali put Tottenham in front with a deflected effort before Estêvão equalised for Chelsea minutes later. Tottenham’s cause was not helped by a red card for Austrian defender Kevin Danso, who lasted just three minutes after coming on at half-time.

After making a mistake, Danso brought João Pedro down and was given his marching orders for denying a clear goal-scoring opportunity. Chelsea came close to taking the lead with their one-man advantage only for Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky to make some crucial saves.Just as the game appeared to be heading to penalties, Richarlison scored on the follow-up after Jamie Donley hit the post in the final few seconds of added time.

Tottenham will take on Getafe and Hoffenheim back on home soil before taking on Brentford on the opening weekend of the new Premier League season.

Delap is found in the centre of the Tottenham box with a cross from the right but the striker’s header from around the penalty spot goes wide and does not really trouble the target.

Kinsky makes another big save to deny Chelsea. Tonali, who thought he had been fouled, loses the ball deep inside his own half, before Estevao has a great chance to put Chelsea in front from inside the Tottenham penalty area but Kinsky makes the save. It would have been a touch soft to give a free-kick to Tottenham but in the Premier League you suspect Tonali would have been awarded a free-kick there.

Tottenham are going to make a change at the back in light of Danso’s red card. Hardy is going to come on for Gallagher, who is booed by some of the Chelsea fans inside Accor Stadium. The England Under-18 international Hardy has come on at right centre-back in place of Danso.

Chelsea hit the frame of the goal. Pedro cuts it back from the byline to the penalty spot. Estevao gets to it first and his shot takes a deflection off Robertson. Kinsky makes a brilliant reflex save to push it onto the bar before Colwill blazes over.

Roberto de Zerbi is slumped in his seat distinctly unimpressed, shaking his head in frustration and perhaps disgust.

Palmer takes the free-kick but his effort is always curling wide of the far post.

Danso makes an absolute mess of a pass back to him from Gray and lets the ball run past him. Pedro gets around him and looks destined to drive towards the Tottenham penalty area but is brought down. Danso is shown a red card as Davies was probably not going to get across in time and it was the denial of a goal-scoring opportunity. Why do that in a pre-season friendly? Stupid.

That was a decent opportunity for Tottenham. Tel finds the underlapping Davies with a pass towards the byline and the latter plays it across the six-yard box but Solanke was not there to meet it. Had Solanke read that, it would have been a simple tap-in.

Tel comes close to putting Tottenham back in front. It would have been a great solo goal as he drives inside from the left wing and moves into the Chelsea penalty area. He gets the better of Essugo on the corner of the six-yard box but is denied by a decent save from Sharman-Lowe.

Pedro has a chance to put Chelsea in front but his effort goes wide. Chelsea steal possession inside the Tottenham half after a poor pass from Robertson and the ball is then played forward to Pedro, who shoots from just inside the Tottenham box but his effort goes wide of the far post. Davies did just enough to put Pedro off.

Tottenham have two penalty appeals in quick succession turned down. First was for a potential handball by Essugo and then a push by Palestra on Tel. The handball would have been very harsh and the second incident was never a foul on Tel, who was losing his balance anyway.

Chelsea gift possession away deep inside their own half and Tel’s eyes light up. The ball rolls across to the Frenchman in a central position just outside the box and he opens up his body, trying to curl one into the top corner, but gets his first-time effort all wrong and his shot misses the target by a mile.

Like London buses, two goals come in quick succession and Chelsea are back on level terms. Chelsea counter from deep inside their own half and the ball ends up with Gittens on the left. From the corner of the box, he crosses towards the far post. It takes a touch off a Tottenham defender and ends up at the back post where Estevao, one of the smallest men on the pitch, beats Robertson and heads into the opposite corner.

Tottenham take the lead in Sydney courtesy of £100m signing Tonali. Solomon lays it back to Tonali who, from just outside the box, hits it first time and his shot takes a big deflection off Colwill, taking it into the far corner and giving Sharman-Lowe in the Chelsea goal no chance. That was probably Tottenham’s first proper foray forward in the game.

It has been a pretty stop-start game as play continues to be halted by fouls. The two managers might enjoy seeing the passion of their teams but they will also want to see their sides actually play, which is quite difficult when fouls are being committed left, right and centre.

Van Hecke has already fouled his former teammate Pedro once and he bundles into him again. Van Hecke has a wry smile as he walks away and Pedro tells the referee that is now twice he has been fouled by Van Hecke. I think it is a fairly safe assumption that Van Hecke and Pedro do not like each other that much!

We are not even 10 minutes into this friendly but there is absolutely no love lost between these two sides and the challenges are flying in. Former Chelsea man Gallagher slides in on Essugo, which infuriates the Chelsea players. The referee takes his time to make his decision as both sides come to blows before giving out the first booking of the game to Gallagher.

Pedro is caught by Van Hecke out on Chelsea left and the latter is absolutely furious with that decision, believing he got the ball. However, replays show that he did not get the ball and a free-kick was the right decision. Those two were teammates at Brighton and supposedly were involved in a training ground altercation just over a year ago!

The free-kick is whipped in towards the back post and the last touch is deemed to have come off Chelsea, much to their chagrin.

Lavia catches Tonali late and eventually the referee blows his whistle to bring play back for the free-kick. In a Premier League game, that may well have been a booking for Lavia. It might be a pre-season game but there will be no love lost between these bitter rivals.

The pitch in Sydney is on the bobbly side, which will make slick passing more challenging, dare I say it probably not really possible or realistic.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel, with Tottenham led out by Archie Gray and Chelsea by Levi Colwill. There is a lights show inside Accor Stadium as the teams making their way onto the pitch.

Here is all the latest Liverpool injury news and return dates.

Dutch midfielder Gravenberch has had an injury-hit campaign so far this term.

He missed out on the travelling squad to Turkey as a result of a fracture in his heel, with Iraola providing an update ahead of the trip to the Chobani Stadium.

“I don’t know, it’s a day-to-day thing,” he said.

Potential return date: Sunday November 8, vs Crystal Palace (A)

Frimpong picked up a muscle injury playing against Brentford last month, in another lay-off for the full-back since his arrival from Bayer Leverkusen.

The attack-minded right-back is not expected to be back until after the upcoming international break, meaning he will have missed six matches in a row.

On the Dutch international, Iraola said: “Jeremie Frimpong is obviously a new muscle injury and it happened, I think, in the second or third minute he was playing, difficult to predict and we will have to wait until he recovers.

“But it’s going to be difficult, I think, before the [November international] break. We will try but it’s going to be difficult to have him.”

Potential return date: Sunday November 22, vs Manchester United (H)

Leoni signed for Liverpool from Parma last summer in a deal worth around £26million, but a serious knee injury means he has been limited to just one senior appearance so far.

The centre-back made his debut in the Carabao Cup against Southampton in September, but he was stretchered off and it was later confirmed that he had suffered an anterior cruciate ligament tear.

He was expected to miss a full year of action, which has proved to be the case.

He had hoped to have made his comeback for the recent September international break, but that has since been delayed.

“It’s taking more time than we wanted,” Iraola said. “The planning was to train with the team in this past international break [but] probably it’s going to be in the next international break, so we’ve lost one month in the process.

“Giovanni’s injury, I wasn’t here but talking to the medical department, it was not just an ACL – it was a bad injury, a lot of things around the knee were involved apart from the ACL.”

Ekitike has not played since rupturing his Achilles against Paris Saint-Germain in April.

The Frenchman was forced to sit out the end of last season and the World Cup, where it was estimated that he would be out for nine months to a full year.

He was included in Iraola’s squad for the Champions League league phase - which came as a surprise to many - with the hope that he could potentially return for the final two games in January, against Inter Milan and Lens.

The striker is thought to be targeting a comeback before the turn of the year.

Right-back Bradley is another long-term absentee for Liverpool, having suffered a serious knee injury at Arsenal back in January.

The Northern Ireland international suffered bone and ligament damage in that match, which has kept him out for almost a year.

Iraola’s latest comments were positive, indicating that Bradley will soon return to full training.

“[He is] doing very well,” Iraola said. “I think [he is] in a good place. Conor is not so far from training with the group – not like full training but doing some things with the group.

“I think Conor is not very far from starting doing things with us."

It looks as though he could rejoin team training during the November international break.

Potential return date: Wednesday, December 2 vs Sunderland (H)

Bournemouth will continue their maiden European campaign in Thursday's meeting with Sparta Prague in the Europa League league phase.

The Cherries are sitting in third place in the Europa League standings, while the hosts start matchday four in 16th position.

Here, Sports Mole provides all the key details about how to tune into the European fixture.

The game will get underway at 18:45pm local time on Thursday, which will be a 17:45 kick-off for UK viewers.

Bournemouth will travel to Stadion Letna, which can hold over 18,000 spectators.

Sparta have won six of their nine competitive home matches this season (D1, L2), although they have failed to win two of their last three games in front of their supporters.

UK viewers with the required subscription can watch the game on TNT Sports 2.

Alternatively, you can catch the game on the HBO Max website and app with a TNT Sports subscription. The HBO Max app is available on a wide range of devices, including phones, tablets, smart TVs and game consoles.

There will be match highlights available on the HBO Max website and app, as well as the TNT Sports Football YouTube channel.

The @footballontnt X account will also share key moments from Thursday's contest.

After featuring in the Conference League last 16 last term, Sparta are aiming to make it back-to-back European knockout appearances in this season's Europa League.

Brian Priske's side are currently sitting in a seeded spot for the knockout round playoffs, with three points separating them from the top eight and a one-point gap to the teams sitting just outside the top 24.

In regard to their overall form, Sparta will be looking to spark an upturn in fortunes after winning just one of their last six competitive matches.

In contrast to their hosts, Bournemouth carry significant momentum into the midweek fixture after winning each of their last six competitive matches without conceding, including a 2-0 Premier League win over Leeds United on Saturday.

Marco Rose's side are looking to maintain their 100% Europa League record after starting their European campaign with three successive wins over Real Sociedad, Sturm Graz and AC Milan.

Another win on Thursday would further strengthen their hopes of a top-eight finish and an automatic last-16 spot.

#1780. Manchester United co-owners INEOS sack manager as official statement released

INEOS have sacked Lausanne-Sport manager Luka Elsner after just five months at the helm, amid ongoing pressure on Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick.

The Swiss club, which is part-owned by Sir Jim Ratcliffe's INEOS group, confirmed on Tuesday that they had mutually agreed to end their relationship with the 44-year-old.

Elsner was appointed on 1 June but struggled to make an impact, winning eight of his 12 Swiss Super League matches. Lausanne's poor start to the campaign left them bottom of the table, prompting the club to make a change.

A statement read: “After lengthy discussions about the current sporting situation, FC Lausanne-Sport and Luka Elsner have mutually agreed to end their collaboration.”

His departure comes at a difficult time for INEOS at Manchester United, where Carrick is facing scrutiny following a disappointing run of results.

United's supporters have made their frustration with the club's ownership clear in recent weeks, directing criticism towards Ratcliffe and the Glazer family.

Protests continued during Tuesday's Champions League meeting with Roma, when fans threw green and gold balloons on to the pitch in the 21st minute while chanting against the owners.

The atmosphere improved after United produced a second-half comeback to secure a 3-2 victory. Bruno Fernandes scored from the penalty spot before Matheus Cunha struck twice to complete the turnaround.

However, the result is unlikely to remove the pressure on Carrick, who remains under scrutiny as United attempt to improve their domestic form.

The decision to part company with Elsner after such a short period is also likely to attract attention given INEOS' involvement in both clubs.

#1778. JJ Gabriel future: Man United's stance 'revealed' amid reports of Real Madrid 'agreement'

By Matt Law | 04 Nov 2026 17:12, Last updated: 04 Nov 2026 17:15

Manchester United are reportedly in the dark when it comes to JJ Gabriel's future despite reports that the attacker has agreed a move to Real Madrid.

Widely regarded as one of the best teenagers in world football, JJ Gabriel stunned Man United in September when he told the club that he wanted to leave.

JJ Gabriel made his senior debut for Man United in their pre-season game against Atletico Madrid during the summer, but he is yet to feature for the first team in a competitive match and is now set to leave the 20-time English champions.

The 16-year-old had been due to sign scholarship terms with the Red Devils last month, with a professional contract then expected to follow a year later.

However, JJ Gabriel's representatives told Man United in September that the attacker would not be signing a new contract and wanted to leave.

According to Sky Sports News, Real Madrid have reached a verbal agreement with JJ Gabriel over a move to Bernabeu in January.

JJ Gabriel has a European passport through both of his parents, and a FIFA loophole could see him join Real Madrid in January despite having a deal with Man United's academy until the end of the campaign.

The attacker is currently in Spain maintaining his fitness, and Barcelona have also been heavily linked with a player regarded as one of the best teenagers in world football.

However, various reports have claimed that Real Madrid are closing in on a move.

According to the Manchester Evening News, Man United have had no contact from JJ Gabriel's representatives nor Real Madrid despite the reports.

Man United still hold JJ Gabriel's registration, but the teenager has not been at Carrington since scoring a hat-trick against Sabah in the UEFA Youth League at the start of September.

JJ Gabriel boasts a record of 29 goals and four assists in 32 appearances for Man United Under-18s. while he has scored twice and registered two assists in two appearances for Man United Under-21s in the Premier League 2.

Man United had allegedly initially been hopeful of keeping JJ Gabriel but have since admitted defeat in what is a major blow for the 20-time English champions.

#1776. GdS: Milan score, Ramos struggles – the paradox that Amorim must fix

As the weeks go by Ruben Amorim continues to tweak AC Milan tactically, but a constant theme remains: Goncalo Ramos can’t score consistently.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, Milan are evolving on an almost game-by-game basis, but the only one who remains the same is Ramos. One factor stands out above all: the Portuguese fails to get into the flow of play, not only when the team is struggling but even when they play well and win.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

His derby stats tragically mirror those reported the previous Wednesday against Bologna: zero shots on target, zero shots off target, zero blocked shots, zero chances created, zero assists. The same story. Even the number of balls played was identical: 31.

Yet they were two very different games. Against Inter, Gonçalo even infuriated Luka Modric, who shortly after the quarter-hour mark unleashed a sharp, angled right-footer that was aimed squarely at Josep Martinez. Ramos was right in the path of the ball, potentially denying a 3-0 goal.

Modric muttered words of frustration under his breath, knowing of course that it was not deliberate sabotage. That incident is proof that there are times when nothing goes right, not even when everyone else is playing with a smile.

Ramos’s first two months resemble Gimenez’s a year ago: just as Santiago couldn’t score but had Massimiliano Allegri’s trust thanks to his backroom work for the team, the same is true for Gonçalo. Unlike Santiago, he has scored three goals, though one was a penalty and one a gift.

In terms of goalscoring, his contribution is completely inadequate compared to expectations, the player’s level, and the club’s investment in bringing him to Milanello. Ramos runs, he battles and he tries to get the team moving forward but he can’t get fully involved.

You can also look at it from the other angle: is it the team that are incapable of giving him service? Perhaps precisely because he’s a striker who roams widely and provides no reference points not only for opposing defenders, but also for his own team-mates.

In any case, he was and remains the starting centre-forward. Partly because Francesco Camarda – in Amorim’s eyes – clearly doesn’t offer enough guarantees, and partly because of Gonçalo’s dirty work, which serves to free up space for others.

It’s no coincidence that Adrien Rabiot is frequently finding the back of the net, and the same goes for Diego Moreira and Alphadjo Cisse, all players who don’t usually hang around in the box.

Furthermore, Milan have recently developed a particular quality: when their shots hit the target, they end up in the back of the net. The two goals against Bologna came with their first two shots, the three against Inter with their first three.

Between the Emilians and the Nerazzurri, Milan have had a total of seven shots on target, squeezing five goals from them: a stratospheric 71%. The million-dollar question, now that Milan are poised for the Scudetto race, is: if Ramos were to unlock himself, how far can this team go?

#1775. Cristiano Ronaldo makes bombshell retirement decision after stunning Portugal suspension

Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international duty with Portugal.

The country’s greatest ever player announced his decision via a video to camera on his social media channels.

Ronaldo scored 146 goals in 234 games for Portugal, becoming the all-time leading scorer in the history of men’s international football.

Between 2003 and 2026, a storied international career delivered three trophies: the European Championship title in France in 2016 and two UEFA Nations League titles, in 2019 and 2025.

Ronaldo said in his social media address that the “time had come” to hand back the No7 shirt but that he had “never felt it belonged to me alone”.

The 41-year-old considered retiring after this summer’s World Cup but was persuaded to stay on by Portuguese FA president Pedro Proenca, a former UEFA referee.

#1774. Cristiano Ronaldo statement in full after stunning retirement decision

Cristiano Ronaldo confirmed that he would retire from international football in a shock announcement on Tuesday.

The 41-year-old calls time on his illustrious 23-year career playing for his country, where he scored 146 goals in 234 games, becoming the all-time leading scorer in the history of men’s international football.

He lifted the European Championships in 2016, and he also won two Nations League titles in 2019 and 2025.

At last summer’s World Cup, the striker could not stop his side crashing out in the last 16 against Spain, when Mikel Merino netted a last-minute winner.

Now, the curtain has come down on his international journey, just weeks after his historic rival Lionel Messi did the same with Argentina.

He had been suspended by the Portuguese FA last month for 30 days, as well as receiving a £215 fine, after storming out of the Nations League camp having fallen out with manager Jorge Jesus.

In an emotional five-minute video posted to his social media channels, Ronaldo addressed the Portuguese people.

"To the Portuguese people, the day has come to hand back the shirt and the captain's armband of the national team that belongs to all of us,” he began.

"I never felt that it was exclusively mine, but for 23 years, I had the privilege and responsibility of wearing it, defending it, and carrying it with me to stadiums all around the world.

"Today, the moment has come to pass it on to the future.

"It was not an easy decision, because some decisions are not made with the head alone. They are also made with the heart.

"I am bringing to an end a journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever.

"When I look back and think about everything I experienced with the national team, I don't just see matches, goals, records, or trophies. I see people.

"I see immigrants who, for 90 minutes, felt a little closer to Portugal. I see millions of Portuguese people whom I never met personally, but who became part of my life.

"Because, at the end of the day, football is much bigger than a game. Football is about people.

"Throughout my entire career with the national team, I always tried to push beyond my limits. I wanted to win, I wanted to be the best, I wanted to make history.

"I was always demanding of myself. I always wanted more. I always believed we could go further, and I gave everything I had for this shirt.

"There were perfect afternoons and nights. There were victories I will never forget. There were defeats that still hurt to remember today.

"I also failed. I also suffered. There were moments when I couldn't give the Portuguese people what they wanted so badly. But I never gave up.

"And above all, I never stopped feeling proud to represent Portugal.

"Over these years, I learned some very simple things: goals come and go, trophies end up in museums, records are eventually broken, but there is something that time can never erase.

"If I ever made you happy, if one of my goals ever made you hug someone, forget a worry, or feel proud of our country, then it was all worth it.

"Because being Portuguese is also about that.

"We suffer together. We get back up together. We believe again.

"Portugal will always need young people who dream, players who never give up, and new generations who believe it is possible to reach places no one has reached before.

"Because a country that continues to create new heroes is a country that never stops believing in itself.

"To my national team teammates, I want to leave a special message.

"Thank you for every run, every hug, every argument, every moment of silence before stepping onto the pitch, every victory we celebrated together, and every defeat that made us stronger.

"I had the privilege of being your captain, but no captain walks alone, and you are all part of my story.

"To all the coaches, directors, doctors, physiotherapists, kit managers, staff members, and the many people who worked with me throughout these years, thank you.

"Many of you never appeared in the photographs, but without you, none of those photographs would have been possible.

"To my family, thank you for sharing this dream with me.

"Thank you for understanding the absences, the sacrifices, and the moments when the national team had to take up a space that also belonged to you.

"If I made it this far, it was because we always walked hand in hand.

"And to the Portuguese people, to every Portuguese person around the world, I want to tell you one last thing.

"There is an image that I will always carry with me.

"A moment when the national anthem begins.

"I look around me. I see my teammates. I see the stands.

"I see children, mothers, fathers, and grandparents. I see Portuguese people who travelled from so far away just to be there.

"And during those moments, we stop being different.

"There are no clubs. There are no colours. There are no classes. There are no professions. There are no opinions.

"That is the feeling I will carry with me for the rest of my life.

"Today, my journey on the pitch with the national team comes to an end.

"I leave with my head held high, proud of the journey I have taken and knowing that I gave everything I had for Portugal.

"I will continue to suffer, to feel the excitement, and to celebrate every Portuguese victory, just as I always have.

"I spent my life working to become the best player in the world.

"Today, I realise that my greatest victory was earning the honour of representing the best country in the world.

"Thank you for allowing me to live a dream that began when I was just a little boy in Madeira, running after a ball.

"The number 7 shirt remains, but the pride of having worn it will be mine forever.

"Portugal will always be a part of me. Forever."

#1773. Bruno Fernandes admits Michael Carrick was right to drop him

By Naim Beneddra | 04 Nov 2026 17:54

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has admitted that Michael Carrick was justified in dropping him from the starting lineup, while denying reports of a breakdown in his relationship with the under-pressure manager.

The Portugal international made the surprising admission following United's dramatic 3-2 Champions League victory over Roma on Tuesday, which ended a nine-match winless run and provided some much-needed relief at Old Trafford.

Fernandes had been left on the bench for last month's Premier League defeat to Bournemouth, just days after publicly questioning the team's tactical approach following a humiliating 4-1 loss to Como.

His comments prompted speculation that Carrick had punished his captain for speaking out, although the United boss maintained that the decision had been made for footballing reasons.

Now, Fernandes has acknowledged that his own performances warranted the decision, while insisting that the controversy had not affected his confidence in the former England midfielder.

"Carrick was right" ?? Bruno Fernandes gave an open, honest assessment after United's 3-2 win over Roma ?️ https://t.co/QAWDt6VXQr

Speaking to Amazon Prime Video after the Roma victory, Fernandes addressed the circumstances surrounding his absence from the starting lineup against Bournemouth.

The 32-year-old revealed that he understood why Carrick had decided to make a change, even though the timing had led to suggestions of a disciplinary response.

"The manager took a decision of putting me on the bench because I wasn't performing," Fernandes admitted.

"Everyone felt that was a punishment for the words that I had. If it was, it was right."

Those comments represent a notable change in tone from the midfielder, whose public criticism after the Como defeat had intensified scrutiny of Carrick's management.

Fernandes had questioned United's decision not to press their opponents man-to-man and suggested that the players needed to show greater bravery under pressure.

Four days later, he was named among the substitutes for the 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth, marking the first time Carrick had dropped him from a Premier League starting lineup.

At the time, the manager insisted that his decision to leave Fernandes out was based purely on footballing considerations.

The captain's latest explanation supports that assessment, although he stopped short of confirming whether his earlier comments had influenced Carrick's thinking.

Fernandes also challenged reports suggesting that he and the manager had needed to resolve a personal disagreement behind the scenes.

He described some of the speculation surrounding their relationship as "lies", rejecting claims that the pair had held talks to clear the air following his controversial interview.

The midfielder was equally clear that being dropped had not diminished his commitment to Carrick or the club.

"It doesn't change the belief I have in the manager," Fernandes insisted, adding that he retained the same confidence in the coaching staff and his teammates.

His response is significant given the uncertainty surrounding Carrick's position and the questions that have been raised about the mood within United's dressing room.

Rather than portraying his omission as an injustice, Fernandes has publicly accepted responsibility for his performances and acknowledged the manager's authority to make difficult selection decisions.

Fernandes also responded to suggestions that United's remarkable recovery against Roma might have saved Carrick from dismissal.

The Red Devils had entered Tuesday's encounter without a victory in nine matches across all competitions, having slipped to 17th in the Premier League.

Their situation appeared to deteriorate further when Matias Soule and Donyell Malen gave Roma a two-goal advantage in the opening stages at Old Trafford.

However, Fernandes converted a retaken penalty in the second half before Matheus Cunha scored twice late on to complete the comeback.

Asked afterwards whether the players had rescued their manager's job, the United captain rejected that interpretation.

"We don't need to save anyone's job," Fernandes declared.

He explained that the victory had been necessary for the entire club after a prolonged period of poor results, rather than solely for Carrick's personal circumstances.

The Portuguese also acknowledged the frustration felt by supporters, who have watched United struggle to reproduce the standards associated with the club's most successful years.

Carrick adopted a similarly measured approach in his post-match comments, describing the victory as an important moment for the club without suggesting that one result had resolved its problems.

United's next test comes against Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday, November 8, when they will attempt to secure consecutive victories for the first time in several weeks.

Fernandes has already returned to Carrick's starting lineup, featuring against Chelsea before playing a decisive role in the European comeback.

His latest comments may help dispel some of the speculation surrounding his relationship with the manager. Whether United can build on Tuesday's result will provide a more meaningful indication of Carrick's prospects of remaining in charge.

#1772. Liam Rosenior speaks out on Chelsea struggles in new interview: 'I'm not a joke'

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Liam Rosenior has declared his 107-day tenure at Chelsea as “the best and hardest experience of my life” but hit back at how he was perceived “in a country where tolerance is an important value”.

After an impressive spell in charge at BlueCo sister club Strasbourg, Rosenior was hired as Chelsea’s permanent replacement for Enzo Maresca in January.

However, he lasted only four months and was sacked in April after Chelsea lost five consecutive league games in a row without scoring for the first time since 1912.

During his time at the helm, Rosenior received criticism for his approach from a number of pundits and columnists as well as on social media.

Chelsea fans were initially split on his appointment and support for him dwindled further as results began to take a turn for the worse.

Now, in an interview with French outlet So Foot, Rosenior has spoken about his time in charge at Stamford Bridge at length for the first time since his sacking, having returned to France and begun thriving in a new role at high-flying Paris FC.

“It was the best experience of my life, and the hardest too,” Rosenior said of the Chelsea job, per Sport Witness. “It was fantastic, even though it only lasted four months.

“I don’t want to go into details now; I’ll talk about it one day, when the time is right. But in a country where tolerance is an important value, what happened there has nothing to do with football.”

He added: “The moment that worried me the most was at the beginning, when we went through that five-game winning streak. Any club would have been happy with such a run, but not Chelsea.

“You get good results and you’re in the spotlight. Then, there was a kind of snowball effect in the media.

Manchester United will not hire another interim manager should Michael Carrick be sacked.

That is according to Sky Sports, who report that there is a contingency plan in place should the under-fire head coach be relieved of his duties.

Carrick has faced serious scrutiny in the last few weeks after a poor run of results led to a nine-game winless streak.

That was ended on Tuesday in dramatic fashion as the Red Devils roared back from 2-0 down to defeat Roma in a 3-2 victory at Old Trafford.

The former midfielder had been on the brink of the sack following a heavy week of defeats by Como and Bournemouth a fortnight ago, but he was retained in-post for the trip to Chelsea, which United also lost.

Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe and Antonio Conte have all been linked with replacing Carrick in the hotseat at Old Trafford, but it is believed that the former United man still has supporters within the club boardroom.

#1770. Kovac did not want to take ‘risk’ with Guirassy injury

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Niko Kovac has revealed Serhou Guirassy's substitution against Real Betis was to avoid risks after the Borussia Dortmund striker felt discomfort in his thigh.

Dortmund made it back-to-back wins in the Champions League with Wednesday's 2-1 victory over Betis, with Fabio Silva and Konstantinos Karetsas netting either side of Aitor Ruibal’s equaliser.

But Dortmund were dealt a blow just 34 minutes in when Guirassy had to go off the field, though it was match-winner Karetsas who came on in his place.

Before the match against Betis, Guirassy had been Dortmund’s only goalscorer in the Champions League (four goals), while his eight goals in all competitions this term are a team-high.

"He says he feels his thigh," Kovac told DAZN when asked about Guirassy's injury.

"Now we have to see if it's more than a strain, which I don't think it is. But still, it didn't go any further, and we didn't want to take risks.

"If he's not available against Elversberg, we hope he'll be back after the break."

— Borussia Dortmund (@BlackYellow) November 4, 2026

Guirassy’s absence could now open the door for 18-year-old Karetsas to start in the Bundesliga this weekend, after he made Champions League history for the club.

He is the youngest Dortmund player to score a winning goal in the Champions League (18 years 350 days), beating Jude Bellingham’s record from October 2022 against Sevilla (19y 98d).

Kovac was particularly impressed, even after he had to search for Karetsas before bringing him on, due to the substitute making a trip to the toilet.

"You could see that Kostas is a really good footballer," Kovac added. "It's difficult to defend [against] him; he has a lot of good step-overs. He brought a lot of momentum, and I thought he and Fabio harmonised very well. I liked that.

"He will probably play from the start in the next few games as long as Serhou is not there. I'm glad, after a difficult time for him, that he gained such a good foothold in the game.

"I'm sure there's still room for improvement, but at 18 he's okay – if he performs like that up front, then I can turn a blind eye at the back.

"I was looking for him! I thought about going in – suddenly he wasn't there. Then I called Carney [Chukwuemeka] and 'poof', he came around the corner. So, he would still have been sitting on the toilet if he hadn't come in!"

Dortmund have now won each of their last five games against Spanish sides in the Champions League (all since April 2025), which is as many wins as they managed in their previous 21 games against LaLiga opposition in the competition (five).

They have also only lost two of their last 25 home outings in the competition (W16 D7), while averaging over two goals per match in this run (2.16 – 54 in 25 games).

TEAMtalk cite reports claiming that Chelsea are compiling weekly scouting reports on the 19-year-old, who continues to go from strength to strength at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Chelsea are widely expected to swoop for another top young midfielder in January in Bournemouth’s Alex Scott, 23.

Harry Kane’s bumper new Bayern Munich contract has now been confirmed.

The Ballon d’Or winner has been in talks with the reigning Bundesliga champions for months now regarding a lucrative extension to his previous deal that was due to expire next summer.

Kane is now tied to Bayern until 2029 on a record-breaking contract that is said to make him the highest-paid player in Europe by salary.

The England captain will be 36 by the time it expires, meaning he may well now never return to the Premier League and looks destined to stay second on the list of all-time top scorers behind Alan Shearer.

Manchester United looks set to make a sensational loan swoop for Ivan Toney in January, reports claim.

The struggling Red Devils are desperate for more firepower under Michael Carrick with first-choice striker Benjamin Sesko out until January with his lingering shin injury.

According to Football Insider, United want England star Toney, who now plays his football in Saudi Arabia with Al-Ahli.

They are more likely to make a loan move for the former Brentford frontman than a permanent offer, however.

Arsenal could be lining up a shock move for an Atletico Madrid star that ISN’T Julian Alvarez.

The Gunners chased a high-profile deal for the Argentine striker throughout the closing stages of a hectic summer transfer window and are understood to have retained their interest in his services.

However, it seems that one of Alvarez’s team-mates at the Metropolitano Stadium has now caught Mikel Arteta’s eye.

According to TEAMtalk, Arsenal are keeping close tabs on highly-rated Spain midfielder Alex Baena, though could face serious competition for his signing.

Tottenham goalkeeper Luca Gunter will assess his loan options in January after being recalled from Boreham Wood last month, writes Sam Tabuteau.

Gunter joined the runaway National League leaders over the summer and immediately secured his spot as their first-choice option, but has returned to Spurs to train with the first team following an injury to third-choice goalkeeper Brandon Austin.

Standard Sport understands that Gunter will continue to be around first-team training before looking to go back out on loan when the January transfer window opens.

Gunter is one of several academy talents at Tottenham who are assessing their options ahead of the January window, with Tyrese Hall expected to have both loan and permanent offers on the table.

Under-21s captain James Rowswell is another player who will be potentially looking to leave Spurs on loan in the New Year, having failed to secure a summer switch.

Celta Vigo defender Javi Rodriguez is attracting interest from a number of clubs across Europe, writes Sam Tabuteau.

Despite reports, though, there has not yet been any contact from Fulham for the 23-year-old.

Rodriguez made his Spain debut in June and is expected to attract interest in January.

Real Madrid are confident of winning the race to sign Manchester United teenager JJ Gabriel, who has not returned to Old Trafford since leaving the club in September.

The 16-year-old is currently training independently in Spain after deciding to pursue a pathway towards senior football elsewhere.

Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain have also shown interest, but Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid are considered the leading contenders, according to BBC Sport.

Gabriel has impressed at youth level, scoring a hat-trick on his UEFA Youth League debut, and has obtained an EU passport that could ease a move abroad.

United would receive compensation if he leaves, although the fee would be lower for an overseas transfer.
