#1768. “Where the problems arise” – Vitiello reveals the ‘truth’ that Milan’s derby win exposed

Antonio Vitiello believes that the derby win over Inter offered one very clear lesson regarding AC Milan’s current status.

The mood around Milan has been buoyed by a fourth straight victory against the city rivals, one that was very much needed after the 4-2 loss to Bologna on Wednesday night that featured a second-half collapse.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Three goals in the first half from Christian Pulisic, Adrien Rabiot and Diego Moreira demonstrated the potential of this team when everyone is healthy. However, the issue has been when Ruben Amorim has not had all his key men out there.

Vitiello published his weekly column for MilanNews and he chose to focus on the major takeaway from the derby, which was the display of the potential of this team, in contrast to the limitations shown a few nights prior against Bologna.

“The tradition continues. AC Milan have dominated recent derbies and confirmed this in their recent 3-1 victory over the Nerazzurri, demonstrating their much better management of the Milanese derby,” he began.

“The atmosphere is galvanised by the victory, and the San Siro match revealed an unquestionable verdict. When Milan field their first team, it’s a completely different story. The Rossoneri with their best players are truly fearsome.

“When Moreira, Rabiot, Modric, Pulisic, Maignan, and company play together, the other teams have to worry. However, this isn’t always possible due to a tight schedule that forces coaches to change line-ups when there are games every three days.

“It’s literally impossible to consistently field the same team, also to avoid injuries. But that’s where the problems arise. In the long run, the teams with deeper squads, those who don’t suffer too many fluctuations when switching from starters to second string players, prevail. And the derby reaffirmed this truth.

“So, to be truly competitive, the team must improve in the next two transfer windows. First in January, with at least a couple of valuable additions, even spending significant sums. And then next summer, with the second batch of strong players. The next moves are already planned.

“Milan will soon announce their new manager, Markus Krosche, who will oversee the transfer market and in January will focus on a central defender, while also evaluating a winger and a striker. Three players to raise the bar after the summer transfer window ended with some shortcomings. An incomplete transfer window to compete on three fronts simultaneously.

“But this time Gerry Cardinale has chosen to take a risk. He said so himself in a recent interview with ClassCNBC. ‘The decision to finish in the red this summer was my own, made the day after we were eliminated from the Champions League. Looking at how things had gone over the last four years, I realized it was time for a real change,’ said Gerry Cardinale.

“Compared to previous years, when the club prioritized a profitable budget, this time the decision was to finish in the red. The summer expenses, and those expected in the January transfer window, will lead the club to invest in players to strengthen the squad.

“The goal is to return to the Champions League after two years of absence. And there’s no room for error.”

#1767. Famalicao vs Arouca - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 04 Nov 2026 18:51

Seaching for their first home victory this season, Famalicao welcome an in-form Arouca side to the Estadio Municipal 22 de Junho on Friday night.

The hosts sit 11th in the Primeira Liga table, three points above the relegation zone, while the visitors occupy fifth place, ahead of sixth-placed Academico de Viseu on goal difference.

Famalicao have struggled to reproduce the form that earned them a club-best fifth-place finish last season, with the departures of former boss Hugo Oliveira, Ibrahima Ba and Gustavo Sa contributing to a difficult start to the new campaign.

Carlos Carvalhal, who took over in the summer, was dismissed in October following a shock Taca de Portugal defeat to third-tier Paredes, leaving 46-year-old assistant coach Ricardo Silva in charge on an interim basis.

Although Silva made an impressive start, securing a 4-0 away victory over Rio Ave before edging Braga on penalties in the Taca da Liga quarter-finals, the Vila Nova outfit were brought back down to earth by the same Minho rivals at the weekend, suffering a 3-0 league defeat.

That result leaves Famalicao with just two wins from their opening 10 Primeira Liga fixtures this season (D4, L4), while they have scored 14 goals and conceded the same number, highlighting the need for greater efficiency at both ends of the pitch.

The Vila Nova outfit have also struggled at the Estadio Municipal 22 de Junho this term, with Fama among three sides in the division yet to record a home victory, having collected just two points from four outings on their own turf, the most recent of which was a 4-1 defeat to Alverca.

Arouca, on the other hand, arrive in considerably better shape compared to the hosts, having enjoyed an impressive start under Vitor Severino, who took charge in October following Vasco Seabra's departure for Rio Ave.

Although the Wolves had enjoyed an encouraging campaign under Seabra, Severino inherited a side that had gone three matches without a win but has since guided them to four consecutive victories across the league and Taca de Portugal.

An extra-time cup victory over Belenenses came between three successive 1-0 league wins against Estrela Amadora, Alverca and Nacional, leaving Arouca with 13 goals scored and seven conceded in their opening 10 Primeira Liga matches, as well as a joint-league-high six clean sheets.

The Wolves have also been resilient on their travels, with their only defeat in five league trips this season coming against defending champions Porto, while two victories and two draws have given them eight points and made them the division's eighth-best away side.

However, Arouca have struggled in recent meetings with Famalicao, going winless in their last four competitive encounters and losing two of their previous three league visits to Vila Nova, while failing to score during that period.

Famalicao will be without Rodrigo Pinheiro, who is suspended after being sent off during last weekend's league defeat to Braga.

Georgios Koutsias is expected to lead the attack after scoring five league goals this season, while Sorriso and Romeo Beney could provide support from the flanks, with Oscar Aranda another option in the wide areas.

Arouca have a considerably cleaner bill of health, with Miguel Puche their only notable absentee as he continues his recovery from an anterior cruciate ligament injury.

Gabriel Rukavina is available again after serving a one-match suspension following his dismissal against Alverca, although the midfielder is yet to start a league game since joining from Rijeka in the summer.

Ivan Barbero should lead the line as he looks to add to his five league goals this season, while Nais Djouahra is expected to feature prominently after registering five assists in the competition.

Carevic; Garcia, Rofino, Realpe, Bondo; Van de Looi, De Amorim; Beney, Santos, Sorriso; Koutsias.

De Arruabarrena; Esgaio, Sanchez, Fontan, Lebedenko; Van Ee, Fukui; Trezza, Flores, Djouahra; Barbero.

Famalicao's home struggles and the uncertainty surrounding their interim management make it difficult to back them against an Arouca side that has found its rhythm and been particularly solid defensively, so a narrow away victory looks likely.

#1766. City fire blanks in shoot-out as Maresca’s opening game ends in defeat by Inter

Manchester City lost the Asahi Super Dry Trophy 3-1 on a penalty shoot-out against Inter Milan.

Enzo Maresca took charge of the Premier  League runners-up for the first time since his arrival as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, though he was without many of his stars who had yet to return from World Cup duty.

One of the players missing was Elliot Anderson, the £116m signing from Nottingham Forest, though Jeremy Monga, 16, was an unused substitute after being brought in from Leicester City in the summer transfer window.

City took the lead on 14 minutes through Divin Mubamba as he tapped in an Antoine Semenyo cross, but Inter’s experienced defender Benjamin Pavard levelled just six minutes later when City failed to clear a corner.

The Premier League side dominated possession in the second half after an even first 45 minutes but could not find a way through. Phil Foden, the captain, was again underwhelming after a difficult year last season, but with the season still to come he had plenty of time to show his best form once more after signing a new contract at the Etihad.

The game went to penalties after full-time with no extra time played, and only Claudio Echeverri held his nerve for City as Inter Milan scored three of theirs, Matteo Lavelli netting the winning spot-kick.

Both teams learnt little from the match as Inter made 11 changes and City eight, though Maresca will have been impressed by Ryan McAidoo’s performance as a second-half substitute, as he regularly threatened from the right wing. The 18-year-old forward will surely be in demand from other clubs looking to loan him, and City may yet be tempted to keep him around for the coming season.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester City and Inter Milan.

The two sides meet  at Kai Tak Sports Park, Hong  Kong as their pre-season work kicks up a gear ahead of the new campaign.

City are still getting used to life without Pep Guardiola, the coach who left after a decade of high spending and high performance.

In his place is Enzo Maresca, who is not shy with the chequebook himself.

Ayyoub Bouaddi, the outstanding 18-year-old Moroccan international, should soon arrive from Lille when a fee is agreed, but Elliot Anderson and Jeremy Monga have already been signed.

City were runners-up last season, so Maresca is under pressure not just to keep things going without Guardiola, but to get the team back to the top of English football. That looks to be a tough prospect with Arsenal likely to sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle in the coming days.

Inter, meanwhile, have swooped to pick up John Stones on a free transfer after his contract ended at the Etihad Stadium, and he is joined by Manuel Akanji, another former City centre-back whose loan turned permanent in the summer.

Inter won Serie A last season under head coach Cristian Chivu, and they are still one of the best sides in Europe.

While this friendly is likely to be played at a reduced pace, and will be disrupted by rustiness and substitutes, we could still learn a lot about both sides going into the new campaign, and there may be the odd surprise thrown up by a young player looking to stake a claim ahead of his senior colleagues this year.

#1765. Avram Glazer sparks Manchester United fan fury with bold claim in rare public interview

Co-owner Avram Glazer has reportedly claimed that clubs of Manchester United’s stature do not have to rely on sporting success to generate huge commercial revenue.

Michael Carrick’s side snapped a dismal run of nine games without a victory across all competitions with a dramatic comeback win over Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday night, offering the beleaguered head coach some much-needed respite after a torrid start to the campaign.

But any excitement over a potential turnaround in fortunes on the pitch have been dampened somewhat by Glazer’s rare appearance as a speaker at the inaugural Deutsche Bank Sports Investment Conference in London back in September.

According to the Man Utd co-chairman, sporting teams on the scale of Manchester United do not require success on the pitch to yield commercial power.

The Athletic report that Glazer drew comparisons between Manchester United and Major League Baseball (MLB) giants the New York Yankees, plus NFL powerhouses the Dallas Cowboys.

The Yankees have not lifted baseball’s major honour, the World Series, since 2009, with the Cowboys’ Super Bowl drought dating back to 1995.

Despite the long waits for glory, both franchises are among the most successful teams in their respective sports. The Yankees’ 27 titles are the most World Series wins by any team by some distance, while the Cowboys’ five Super Bowl victories sit behind only the Pittsburgh Steelers and New England Patriots.

Although Manchester United have won multiple cup competitions following Sir Alex Ferguson’s departure, since 2013 they have failed to lift the most direct comparison to a World Series or Super Bowl - the Premier League title.

Glazer’s comments have been construed by some angry fans on social media as an acceptance of poor results on the pitch, as long as revenues remain high.

Fans have ramped up their protests against Manchester United’s owners - majority shareholders the Glazer family, as well as minority stakeholders INEOS, who control the club’s sporting operations and are fronted by Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

#1764. RB Leipzig vs. Man City lineups confirmed: Captain Haaland as Cherki, Foden, Guehi decisions made for Champions League game

By Oliver Thomas | 04 Nov 2026 18:52, Last updated: 04 Nov 2026 19:11

Erling Haaland will captain Manchester City in tonight’s Champions League clash against RB Leipzig at the Red Bull Arena.

The prolific Norwegian drew a blank in front of goal in City’s 1-0 Premier League home defeat to Brighton last weekend, but he has scored more goals against Leipzig (12 in just eight games) than he has against any other opponent in his career and will be looking to add to his tally in Germany.

Manager Enzo Maresca has made a total of four changes to his starting lineup, with Marc Guehi, Nico O'Reilly, Rayan Cherki and Phil Foden all recalled at the expense of Ruben Dias, Josko Gvardiol, Ayyoub Bouaddi and Jeremy Doku.

Haaland will wear the captain’s armband in the absence of Dias, who will begin on the substitutes’ bench for the first time this season in either the Champions League or Premier League.

Guehi and Abdukodir Khusanov will therefore start together at centre-back, with Matheus Nunes and O’Reilly playing either side of them as full-backs.

Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez retain their midfield partnership, with Cherki returning to operate in the number 10 role as Foden and Iliman Ndiaye begin out wide in support of Haaland leading the line.

As for Leipzig, head coach Martin Demichelis – a former Man City defender – has made just two changes to the side that began the 2-0 win over Schalke 04 in the Bundesliga last weekend.

Christoph Baumgartner is fit to start in centre-midfield alongside Neil El Aynaoui and Ezechiel Banzuzi, with the Austrian coming into the first XI at the expense of Rocco Reitz.

The other change sees Ridle Baku replace Benjamin Henrichs at right-back, joining Willi Orban, Castello Lukeba and David Raum in a four-man defence.

Antonio Nusa and Romulo Cardoso, who were both on target against Schalke, continue in a three-man frontline next to Brighton loanee Brajan Gruda.

Christopher Nkunku, who scored a memorable UCL hat-trick against Man City in a 6-3 defeat at the Etihad in 2021-22, will begin as a substitute along with defender Maxime Esteve, who has recovered from a knock to make the matchday squad.

RB Leipzig starting lineup: Vandevoordt; Baku, Orban, Lukeba, Raum; Baumgartner, Banzuzi, El Aynaoui; Gruda, Romulo, Nusa

Subs: Nyland, Kone, Esteve, Klostermann, Henrichs, Seiwald, Reitz, Maksimovic, Bakayoko, Gomis, Nkunku

Manchester City starting lineup: Donnarumma; Nunes, Khusanov, Guehi, O’Reilly; Anderson, Fernandez; Ndiaye, Cherki, Foden; Haaland

Subs: Bettinelli, Rulli, Dias, Kovacic, Doku, Ait-Nouri, Reis, Gvardiol, Bouaddi, Allan, Samba, Lewis

#1763. Harry Kane signs record-breaking Bayern Munich contract to become Europe's highest-paid player

Harry Kane has signed a lucrative new contract at Bayern Munich that is believed to make him the highest-paid player in Europe by base salary.

Kane has committed his future to the Bundesliga giants until the end of the 2028/29 season.

The 33-year-old’s new deal comes just over a week after he beat Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to win the 2026 Ballon d’Or award.

It follows months of negotiations with Bayern chiefs over the finer details, though both parties were confident throughout those talks that a breakthrough would eventually be found.

Kane had this season entered the final year of the contract he initially signed with Bayern in 2023 when he left Tottenham to join the German club for €100million (£86m).

Kane, who scored a club-record 61 goals in 51 games for Bayern across all competitions last season, said: “I feel right at home at FC Bayern. I love the club, the fans and the city of Munich.

“We have a fantastic team and, in Vincent Kompany, a fantastic manager. It makes me very proud to be part of this club.

“My whole family is very happy here. I was keen to stay. I'm now looking forward to the future and I want to win many more titles with this great club.”

Kane has won three Golden Boot awards in Germany and two Bundesliga titles so far. In last season’s German Cup final, he scored a hat-trick in a 3-0 win over Stuttgart as Bayern won the trophy for the first time in six years.

In late September, Kane had said: “We're still talking, we're in good talks [over a new contract], I'll be honest, we're fairly close.

“There's still some things that we need to iron out but I'm happy there. I think it won't be too long before there's some sort of announcement.”

#1762. Fabregas stays grounded, says Como have more work to do after nine-goal rout

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Cesc Fabregas chose to remain grounded and pointed out that Como have more work to do to reach the knockout rounds of the Champions League, after they put nine goals past Lens.

On Wednesday, Como recorded the joint-biggest win in Champions League history with their staggering 9-1 success at the Stade Bollaert-Delelis.

The only previous eight-goal victories in the competition were Liverpool's 8-0 win over Besiktas in 2007 and Real Madrid's 8-0 triumph against Malmo in 2015.

Como also became just the second team to score nine goals in a Champions League match, after Bayern Munich beat Dinamo Zagreb 9-2 in 2024, while they are the first Italian side to score nine in a major European competition since Roma beat Altay SK 10-1 in 1962.

Como's 19 goals in their first four major European games are the joint-most by any club, matching QPR's tally when they made their continental bow in 1976, and after taking nine points from those matches, they sit fourth in the league-phase standings.

However, Fabregas urged his players not to get carried away, particularly with Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona among their future opponents in Europe and a trip to San Siro to face Inter coming up this weekend, in Serie A.

"It is also our fourth ever Champions League game, so four is the key number here," Fabregas told Sky Sport Italia.

"I'm happy – everything went our way. The lads did well; now we have to prepare for a very important match on Sunday, the ninth one between the international breaks.

"When I saw the last two games were PSG and Barcelona, I thought we needed to get as many points as possible in the early fixtures.

"Nothing is impossible, but these are two teams who are superior to the rest.

"There is a long way to go. Those games are in the last two weeks of January, so all I am focused on is recovering the injured players, because we are missing so many, in attack especially."

▪️ Lens 1-9 Como (2026) ▪️ Real Madrid 8-0 Malmö (2015) ▪️ Liverpool 8-0 Beşiktaş (2007) Como making history  #UCL https://t.co/mSbmhcLpHG

— UEFA Champions League (@ChampionsLeague) November 4, 2026

The previous record for most goals scored by a team in their first four Champions League fixtures was set by Juventus in 1995-96, with 14, a mark Como have shattered.

No French team had previously lost a home European game by more than five goals, and Lens boss Yannick Cahuzac pulled no punches in his post-match interview with UEFA.com.

"It's a heavy scoreline; we were completely dominated. We've got to have a long, hard look at ourselves and attempt to regain some pride against Marseille on Sunday," he said.

"I can't offer you an in-depth analysis of what went wrong. We're hurting, but I'm going to concentrate on my players and how we can pick them up from this."

#1761. Sky Germany: Krösche heading for Milan but compensation must be discussed – the situation

Sources in Germany are confirming that Markus Krösche should be announced by AC Milan in the coming weeks, ready to start in January.

It is seemingly not a very well-kept secret by this point that Milan are looking to appoint Krösche as their new Head of Football, having made an attempt to get him in the summer. Sources in Italy have claimed things are done, but their German colleagues have always been a bit more hesitant.

Now, Sky Germany confirm that Krösche’s future likely lies in Italy because a move to Milan is becoming increasingly likely. However, no deal has been finalised yet: officials from both clubs still need to hold talks as Krösche is only on leave from Frankfurt.

His contract, which runs until 2028, is currently still valid. The 46-year-old insisted on having a release clause included in his contract. Specifically, this means that any club wanting to hire him before the summer of 2027 will have to pay a fee of approximately €5-7m, or negotiate with Eintracht.

No advanced talks have yet taken place, but Sky do add that Krösche is expected to take on the role of Head of Football with Milan. A start date of January 1, 2027 – coinciding with the start of the winter transfer window – is being discussed.

Meanwhile, Eintracht Frankfurt have already settled the question of Krösche’s successor. Joti Chatzialexiou is coming from 1. FC Nürnberg and will take over the position of sporting director. So, it seems like just a matter of time.

#1760. Harry Kane salary: How much will England captain earn on record-breaking Bayern Munich contract?

Harry Kane’s phenomenal 2026 just gets better and better, with the England captain signing a lucrative new contract with Bayern Munich - reportedly becoming the highest-paid player in Europe when it comes to base salary.

Last week, Kane was named Ballon d’Or winner after a goal-laden 2025/26 season, having scored 73 times in 65 games for club and country. With 61 goals for Bayern, Kane helped the Bavarian side win the DFB Pokal, German Super Cup and the Bundesliga, as well as reach the semi-finals of the Champions League.

Since arriving in Germany from Tottenham for £86million in 2023, Kane has grabbed 156 goals in 161 total matches. After proving he can still score at an unbelievable rate, Bayern moved to tie their star down as he approached the final six months of his previous deal.

Kane certainly becomes the best-paid player in Bayern’s history, with reports suggesting that the 33-year-old is set to earn around £400,000 a week. That is before any bonuses are accounted for, with the new deal earning him similar wages to Manchester City’s Erling Haaland and Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappe.

Real Madrid did not have to pay a fee to secure Mbappe’s services, with the Frenchman arriving at the Bernabeu in 2024 on a free transfer. BBC Sport reported at the time that Mbappe would earn £12.8m a season, working out to a base salary just shy of £250,000 a week.

However, that does not include a £128m signing-on bonus that will be paid out over the course of his five-year contract, effectively doubling Mbappe’s salary.

Spanish rivals Barcelona have two players reportedly paid around £26.06m a season in gross wages. Summer arrival Rodri was given a similar deal to teenage star Lamine Yamal, who finished third in Ballon d’Or voting behind runner-up Mbappe and winner Kane.

Including bonuses, World Cup winners Rodri and Yamal are believed to earn around £500,000 a week at the Camp Nou.

Haaland signed a contract in January 2025 that tied his future to Manchester City for the best part of a decade. It has been reported that the total package for the deal that lasts until 2034 is worth £260m, which would work out to around £500,000 a week.

However, it is unclear how much of Haaland’s contract is guaranteed wages, nor what percentage of the deal is based on bonuses.

Even Haaland’s contract pales in comparison to that of Cristiano Ronaldo, the highest-paid player in the world who just announced his shock retirement from international duty with Portugal. The 41-year-old’s latest Al-Nassr contract is worth a reported £492m for just two years, with further benefits such as shares in the club.

#1759. Chelsea signing delivers honest admission after slow start: 'I need to improve'

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Marco Palestra has admitted the “need to improve” if he is to make a success of his move to Chelsea.

The Italian joined the Blues in the summer from Atalanta in a move worth around £45million, becoming the first new signing of the Xabi Alonso era at Stamford Bridge.

The versatile wing-back was out injured at the beginning of the season but finally made his first competitive start for the club in Saturday’s 2-0 Premier League victory over 10-man Manchester United.

There was criticism from some quarters of the Chelsea fanbase for the 21-year-old’s defensive positioning in the United game, but Palestra still managed to help the Blues to a rare league clean sheet at home - their first in a game they had also won since January.

Speaking via Chelsea’s official channels, Palestra was asked to describe his emotions back when he discovered in June that his move to Chelsea was going through.

“I was just happy because, when I was young, I never thought I could be a Chelsea player,” said the winner of last season’s Serie A Defender of the Year award.

“So the first emotion was only happiness. Now I am still happy, but I need to improve myself to win with this team.”

Palestra was also asked to recall a coach he had worked with who had given him important advice.

“When I was a bit older, like 16, our coach changed my position,” Palestra said. “His name is Marco Fioretto. He was the first one who moved me from midfield to out wide and he maybe changed my career.”

Palestra will be hoping to retain his place in Chelsea’s starting lineup when Alonso’s team face bottom club Sunderland at the Stadium of Light on Sunday.

#1758. How Fabregas built the most exciting team to watch in today’s football

Lake Como had an international reputation long before its football club began making European headlines. The scenery and the visitors were already there. Inside the stadium, supporters had lived through a rather less glamorous sequence of relegations, financial trouble and fresh starts.

In 2017, Como was starting again in Serie D, the fourth tier of Italian football. Nine years later, it has just beaten Lens 9-1 away from home in the Champions League, with Cesc Fabregas coaching a team that is arguably the most exciting to watch in Europe at the moment.

The result in Lens was extraordinary. But very few people are aware of how Como created the conditions for a night like that to become possible.

Como’s history stretches back to 1907. Before returning in 2024, the club had already spent 13 seasons in Serie A. It had a place in Italian football’s memory, although its previous top-flight appearance, in 2002/03, wasn’t this successful.

The years that followed brought repeated financial trouble. The club’s own history records a brief return to Serie B in 2015, immediate relegation, bankruptcy and an unsuccessful ownership transition. By 2017/18, Como was rebuilding in Serie D.

The ownership change that reshaped its future arrived on April 4, 2019, when London-based SENT Entertainment acquired the club. Promotion to Serie C followed that spring. Como then won its Serie C group in 2020/21 and returned to Serie B, where it stayed for three seasons before the eventual promotion to Serie A.

SENT brought the backing of Indonesia’s Hartono family, whose business interests include the Djarum group. UK company records identify Robert Budi Hartono as SENT’s controlling person. For a club accustomed to financial uncertainty, that ownership gave the rebuilding effort a very different starting point.

Suwarso has helped turn that backing into a broader commercial plan. In a 2024 interview with Reuters, he described linking football to the city’s appeal through tourism, fashion, retail and media. The attraction was easy to understand: a globally recognizable destination offered ways to reach an audience far beyond the club’s existing supporters.

The football operation needed its own investment. Como acquired the Mozzate training center in 2021, adding a permanent asset around which the first team and academy could develop. That kind of work gives a project substance between transfer windows, when the daily business of improving players takes place.

The spending on the squad has also been substantial. In August 2026, La Gazzetta dello Sport reported transfer expenditure of €342 million since the start of 2024/25. That figure puts the scale of the ambition into perspective.

Suwarso oversees the project as president, with sporting director Carlalberto Ludi central to the football operation. Their challenge is to make recruitment, facilities and coaching serve the same purpose. The more expensive the squad becomes, the more important those decisions are.

Fabregas arrived as a player in 2022, when Como was still in Serie B. Thierry Henry also joined as a shareholder that year, giving the club another recognizable figure attached to its ambitions.

Fabregas’s involvement gradually became more substantial. After retiring, he worked with the youth team and took interim charge of the senior side in November 2023. His coaching qualifications were still being completed, so Osian Roberts became caretaker head coach, with the Spaniard remaining on the staff.

Roberts deserves his place in this account. Together, they helped Como finish second in Serie B in 2023/24. The decisive draw with Cosenza on May 10, 2024 ended a 21-year absence from the top flight. Patrick Cutrone, playing for his hometown club, had scored 14 league goals along the way.

That promotion connected the international ambitions of the owners with something much closer to home. For supporters who had followed Como through the lower divisions, Serie A meant seeing a familiar shirt in a competition that had been missing from their lives for more than two decades.

Fabregas was appointed permanent head coach in July 2024, while Roberts moved into a development role. The club was giving a young coach room to establish his ideas while keeping experienced football knowledge around him.

The first full Serie A season ended in tenth place with 49 points. The next season was even more successful and brought Champions League qualification.

Fabregas has made Como recognizable on the field. The team wants the ball, looks for ways through an opponent’s pressure, and gives technically gifted players enough support to attempt difficult things.

The 4-2-3-1 provides a starting structure. Within it, midfielders can drop toward the defense, fullbacks advance and attacking players move inside. Coaches’ Voice documented those rotations in 2025, showing how the foundations of the current approach were already developing in Fabregas’s first Serie A season.

His explanation after the recent win over Manchester United was particularly revealing. Speaking to TNT Sports, Fabregas described exploiting the spaces United’s pressing decisions left available. Two center backs could work around one forward; a player stepping toward a center back could leave Como’s fullback free.

“I don’t like passing the ball just to pass the ball,” he said.

This is very important to understand when watching the game. Fabregas is clearly influenced by the 21st-century Spanish school of football, or tiki-taka, made by Pep Guardiola in Barcelona, the system in which Fabregas also excelled. However, his philosophy is more concrete and similar to Luis Enrique’s, who has a more direct approach with PSG.

While circulating the ball around, Como makes their opponent move, and then tries to attack the opening that follows. A midfielder coming short can draw a marker away from the space another player wants to enter. A fullback advancing can give the attack width while a teammate moves closer to goal.

OF course, this is not easy, and requires considerable coordination. The player receiving under pressure needs to trust that the next option will appear. That’s why all Como’s players are technically gifted, and they are amazing when solving pressing and transforming from defense to attack.

Without the ball, Fabregas has used a 4-4-2 shape, narrowing the midfield and looking to direct opponents toward the touchline. The forwards begin the pressure, but the midfield and defense have to move with them. The attacking football depends on that collective work.

Nico Paz gives Como a player who can turn that structure into something exceptional. His left foot can supply the pass beyond the defense, the shot from the edge of the area or the touch that lets him escape a crowded midfield.

His two goals and an assist against Manchester United were followed by another goal and two assists at Lens. After four Champions League appearances this season, he has three goals and five assists.

Tasos Douvikas gives those creative qualities a willing partner. His movement beyond the back line can pull defenders deeper, while his presence near goal gives teammates a target for the final ball. His hat trick at Lens took him to six Champions League goals, having scored in all four of Como’s matches.

My reading of their partnership is that each helps make the other’s decisions easier. Paz can look forward knowing someone will attack the space. Douvikas can begin a run knowing the player behind him is capable of seeing it.

Maximo Perrone and Luis Milla help connect the buildup to those attacking players. Lucas Da Cunha contributes movement and combinations, Maxence Caqueret offers another midfielder comfortable in tight spaces, and Martin Baturina gives Fabregas an additional creative option.

The second goal in the 9-1 win at Lens brought several of those ideas together. The move began with Jean Butez, Paz delivered toward the far post, Alex Valle arrived to volley across goal, and Douvikas finished. Four different roles contributed to one attack.

By full time, seven Como players had scored, including substitutes Mattia Liberali, Baturina and 18-year-old debutant Matteo Papaccioli.

Como’s first four Champions League results are remarkable: 4-1 against Leipzig, a 3-2 defeat at Feyenoord, 4-1 against United and 9-1 at Lens. That leaves 19 goals scored, six conceded and nine points, with Como fourth in the league-phase standings after matchday four.

Before the European opener, Fabregas had urged his players to approach the Champions League like any other game. The team has carried its ambition into the competition, even when that has involved accepting risks.

The domestic results are important to the argument. Como is also fourth in Serie A and has won four consecutive league matches.

A season needs those victories too. European masterpiece is setting the spotlight on the team, but qualifying for the Champions League again depends on collecting points through months of domestic competition.

There are still weaknesses for opponents to examine. Como has conceded in every Champions League match, and Feyenoord has already shown that its approach can be beaten. When the press breaks down, the space behind the defense can become a problem.

Fabregas has acknowledged that trade-off. After the October win at Fiorentina, he discussed difficulties defending balls in behind in an earlier match against Frosinone. His assessment of those risks sounded like a coach still working through problems as the level rises.

Inter awaits in Serie A after winning 3-0 at Feyenoord. Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona are among Como’s remaining European opponents. Those games will help establish how well the team’s habits survive against stronger pressure and better finishing.

The longer challenge belongs to the whole club: retaining important players, spending effectively and keeping the football operation aligned as expectations grow. The owners have supplied considerable resources. Fabregas and his staff have given the squad a way to use its talent together. Sustaining both parts will determine what follows.

For the supporters who watched Como restart in Serie D, there is already plenty to absorb. The journey back to Serie A took years. Two seasons later, their club is scoring nine in a Champions League away game.

#1757. Joao Neves rules out Premier League move in PSG pledge

By Naim Beneddra | 04 Nov 2026 18:52

Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Joao Neves has delivered a clear message about his future, revealing that he has no ambition to play in the Premier League or La Liga despite previously attracting interest from some of Europe's biggest clubs.

The 22-year-old Portugal international has established himself as a key figure in Luis Enrique's side since arriving from Benfica in 2024, helping the French champions secure back-to-back Champions League titles.

However, Neves has now gone a step further than simply expressing his satisfaction with life in Paris, revealing that he would like to spend the remainder of his playing career at the Parc des Princes.

His comments come shortly after signing a new contract until June 2031 and ahead of PSG's continued pursuit of a third successive European crown.

The midfielder also underlined his importance on the pitch on Tuesday evening, opening the scoring and providing an assist in PSG's emphatic 6-0 Champions League victory away to Villarreal.

Speaking in an interview with French broadcaster CANAL+, Neves made it clear that moving to either England or Spain is not among his career objectives.

"I don't have the objective of going to Spain or England," the former Benfica youngster explained.

"I have an objective, and it is to feel good in my life and to win here. Joao wants to stay here his whole career."

The declaration is particularly significant given Neves's age and the transfer speculation that has surrounded him since his emergence in Portuguese football.

Manchester United were among the clubs linked with the midfielder before his move to PSG, while Manchester City were subsequently credited with an interest in bringing him to the Etihad Stadium.

In September 2025, reports suggested that City were considering an offer worth approximately £105m for Neves, although PSG were understood to be unwilling to entertain his departure.

That speculation never developed into a confirmed transfer agreement, and there is no indication that either Manchester club is currently negotiating for his signature.

Nevertheless, Neves's latest comments suggest that even the prospect of playing in England's top flight holds little appeal to him at present.

His position is supported by his recent contractual commitment.

In September, PSG announced a series of extensions involving several important members of Luis Enrique's squad, including Neves, Willian Pacho, Lucas Beraldo, Senny Mayulu and Fabian Ruiz.

The Portuguese midfielder's agreement now runs until the summer of 2031, giving the French champions considerable security over his future.

While such a contract does not rule out a transfer later in his career, Neves has made his personal preference unusually clear.

For Premier League clubs hoping to attract one of Europe's most accomplished young midfielders, his comments provide little encouragement.

Neves's commitment to PSG is closely connected to the success he has experienced since leaving Benfica.

The Portugal international has developed into an integral part of Luis Enrique's midfield alongside compatriot Vitinha, combining an ability to regain possession with the technical quality required to operate in tight spaces.

His contribution has been particularly important to PSG's recent European dominance.

Since his arrival in 2024, the French club have won two consecutive Champions League titles, establishing themselves among the continent's leading teams.

Neves has also demonstrated that his role extends beyond winning possession and maintaining control in midfield.

Against Villarreal on Tuesday, he opened the scoring after nine minutes, reacting quickly inside the penalty area following a corner.

He later supplied the assist for David Boly's goal as PSG completed their record-breaking away victory in the Champions League.

The result maintained the defending champions' perfect record in this season's league phase, with four victories from their opening four matches.

Despite that impressive start, Neves believes maintaining the standards established over the previous two seasons will present a considerable challenge.

"It's the mentality," he explained when discussing PSG's continued ambition.

"You have two Champions Leagues, but you keep making the necessary efforts. Maintaining that quality is even harder than winning two Champions Leagues."

The midfielder also identified a specific objective for the current European campaign.

"We want to try to finish in the top eight, something we haven't managed in the last two seasons."

That target reflects PSG's determination to avoid the additional knockout-round play-offs and secure direct qualification for the last 16.

Neves's performances against Villarreal offered another illustration of why Luis Enrique considers him central to those ambitions.

And while his contract already ties him to Paris for several more years, his latest declaration suggests that he sees no need to leave the French capital to fulfil his remaining ambitions in football.

#1755. Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid

JJ Gabriel showed glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

United fought back after conceding an early goal against Atletico to secure their second win of pre-season.

They fell behind in the sixth minute when Arnau Ortiz’s cross into the box evaded everyone, including United keeper Tom Heaton before hitting the back of the net.

United got the equaliser their performance deserved when the impressive Shea Lacey showed his skill in the box and was fouled. From the resulting penalty, Bryan Mbeumo sent the goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

In the 72nd minute, Mbeumo got his second of the afternoon after he bundled the ball home after the United press forced Atletico into a mistake.

The Spanish side hit the post twice in the closing stages but United held on to win.

“We had a clear plan before the game, everyone stuck to it and made the game enjoyable,” Mbeumo said. “We work really hard during training for these games, the main goal is to be ready for the season starting. I have done great things on the right but also as a striker.

“I think I am more experienced on the wing but I enjoy playing as a striker. For an offensive player, it is always good to score for the team.”

And it is. All over in Stockholm as United come back from behind to win. A really good performance by Michael Carrick’s side.

Iker Luque shoots from distance. It looks good but flies over the bar. And that should be the final effort of the match...

Mendoza and Hjulmand both hit the post in quick succession. Heaton was beaten on both occasions. United were a bit fortunate there.

Now that they are behind, Atletico are starting to have a bit more possession and play on the front foot.

A slow second half comes alive as United take the lead. A slack pass in defence by Atletico is pounced upon by Fletcher. He runs to the byline, cuts the ball back to the unmarked Mbeumo, who taps in.

OFF: Shaw, Dorgu, Lacey, MaguireON: Armer, Amass, Zirkzee, Williams

Big save from Heaton to deny Atletico at the near post after Yoro was beaten by a lovely pass from Lemar.

The energy and intensity of the first half has largely disappeared in this half. Neither keeper has been worked.

Another player, who has been tidy for United is Santos in midfield. He’s controlled the middle of the park, been safe in possession but also willing to fire a pass into the forwards.

Seven changes coming for Atletico. Typical pre-season move.

Mbeumo takes responsibility, waits for the keeper to dive and strokes the ball into the bottom left corner.

Dancing feet from Lacey in the box and Castillo brings him down. The referee rightly points to the spot.

Atletico make three changes. I’ll get them to you shortly!

No time added on, so that is the end of the half. An intriguing 45 mins. United will feel they don’t deserve to be losing.

United fail to clear the ball and it falls to Arnau Ortiz, who forces a good save from Heaton. That would have been harsh on United.

Lookman has been very quiet for Atletico. Yoro has marked him out of the game but in truth, Atletico have given him nothing to work with.

Apart from the move that led to Atletico’s goal, they have barely been in United’s half. They are struggling to beat United’s press and keep the ball. United are losing but they are working very hard and playing well.

Great pressing by United leads to Amad winning the ball back. Yoro finds Lacey, who spins and goes down the right. He whips in a cross and Mbeumo rises to attack it but heads wide. Probably should have done better.

It is probably an easy comparison but Lacey has a bit of Phil Foden about him with his movement and touch. He looks promising.

Carlos Martín goes down after a coming together with Heaven. The United defender got his arm across and made minimal contact with Martín’s face but the referee falls for the play-acting and calls a foul.

An aggressive press from United as they look to deny time to Atletico. They are pushing for that equaliser.

Amad, Mount and Mbeumo all want it. Amad takes it and his low strike is deflected and looks certain to beat Oblak but the keeper reacts quickly to make the stop.

Santos punches a pass through the lines, Mbeumo combines with Mount and the attacker is brought to the ground on the edge of the box...

Nearly a quick reply by United. Amad sets the ball for Mount to cross into the box. The midfielder’s ball goes to the far post, where Shaw meets it with a thumping volley but Oblak stands his ground and palms the ball over the bar.

From the resulting corner, Yoro should do better with his header but his effort goes wide.

Early goal for Atletico. They take a short corner, Arnau Ortiz whips in a dangerous ball that beats everyone and drops in at the far post. Heaton never moved.

United dominating possession in the opening stages with Atletico happy to sit off and let the Premier League side have it. Even in pre-season, Diego Simeone has his side set up well to defend.

The visit to the Strawberry Arena means United are back at the stadium where they won the 2017 Europa League.

📸 Wayne Rooney, 2017 🏆#UEL | @ManUtd pic.twitter.com/HxZVn1mAEQ

Gianni Infantino is facing an ultimatum from Uefa: resign or face an emergency no-confidence vote.

It is understood all 55 of Uefa’s member nations would opt to oust Infantino in a vote of no-confidence if he refuses to step down. Uefa can trigger such a vote with just 43 member nations.

European football’s governing body announced a loss of confidence on Saturday morning and has demanded change after Infantino was forced to scrap his £15bn plan to sell a stake in the World Cup.

Uefa’s statement followed widespread opposition and a revolt within Fifa’s ranks that staff are calling “kill the monster”.

The Football Association backed Uefa’s stance, saying: “We fully support Uefa’s position. It is time for a full and robust review of Fifa’s leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long-term stewardship of football at its heart.”

Good afternoon and welcome to pre-season coverage of Manchester United against Atletico Madrid.

Michael Carrick’s squad continue their preparations for the new season with a trip to the Swedish capital, Stockholm, where they face Diego Simeone’s La Liga side.

Last week, United cruised to a 5-0 victory over Rosenborg but today will be their first real test. They are slowly starting to get players back but the likes of captain Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans will not be involved.

“I think we’re in a good place. I think there’s four weeks to go to the start and we’re gradually getting some boys back from the World Cup as we progress,” Carrick said.

“But I think a little bit of patience and time and trying to keep ahead and as I said, keeping everyone fit but moving forward is a really good direction to go in. And as it stands right now, I think we’re in a pretty good place. So, the boys will get better as we go.”

One player who will be looking to impress is Mason Mount. He has had an injury-hit spell at Old Trafford but is fit and ready to go for the season. He is also growing into a leadership role at the club.

He told BBC Radio Manchester: “You have different types of leaders, you have ones that are very vocal. I always want to see myself as one that leads by example and never stops working on the pitch.

“I’ve been captain previously years ago. I love the role especially with a lot of younger players on the pitch being able to speak to them and make them feel comfortable in the game and off the pitch as well. It’s a role that I really like and loved having it [the captain’s armband] in the second half.”

#1753. Hamburger SV vs Borussia Monchengladbach - prediction, team news, lineups

By Lewis Nolan | 04 Nov 2026 19:16, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 01:35

Volksparkstadion will be the backdrop for an early-season six-pointer in the Bundesliga's relegation battle on Friday, when Hamburger SV host Borussia Monchengladbach.

HSV find themselves in 15th place with just nine points after eight matchweeks, though their position is not nearly as dire as the visitors, who are last in 18th place with four points.

Hamburger should not yet panic about their position in the table give just two points separate them from eighth-placed Eintracht Frankfurt, but they have lost key matches to rivals in recent weeks.

The hosts' last two Bundesliga games were 1-0 and 3-1 losses against Paderborn and Frankfurt respectively, the latter of which occurred on November 1.

Between those two results was another 3-1 defeat against Frankfurt in the DFB-Pokal, but it should be noted that they had won their prior three matches, with all three successes coming in the top flight.

Merlin Polzin will be concerned that only one team have conceded more times in the Bundesliga this season (19), while his players have only netted two goals in their past three league outings.

HSV's form at home has been strong considering they have won two of their three clashes at Volksparkstadion in the top flight this term, and a win on Friday would be their third consecutive victory in the division at the stadium.

Gladbach may be at the foot of the table, but they have now taken four points from the last six on offer, including when they beat Stuttgart 3-2 on October 23.

Die Fohlen are unsurprisingly the worst defensive team in the division having conceded 22 times in just eight games, though perhaps their goalless stalemate with Paderborn on October 31 is a sign of improvement.

Boss Alexander Blessin was widely praised for his time at St Pauli, especially for 2024-25, when his team ended the campaign with the second fewest number of goals conceded (41).

The visitors' record against their hosts has not been positive considering they have only won one of their five most recent meetings with HSV, losing on two occasions while failing to win any of their last three encounters with Hamburger.

A victory for Gladbach would be their second in a row on the road following their success against Stuttgart, though they did lose their opening three away Bundesliga fixtures.

Borussia Monchengladbach Bundesliga form:

Borussia Monchengladbach form (all competitions):

Hamburger still have a number of injury concerns to deal with, including to centre-backs Sebastiaan Bornauw (jaw) and Nicolas Capaldo (muscle), while striker Yussuf Poulsen's hip issue is likely to keep him sidelined.

Whether Albert Gronbaek can lead the line and score his first Bundesliga goal of the season remains to be seen, though he will need support from midfielders Albert Sambi Lokonga, Miro Muheim and Martin Adeline.

In defence, expect to see a three-man unit consisting of Shafiq Nandja, Jordan Torunarigha and Warmed Omari.

Gladbach come into the clash without the likes of Hugo Bolin (muscle), Franck Honorat (muscle) and Tim Kleindienst, leaving their attack looking especially light.

Isac Lidberg may be trusted to start as his team's number nine, while Robin Hack and Wael Mohya could play in supportive roles.

Hamburger's form has been disappointing, but given they have often played well at home this season, they are sure to pose a challenge on Friday.

#1752. Frenkie De Jong hits back at critics and sends Hansi Flick message

By Naim Beneddra | 04 Nov 2026 19:44

Barcelona midfielder Frenkie de Jong has expressed his frustration at the constant speculation surrounding him, while making it clear that he wants to reclaim a regular starting place under Hansi Flick.

The Netherlands international spoke out after reaching 300 appearances for the Catalan giants during Tuesday's 3-0 Champions League victory over Aston Villa, having recently returned from a lengthy injury absence.

De Jong believes that his performances, fitness and future attract considerably more scrutiny than those of his teammates, particularly when he is unavailable for selection.

However, the 29-year-old also delivered an encouraging update on his physical condition, insisting that his knee is no longer causing problems and that he is ready to compete for a more prominent role.

His comments arrive at an important moment for Flick, with Barcelona preparing to face Atletico Madrid this weekend and uncertainty emerging over the availability of fellow midfielder Rodri.

Speaking to reporters following the victory over Aston Villa, De Jong acknowledged that the speculation surrounding him had become a recurring source of frustration.

"There is always a bit of noise around me, especially when I'm not there," the midfielder said, as quoted by Mundo Deportivo.

"For some reason, in the summer when there is no football, or when I'm injured..."

De Jong went on to suggest that he receives more attention than other members of the Barcelona squad, although he accepted that this might partly reflect his personal perception.

"I feel that there is always more noise around me than around others. But perhaps that's just my impression when people talk about me. These are things I don't have much control over."

The Dutchman's remarks follow several months of questions about his fitness and position at Camp Nou.

De Jong sustained a knee ligament injury while representing the Netherlands at the 2026 World Cup, leaving him unavailable for the opening weeks of Barcelona's campaign.

During his recovery, he also addressed reports concerning his relationship with Flick and the club's hierarchy, rejecting suggestions that he had fallen out with the German coach.

His latest comments suggest that the scrutiny remains a sensitive subject, even after his return to competitive action.

Nevertheless, De Jong was keen to emphasise that his physical condition has improved considerably.

"I feel very good, very strong, with a lot of desire and motivation," he explained.

"My knee isn't bothering me. What's happened has happened."

The midfielder made his first appearance of the season as a substitute against Real Madrid on October 25, before starting Barcelona's emphatic 6-1 league victory over Alaves six days later.

Flick deployed him in central defence against Alaves, illustrating the versatility that has allowed the former Ajax player to operate in several positions during his Barcelona career.

Tuesday's Champions League encounter brought another significant moment, as De Jong replaced Pedri in the 70th minute to make his 300th competitive appearance for the club.

He was subsequently presented with a commemorative shirt by his teammates.

Having already surpassed Philip Cocu and Ronald Koeman, De Jong holds the record for the most competitive appearances by a Dutch player in Barcelona's history.

Despite his willingness to help in defence, De Jong made no secret of his preferred position or his desire to return to the starting lineup.

"I feel more comfortable in midfield, but I will help the team wherever it needs me," he said.

Asked whether he hoped to start against Atletico Madrid on Sunday, the Dutch international acknowledged that his recent injury would influence Flick's decision.

"I would like to start matches, but we have to take into account that I've been out for a long time, and that depends on the coaching staff."

His comments are particularly relevant following Rodri's withdrawal at half time against Aston Villa.

The former Manchester City midfielder complained of muscular discomfort during Tuesday's encounter, prompting Flick to introduce Marc Bernal for the second half.

Barcelona have since confirmed a minor hamstring injury, leaving Rodri's availability for the trip to Atletico in doubt.

Flick has already suggested that Bernal could be considered as a replacement, while also pointing out that De Jong has only recently returned from injury.

That leaves the Barcelona manager with a decision to make over his midfield combination, particularly given the demands of facing one of La Liga's strongest opponents away from home.

De Jong's ability to operate alongside Pedri, provide defensive cover or contribute further forward gives Flick another option, but his limited minutes this season remain a consideration.

The Dutchman has repeatedly expressed his commitment to Barcelona, having signed a contract extension until June 2029.

His immediate priority, however, is considerably more straightforward: putting his injury problems behind him and earning a place in the team through his performances.

After reaching 300 appearances, De Jong is determined that his next chapter at Barcelona should be defined by what he contributes on the pitch rather than the speculation surrounding him.

This greatly reflects his vision and ability to curb any impulse to seek a ready-made answer in the transfer market.

If you include the loan and youth players, Liverpoolai??i??s squad strength is pretty massive. So there is little sense in buying loads of new players, unless thereai??i??s conclusive evidence that the current crop canai??i??t cut it at the highest level. Seeing how itai??i??s still early days in the reign of Klopp, itai??i??s unlikely he would have been able to reach that conclusion about too many of his players.

In the last two weeks, Klopp has recalled loanees Tiago Ilori (Aston Villa), Sheyi Ojo (Wolverhampton), Ryan Kent (Coventry City), Danny Ward (Aberdeen) and Kevin Stewart (Swindon Town). Against Exeter City, he also utilized all of these players barring Ward, and played youngsters Cameron Brannagan, Joao Carlos Teixeira, Jerome Sinclair, Brad Smith and Connor Randall.

This is exactly what the youth academy is there for, and itai??i??s very pleasing to see Klopp isnai??i??t ignoring it and focusing on the transfer market. That being said, itai??i??s not as if the German should never sign a player. In the transfer market, there are 3 types of signings — the doai??i??s, the donai??i??ts, and the ones you sign only if you absolutely have to.

So then, thereai??i??s only two possible types of players Liverpool should be buying in the winter window:

In the summer windows, one can look at options beyond these two. Your scouting team can have a list of targets, clubs are more open to listening to offers, and you have an opportunity to move out some of your own players to make room for signings. You also have a solid pre-season ahead, so that players who might need to be brought up to speed on the teamai??i??s style of play can be worked with before theyai??i??re thrown into the deep end. January simply isnai??i??t the right time for all this.

So what kind of signings should be avoided? Letai??i??s just call them the a Southampton signingsai??i??. These are the so-called a Premier League readyai??i?? players who seem like an improved version of the current squad, mostly based on their performances in the current season. Some examples of such players would be the likes of Saido Mane, Marko Arnautovic, and Riyad Mahrez. All 3 are talented players, and on paper would make good additions to a side that has not performed well in front of goal. But one good season does not a good player make. Keep in mind that Christian Benteke, Adam Lallana, Dejan Lovren and Roberto Firmino were all their former clubsai??i?? best players, and highly coveted at the time, but none of them have been instant hits at Merseyside. Therefore, to imagine that a January signing will suddenly improve your season is misguided, and you end up paying over the odds as most clubs donai??i??t want to lose their best players mid-way through the season.

One recent transfer rumour has linked Alexandre Pato to a move to Merseyside. What a pointless and risky transfer this would be. Liverpool already have 4 senior strikers on their rolls, excluding Roberto Firmino who can also play up front. Other than Daniel Sturridge, who is one day elder to Pato, all the other 3 are younger than the Brazilian. Before his move to the Brazilian league, his injury record at AC Milan was as bad as Daniel Sturridgeai??i??s. All 4 of the Liverpool forwards have proven themselves either in the Premier League (Ings, Sturridge, Benteke) or the French Ligue 1 (Origi).

Pato is exactly the kind of transfer Liverpool need to steer clear of. Additionally, talks of an early exit from the club for Christian Benteke are ridiculous. The big Belgian has not had time to settle at the club, with his 17 appearances for the club being overseen by two different managers with different styles of playing, and both of these styles being vastly different from how he was played at Aston Villa last season. He deserves till the end of this season at the very least, if not more.

This is the a emergency signinga scenario — a situation all managers (and Boards) hope never arises. For a club with a relatively deep squad like Liverpool, injuries should be the last reason to sign a player, but there are exceptions. For example, the centre-half situation at Liverpool right now. When youai??i??re forced to play Jose Enrique and Tiago Ilori (who started his first competitive game of the season) as the centre-back pairing, the situation is truly dire. One could make a case for signing an experienced centre-half to step in, like Andrea Ranocchia (Inter Milan) and Neven Subotic (Borussia Dortmund), both of whom have been linked with a transfer to Liverpool FC.

Even in such an extreme scenario, seeing how Mamadou Sakho and Kolo Toure may possibly return within the week, these signings make no sense. You donai??i??t spend A?7 to A?10 million on players just to feature in a few games. Hopefully Liverpool FC will make it out of this window without any such expenditures.

History teaches us that short-cuts and quick-fixes can be accompanied by pretty massive pitfalls. Liverpool FC fans need to stop looking to the transfer market for the answers. Jurgen Klopp is at the helm, and his methods require investing time and effort in the players he works with. Heai??i??ll sign players when he comes across the right ones, but hopefully wonai??i??t be spending money searching for some unicorn signing that will miraculously fly the club to success.

And it is absolutely the right approach to take.

#1750. Allegri rues late errors from tired Napoli in Porto loss

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Massimiliano Allegri conceded that Napoli are struggling to cope with the demands of their busy schedule amid an injury crisis, following their heavy loss to Porto.

Allegri is coming under increasing pressure at Napoli, which was compounded by their 4-1 Champions League defeat to Porto on Wednesday.

Despite Scott McTominay cancelling out Jan Bednarek's early header to take Napoli into half-time level, Gabri Veiga, Jakub Kiwior and Samu Aghehowa all scored in the final 20 minutes to secure a big win for Porto.

Napoli were without nine players through injury, including the likes of Giovanni Di Lorenzo, Mathias Olivera, Benoit Badiashile and Leonardo Spinazzola.

With the majority of his absentees coming in defence, Allegri, who was only able to name seven substitutes on his bench, tweaking Napoli's formation to a 3-5-1-1 to try to combat his issues.

However, they had little success as Porto had 19 shots (eight on target) worth 3.1 expected goals (xG), while they also hit the woodwork twice.

"We made mistakes on two set-plays; the team had, in my view, a good performance up to the 70th minute," Allegri told Sky Sport Italia.

"It was an aggressive performance. We went man for man but then conceded this second goal on a bouncing ball and, with fatigue, we didn't push up in time for the offside.

"These are errors that unfortunately can happen when you are tired. The tempo is high in the Champions League, and in those final minutes we were struggling, as they hit the crossbar twice just before the goal and were cutting through us fairly easily.

"I know the limitations of this squad. In the first game with Genoa, I was accused of having a bad first half, but it was because we needed to control the tempo.

Full time: #PortoNapoli 4-1 #ForzaNapoliSempre https://t.co/0jsLmELuCz

— Official SSC Napoli (@sscnapoli) November 4, 2026

"Lately, we've had good first halves, but then fallen away in the second half; it's because we have a limited squad.

"If the same lot play every three days, the tempo is high; by the 70th minute, it becomes a different match. You can only control that if you have eight or nine players on the bench. Now we've got one more game to play with Lazio; then we'll see what happens when more players return."

Napoli have lost five of their last seven group- or league-phase matches in the Champions League, as many defeats as they suffered at this stage of the competition across their previous 23 games combined.

The Partenopei sit 27th in the table at the halfway stage, but their troubles span across all competitions as they also sit eighth in Serie A after just one win in their last four games.

They face Lazio in their final league game before the upcoming international break, and Allegri says he is well aware of how important it is for them to get three points.

"We have a game on Sunday against Lazio and need to recuperate, because these are the only players we've got," he said when asked if he could turn things around.

"You win and lose matches on details, not the big things, but the small ones. The team fought and chased Porto around man for man as long as they could, but then we ran out of fuel.

"It's like a cup final for us against Lazio, and then, hopefully, we can recover some players during the break for international duty."

#1749. Kaka speaks for the first time since San Siro tears: “Milan is second home to me”

One of the most striking images from AC Milan’s derby win over Inter on Saturday was Ricardo Kaka’s tears as he was welcomed on the field.

Saturday night was the night of Milan’s resounding derby victory – their fourth in a row against Inter – but it was also the night of Kakà’s return to San Siro. He was presented with a trophy before kick-off to mark his induction into the Rossoneri Hall of Fame.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It was a moment filled with emotion for all the fans present who chanted his name, but above all it was a moving moment for Kakà himself, who couldn’t hold back the tears as a montage video played on the screen.

Now, the Brazilian has spoken for the first time since that memorable evening as the NSS Sports Instagram page published a short interview with him.

“Milan is a second home to me: that’s the word that comes to mind when I think of this city. I’ve been truly fortunate to have so many great champions at my side, at AC Milan, in the national team, in Madrid: I’ve played with some truly brilliant players.

“The most elegant? Zidane, even though I didn’t play with him, but against him. The best moments associated with San Siro are definitely the victories, the Champions League celebrations in 2007, so many matches like the one against Manchester United or the one against Roma when we won the Scudetto.

“But there were also many moments, every time I entered San Siro and heard the chant ‘Siam venuti fin qua, siam venuti fin qua…’, I got goosebumps.”

#1748. Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Home » Home 2 » Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Table-toppers Arsenal travel to Anfield tonight with their first Premier League trophy since the ‘invincibles’ season of 2004 in sight. The Gunners top the table and with stuttering performances from Manchester City and a Leicester City whose fairytale run seems at an end, and are in pole position to finish the current campaign as champions.

While Jurgen Klopp’s men are still finding their way inconsistently since his appointment, Arsenal are in top form with five victories out of their last six matches. In comparison, Liverpool have been as easy to predict as a magic 8 ball, with impressive wins over Leicester City and Manchester City, but accompanied with horrific losses against Watford and West Ham. With fourth place still within grasp and with an impressive record against the table topping teams this season, Liverpool would look to give their long suffering fans some cheer with which to greet this New Year.

The Reds desperately need a victory to steady the ship as their erratic and wayward form sees them enter 2016 still outside the top 4 and distant from any title challenge.

With a host of injuries to his main XI, Jurgen Klopp could be forgiven for dipping into the transfer market so early. The Reds have captured QPR right-back Steven Caulker along with Marko Grujic in the January transfer window.

With Grujic returning to his former club Red Star Belgrade on loan, Steven Caulker is likely to be given a run out as a substitute with the current spate of Liverpool injuries.

Ings, Sturridge, Lovren, Coutinho, Origi and Flanagan are amongst the Liverpool afflicted and will take no part in the match ahead. With Lovren out, Kolo Toure and Mamadou Sakho look likely to be Klopp’s first choice central defending partnership.

Alberto Moreno and Nathaniel Clyne should start as full-backs for the Liverpool side and will be crucial in any attempt to penetrate the Gunner’s defences. Emre Can and Lucas should marshal the midfield, while James Milner, Firmino and Adam Lallana look to give Petr Cech some concerns about his goal. Leading the line should be Christian Benteke, who’s lack of form doesn’t threaten this match as manager Klopp has few options in his position.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Mignolet; Clyne, Sakho, Toure, Moreno; Lucas, Can, Firmino, Lallana, Milner, Benteke.

Arsenal must show that they have the one quality required of all champions : Consistency. The task is hereby straightforward for Wenger’s men. Win, keep winning, regardless of your manner and the title is yours.

With half the season concluded, Arsene Wenger must be wishing that he received a Christmas gift from the Arsenal medical team. Injuries have decimated his midfield with Wilshire, Cazorla, Rosiscky, Coquelin and Sanchez out of the game.

There is some good news with Mesul Ozil having managed to partake in some leisure instead of participating in the FA cup victory over Sunderland. Keeping the nimble playmaker fit would be key to Arsenal aspirations, both in this match and for the remainder of the season.

With both Petr Mertersacker and Gabriel available, it would be interesting to see whom Arsene Wenger picks out for his starting XI. Koscielny, Bellerin and Monreal have nailed down their place in the defence and the inclusion of the slower Mertersacker or the inconsistent Gabriel may have a defining moment in the game.

With Arsenal’s midfield woes, it should fall to Flamini to screen the defence with Ramsey alongside him. Walcott, Ozil and Joel Campbell should be the main thrusts of Arsenal’s attacking play with Giroud as the elegant, decisive focus.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Cech; Bellerin, Gabriel, Koscielny, Monreal; Flamini, Ramsey, Ozil, Walcott, Campbell; Girourd.

With previous encounters between these teams resulting in high scoring draws, we favour a repeat of last year’s epic 2-2 result for the same fixture. Martin Skrtel’s 97th minute header in front of the Kop capped a memorable game which also had Fabio Borini sent off and we expect similar fireworks at Anfield tomorrow.
